Sports.title: Antonelli says doubters “added fuel to the fire” in his world championship pursuit | Formula 1
Sports.content:
New wold champion Andrea Kimi Antonelli says he was driven to disprove those who said he wasn’t ready for Formula 1.

Mercedes brought him up through the junior ranks quickly, skipping Formula 3 entirely and only spending a single season in Formula 2. Antonelli made his F1 debut last year, aged just 18, with Mercedes’ works F1 team rather than one of their customers.

Antonelli’s first season did not go entirely smoothly. He endured a nine-round spell during which he failed to score on seven occasions.

However he was competitive right from the start of his second season and quickly overtook team mate George Russell in the championship. Antonelli clinched the title yesterday with four rounds to spare.

He said that had been a satisfying response to those who suggested he wasn’t ready for F1.

“It’s always good to shut off some of the noise,” said Antonelli. “I think in many ways it does help to add fuel to the fire, the fact that some people said that I didn’t belong in Formula 1 or I wasn’t ready for it.

“At some points last year, it probably looked like that I wasn’t ready for it. But I think last year, being able to experience those moments made me much more ready ahead of this year. Experiencing really low and difficult situations, high-pressure moments, really helped me to face certain situations this year, and definitely they made me mature a lot as a driver and as a person.”

Antonelli clinched the title with nine grand prix wins, the most of any driver. But he admits there was room for improvement in his performance. “I’ve had moments where I could have done better, a lot better. It’s just a constant learning process.

“But I think last year, being able to race [with] Mercedes, obviously [going] straight under the spotlight, made me grow much, much faster than if I would have gone to a smaller team, for example.”

Sports.title: Social Media: Russell vows to rediscover his performance after “more bad days than good” in 2026 | Brief
Sports.content:
George Russell said he has found the 2026 season difficult to deal with as he missed out on his first chance to win the world championship.

He also offered his congratulations to team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli , who won the title yesterday.

“Now feels like a pretty suitable moment to speak from the heart,” said Russell in a post on social media. “This season started off exactly how I had hoped but it very quickly unravelled with tough luck and poor performances. It’s been the first proper season of my career where I’ve had more bad days than good.

“Has it been tough to deal with? Yes, very. Has it been tough to pick myself up week in, week out? Yes, very. Confusion at times? Often. All I know is that I’ve given it my all and 2026 was not meant to be my year.

“I want to sincerely congratulate Kimi on what has been an absolutely incredible season. You truly deserve the championship.

“Thank you to the team for producing the best car and power unit this season; it’s been inspiring to see everyone coming together over four tough years to bring Mercedes back to the top.

“Now, all I can promise is that for the rest of this season, and into the next one, I will be giving my absolute all to rediscover the performance I have been capable of producing for the majority of my career and fingers crossed a little bit of luck returns.

“Thanks for all the support.”

Sports.title: Leclerc has wrong mentality, says Hamilton: ‘It’s ‘do-or-die, either I win or none of us do” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari would have lost more wins this year if he had the same “kamikaze” mentality as team mate Charles Leclerc.

The seven-times world champion blamed his team mate for costing Ferrari victory in yesterday’s Mexican Grand Prix. Both he and Leclerc went off at turn four while fighting over the lead on lap one.

Hamilton said he’d noticed Leclerc’s battles with his predecessor Carlos Sainz Jnr cost Ferrari points in the past.

“Before I joined this team, when I was at Mercedes, I watched and witnessed the back and forth between Charles and Carlos several races, where they were battling so much that the person ahead just pulled away, and they had the pace to actually win,” he said. “But it is one thing when that’s happening in fourth and fifth, as opposed to first and second, and you lose the win. That’s significant.

“The guy [Leclerc] is 28 years old, so I don’t think it’s an age thing. I think it’s a mentality thing. It’s like, “Do-or-die. Either I win or none of us do,” and it shouldn’t be that. It should be us having, getting that one-two.”

Hamilton pointed out he did not compromise Leclerc’s race when he won at Silverstone earlier this year. “In Silverstone, I could have gone all kamikaze on him and taken him off and lost us the win, but instead the one-two was there.” They finished first and third but were holding the top two positions before Hamilton pitted when the Safety Car was deployed.

“For me, I’m happy for the team to have experienced that, but I’m hopeful we’ll work towards a better working place in the future.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

In remarks similar to those of Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur, Hamilton said the result did not do justice to the effort made by the team.

“I think the core thing to remember, which maybe comes with age, is that every decision you make in the car impacts all the people that work in the background for the whole team,” he said. “So, working as a team is a part of our job and a part of our contract.

“We have to work as a team, which we could have easily done today. So, it’s a shame to see us lose this, as we did. That will just continue unless action is taken, if a real deep, serious conversation is had. So, it shouldn’t happen [again] moving forward.

“Of course, I’ve had close battles with team mates in the past, and you can’t always get it right, but nine times out of ten we should be able to. So, I think we’ll take it offline and we’ll have some good conversations, hopefully. For sure, it won’t be easy, but it must be done.”

However Hamilton admitted he’d experienced tougher situations previously at other teams, such as at Mercedes, where he and team mate Nico Rosberg once took each other out at the start of a race.

“I’ve had way worse times at Mercedes. There were some really bad moments. I don’t really see there being huge differences. I think it was managed well at Mercedes, and I think Fred’s doing his best.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Fred came and spoke to me before the race, and I think he was nervous. Of course, he wants [his] two drivers to do well.”

He said he would have had to explain his actions had he attacked his team mate from behind the way Leclerc did.

“From my side, if I’m coming from behind and I’m taking all the risk and it ends up that we lose as a team, then I think I have some answering to do, because it impacts a lot of people. But the other way around, I’m in the lead, and it was just unnecessary.

“I think we could have easily had that one-two today, which would have been huge for the team and for everyone back at the factory who’s worked so hard to bring us these upgrades. I don’t really know what will be done because up until now nothing really has been done.”

Sports.title: Antonelli “lost two seconds because I was crying” at end of Mexican GP | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli admitted he was already crying before he took the chequered flag to win the world championship.

The Mercedes driver finished third in Mexico, clinching the title in his second season as a Formula 1 driver. The 20-year-old was so emotional he was struggling to see the track and he lost 1.8 seconds to the leaders on his final lap.

“I lost probably two seconds because I was already crying, basically,” Antonelli admitted. “I couldn’t see clearly ahead.

“I could see two Ferraris, somehow, with the tears. So it was very special.”

Antonelli became the youngest world champion in F1 history, just five years after moving from karts to cars. “A lot of memories went through my mind in that moment,” he said, “all the memories since karting all the way to here.

“It was a very special final lap, and definitely when I crossed the line, I let it all out because it was just achieving one of my biggest dreams. It was very special.”

The championship outcome was a foregone conclusion before the weekend began: Antonelli needed to score only two points to be certain of the title even if his closest rival won all the remaining rounds. Nonetheless he felt the weight of expectation during the weekend.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“I knew I was very close. However, I still needed to get the job done, and, of course, you still want to do a good race. You want to do a good performance, so that was the goal.

“But it hasn’t been the easiest weekend either. Physically, I haven’t been in the best shape, but also yesterday we had a bad qualifying execution, and emotions were a bit high overall.

“But I’m really happy that today we did a strong race and really happy that we managed to finish the job. And then now we’ve got a few races to go, and we’re just going to enjoy all the way and try to finish on a high.”

He made a careful start to the race, ceding a position to eventual winner Max Verstappen on the run to turn one. However he decided to risk more at the second standing start following a red flag period.

“At the start I was very cautious, and I gave a lot of room. So I was probably playing it very much on the safe side.

“But then I saw I had the pace, and especially that first stint, I knew we would be in the fight because the pace was very good on used tyres.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Then with the red flag, it kind of all went back to zero. And in that moment I was like, ‘You know what? I’m just going to take more risks.’

“I had the opportunity to gain a few places, and that move on Charles [Leclerc] was crucial to get on the podium. I tried until the end to stay close, and it was very fun, the last stint, because we were all, I think, the three of us within two seconds, and we were all pushing. It was just difficult, of course, to overtake, but it was high intensity, and it was fun.

“Then on the last lap I just backed off because I just couldn’t see the track. I was getting emotional, and I said, ‘I’m just going to back off because otherwise I crash here.’ So it was just good to bring it home.”

Sports.title: Spotlight: Antonelli says he’ll frame iconic photo with Hamilton and Verstappen | Brief
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli says the post-race photograph of him with two of his fellow world champions deserves a place on his wall.

Sports.title: Call this the ‘Maxico’ Grand Prix says Verstappen after sixth Mexican GP win | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen joked Formula 1 should rename Mexico’s round of the world championship after him following his sixth victory in the race.

The Red Bull driver has now scored more wins in Mexico City than he has at any other venue. He became the fourth driver to score more than five wins at the same venue and the first to do so at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez

“They should actually call it the ‘Maxico’ Grand Prix,” said Verstappen. “That would be great.”

His five previous wins at the track came between 2017 and 2023. Verstappen said he saw no obvious reason why he had been particularly successful at this venue.

“I honestly love being here,” he said. “I love the city, I love the environment, I love the fans, but I have no idea why.

“It just happens. Sometimes your car just comes alive and you’ve had good races and not a lot of bad luck sometimes as well. So it’s just always come together for me here and, of course, I happily take that.”

Verstappen said he was surprised to move into a strong position immediately after the start of the race, thanks partly to Ferrari drivers Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton going off at turn four.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“The first start already made my race a bit better, getting into turn one, and then, of course, the battle that I saw unfold in turn four put me in a quite nice spot.”

Leclerc received a five-second time penalty for his infringement and Verstappen jumped ahead of him when they pitted on the same lap.

“It was a bit tough, to be honest, I think Charles just pulled away. I could not really stay with him. I did not have the pace to follow him, but at the same time, I was still within that five-second window.

“So, then the team did a really good job to follow him in [to the pits]. It’s always very tough when you have a five-second penalty to actually make it exactly five seconds. So, I jumped him, and honestly, after that, it was quite tough.”

The race winner said he feared for his chances when the Safety Car was deployed following Valtteri Bottas’s crash. The race was stopped and restarted, and Verstappen maintained his lead ahead of Hamilton.

“Kimi [Antonelli] was flying, still, out there on the first set of tyres, and I just did not really have the grip for whatever reason. Charles was very close, but at the same time, it’s very hard to follow around here because everything overheats, and that probably helped me as well because I think at one point Charles had to back off just for cooling, and that was quite nice for me.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“But at the same time, when I saw the Safety Car come out just out of the last corner and I couldn’t box, I was like, ‘There’s no way this is happening now,’ because that was then probably game over for me.

“Then, of course, it ended up being a red flag, so then it reset everything. I was a bit worried because our starts this year have not been amazing, but luckily today, twice, they have actually been good, and that then made my way ’til the end.

“But it was not made easy. I mean, Lewis was in my gearbox, pushing hard. It was basically a qualifying lap ’til the end. Yeah, it was tough out there. It was a tough race to the end, just to not make any mistakes. But, of course, I’m happy to win today.”

Sports.title: “I’ll stay with number 12” – no number one in 2027 for new champion Antonelli | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli will not use the number one on his car, which is reserved for world champions, next year.

The Mercedes driver succeeded Lando Norris as the reigning world champion with his third-place finish in yesterday’s Mexican Grand Prix. But while Norris swapped his regular number four for the champion’s one, Antonelli will not do the same.

“I’ll stay with number 12 because, obviously, it’s a very special number for me,” he said. “But also it’s a way for me to stay grounded, to stay humble.

“I feel like by keeping number 12 it allows me to have a new point where to start and build on everything again and try to improve.”

Antonelli admitted there is an element of superstition in his preference to stick with his current number.

“Also, to be honest, I’m very superstitious, and number one has never been a good number for me. Whenever I [used] it, it went extremely badly. So that’s one more reason to stay with number 12.”

Prior to racing in F1, Antonelli used number 12 when he won the European and Middle East Formula Regional championship titles in 2023, and the Italian Formula 4 title the year before.

He is the first driver to win the world championship using number 12 since Ayrton Senna in 1988. Both drivers also scored their first grand prix victories with number 12: Antonelli this year, Senna in 1985.

Antonelli is planning a tribute to the Brazilian three-times world champion at this weekend’s Brazilian Grand Prix.

“I will have a special helmet for Brazil, for Ayrton,” he said. “Also because it’s going to be 35 years since he won [while stuck] in sixth gear in his home race.

“I think it’s one of my best helmets that I’ve made, hopefully you guys, everyone, will like it.”

Sports.title: Mannix Says Munguía and Melikuziev Have Reached Terms
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguía and Bektemir Melikuziev have reportedly come to terms for a WBA super middleweight title fight. Munguía named his mandatory challenger after beating Nikita Zon by unanimous decision Saturday in Riyadh, but Sergio Mora still doubts he’ll take the fight.

“I think Munguía is going to stay away from him,” Mora said during his discussion with Chris Mannix. “Well, I think he’s going to fight him. I don’t think he’s going to give up his belt, and everything I’ve been told [is] that they’ve come to terms on the fight,” Mannix said on his channel. He gave no date for the defense.

Mora had already picked Melikuziev before the Zon fight. He sees a natural 168-pounder who uses his southpaw angles better than Zon and hits harder. Mannix brought up Melikuziev’s close fight with Darius Fulghum, when he needed a knockdown in the 12th. That’s a fair reason to hesitate over picking Bektemir, but Munguía gave him something specific to work on in Riyadh.

When Zon hurt Munguía in the sixth, the champion bent forward and pulled his gloves up around his ears. Zon kept hooking at the sides of the guard. Mora thought a straight punch or an uppercut could have brought Munguía’s head up and given referee Tony Weeks a reason to stop it. Both men backed Weeks for letting it continue. Munguía came back to hurt Zon in the same round.

What would worry me about Bektemir is what happens before Munguía gets to the ropes. Munguía likes to walk a man down and get close enough to work with both hands.

Every step in gives a southpaw with good feet a chance to move outside his lead foot and send a left hand through the middle. Munguía can come back from one bad minute, as he showed against Zon. Against Melikuziev, he may have to solve that left hand every time he tries to get his own offense going.

Sports.title: Could Rocky Marciano Take Away Larry Holmes’s Jab?
Sports.content:
Larry Holmes was one win away from matching Rocky Marciano’s 49–0 record when Michael Spinks took his heavyweight title in September 1985. After losing a close unanimous decision, Holmes had something to say about the champion whose record he’d come up short of tying. “Marciano couldn’t wear my jockstrap,” he said.

I thought Spinks earned that decision by taking the final round, and I gave Holmes the rematch, which Spinks won by split decision. But the crack about Marciano got me thinking about something Holmes did in the ring. He sometimes left his left arm extended between jabs to keep a shorter man at a distance. Most fighters would try to get around it. I think Marciano would have started punching it.

Rocky could come up from his crouch with a short uppercut into the elbow or dig a hook into the upper arm when Holmes covered up. He’d take some clean jabs getting close enough to do it. But if those punches made Holmes think twice about leaving the arm out, Marciano would have more room to step in. A punch that looked wasted in the fourth could buy him a shot at the ribs in the tenth.

Holmes could make that a slow and painful trade for Marciano. A quick jab and half a step back would leave Rocky reaching for an arm that was already gone. If Marciano tried to cover the extra ground by ducking in from too far away, Holmes could catch him with the right uppercut. Rocky might do good work once he got his head against Holmes’s chest and still spend most of the round trying to get there.

The danger for Holmes would come when he started pulling straight back with his hands down. Marciano was behind against Jersey Joe Walcott before knocking him out in the 13th to win the title. In the Ezzard Charles rematch, he scored an eighth-round stoppage with his nose badly split. Holmes could be well ahead after ten rounds and still have to watch where his left hand came back after every jab. If it dropped to his waist, Marciano could throw his right over it without having to get all the way inside.

I’d take Holmes by decision over 15 rounds. I can see Marciano hurting him late, especially if the work on the arm took some snap off the jab. But Holmes could win the first two minutes of a round from a distance and make Rocky spend most of the last minute closing it. I’d give Holmes more of those rounds than I’d give Marciano the kind where he got close early and kept him there.

Sports.title: Chris Billam-Smith Welcomes Oleksandr Usyk Fight
Sports.content:
Chris Billam-Smith would welcome a fight with Oleksandr Usyk at cruiserweight, but it’s hard to see why Usyk would take it.

Billam-Smith faces Cheavon Clarke this Saturday in a fight that has generated little buzz. Even a strong win would leave him a long way from getting Usyk’s attention.

“Anyone would love to have that opportunity,” Billam-Smith said on talkSPORT when asked if he’d like to fight Usyk. He praised Usyk for what he accomplished in his first run at cruiserweight, including beating opponents in their own backyards. He also floated the possibility of Usyk fighting David Benavidez in May.

Benavidez is precisely why the Billam-Smith fight is so hard to picture. If Usyk can get Benavidez, there’s little reason to take a detour through Billam-Smith first. If he beats Benavidez, there’s even less reason to stick around for a fight that would be a much tougher sell.

Saudi backing could put a big purse on the table, but someone would have to be willing to take a hefty loss on the show. A former world champion settling an old score at the Copper Box is a decent Saturday main event. It would take a lot more than a win over Clarke to make Billam-Smith the opponent people want to see for one of Usyk’s last fights.

Billam-Smith tossing his name into the mix sounds like wishful thinking, because from a business standpoint, the numbers simply do not work. At cruiserweight, the appetite begins and ends with marquee matchups. Benavidez brings immense Mexican American star power and guaranteed crossover viewers. Jai Opetaia is viewed as the true elite at 200 pounds, a genuine pound-for-pound talent who can test Usyk athletically.

Those fights carry legitimate commercial intrigue and legacy value. Billam-Smith, by contrast, is a domestic UK ticket seller whose profile drops off steeply once you leave Britain. Expecting Saudi organizers to cut a massive check for an unheralded opponent when far bigger fights exist makes zero sense.

The winner of Tyson Fury versus Anthony Joshua remains a gigantic stadium draw for Usyk regardless of previous records. Fans would gladly line up for an undisputed rubber match or a fresh chapter with Daniel Dubois before Usyk hangs up the gloves.

Sports.title: Yoenli Hernandez Ordered To Fight Michael Zerafa For Vacant WBO Belt
Sports.content:
Yoenli Hernández could have to go through a second purse bid just to get his first WBO title fight. The WBO has authorized negotiations between Hernández and Michael Zerafa for its vacant middleweight belt after stripping Denzel Bentley, whose mandatory defense against Hernández had already gone to bid.

Zerafa, ranked fourth by the WBO, moves ahead of two contenders who are unavailable. No. 2 Vito Mielnicki Jr. is unavailable, and No. 3 Tim Tszyu is under contract to face Erislandy Lara. WBO president Gustavo Olivieri said formal notice would follow. The fighters’ teams will have 20 days from the issuance of that order to reach a deal.

Hernández Has Already Been Through One Purse Bid

“The parties shall have 20 days from the issuance of the formal negotiation order to reach terms, pursuant to WBO Regulations or purse bid proceedings,” Olivieri said on X.

Warriors Boxing was the only bidder for Bentley’s mandatory defense and secured the promotional rights with a $200,000 offer on September 29. Bentley stood to receive $150,000, with the remaining $50,000 going to Hernández. Bentley had asked to fight Shane Mosley Jr. first and defend against Hernández afterward, but the WBO denied his appeal on October 22. He kept the Mosley fight, scheduled for November 7 in London as his Zuffa Boxing debut, and the WBO stripped him.

That first bid shows why the next 20 days matter. Hernández’s promoter did what the WBO process required and put up the money to stage the defense. Bentley still had a fight he preferred to take, and Hernández came out of the process with the same No. 1 ranking he had going in. A deal with Zerafa would spare him another round of bidding and give both camps a chance to settle where the fight takes place and what they’ll be paid.

Hernández (11-0, 9 KOs) brings the bigger punch, but his last fight gave Zerafa something to study. Francisco Verón took him the distance in August and held him to a majority decision. For all the talk about why Bentley took the Mosley fight, that result matters more to Zerafa. There are rounds to win against Hernández if Zerafa can keep him from setting his feet and make him work to close the distance.

The opening for Zerafa came from the two names above him being unavailable. What he can do with it is another matter. Hernández has the power to make this a short night if Zerafa stands in front of him, but the Cuban still has to show he can take charge when an opponent makes him work deep into a fight. That’s what makes the pairing worth seeing once the teams get it signed.

Sports.title: Can Anyone Outside Of  Terence Crawford Defeat Canelo At 168?
Sports.content:
On Halloween night, Canelo Alvarez defeated Christian Mbilli to become a three-time super-middleweight world champion, and now the question is: outside of Terence Crawford, can any other boxer defeat Canelo at 168?

When Christian Mbilli entered the ring to face Canelo Alvarez, a reasonable number of boxing pundits thought Mbilli was going to pull off the upset. Alvarez has a history of stamina issues, and many assumed Mbilli could take advantage.

The idea was for Mbilli to overwhelm Canelo with his high-volume punching, wear him down, take over in the later rounds, and win a close decision. Unfortunately for Mbilli, the bout didn’t go that way.

Canelo Alvarez was able to dictate the range and the pace of the fight. Canelo’s defense was sharp, his stamina was good, and on offense he dominated the action with skillful counterpunching and pinpoint accuracy.

Mbilli fought the wrong type of fight, as most of the bout took place at mid-range as opposed to close quarters. Mbilli gave Canelo too much respect, and on multiple occasions he looked confused.

Christian Mbilli was severely outclassed, and because of that, the fight looked like a glorified sparring session. As a result of the bout, Canelo Alvarez (64-3-2, 39 KOs) is the new WBC super-middleweight world champion.

The sport of boxing is based on levels, and on the night of October 31st, Canelo Alvarez proved he was levels above Christian Mbilli. Now fight fans are wondering: are any of the current top super-middleweights close to being on Canelo’s level?

Terence “Bud” Crawford defeated Canelo Alvarez with his skill set and his ring IQ. None of the top super-middleweights have a skill set compatible with Crawford’s, and none of them come close to Crawford when it comes to ring intelligence.

With that being said, one would ask, outside of a rematch with Crawford, what would be the ideal fight for Canelo at 168? If Terence Crawford can’t be convinced to come out of retirement, then Hamzah Sheeraz is probably the best candidate.

The former WBO world champion Hamzah Sheeraz is a 6-foot-3-inch super-middleweight who is skilled, and he can effectively fight from long range. On Halloween night, Sheeraz was ringside analyzing the fight.

Back in July 2025, Hamzah Sheeraz looked sharp as he stopped Edgar Berlanga in the 5th round. A year later, Sheeraz had a lackluster performance, as he scored a majority decision victory over Simon Zachenhuber.

Now Hamzah Sheeraz (24-0-1, 19 KOs) appears to be the frontrunner in regards to facing Canelo in 2027. If Sheeraz doesn’t get the match, then Canelo may choose to fight one of the other champions at 168.

Sports.title: Lester Martinez Targets Canelo Alvarez With BoMac Behind Him
Sports.content:
Lester Martinez would give Canelo Alvarez a dangerous first defense of his reclaimed WBC super middleweight title. The aggressive Guatemalan can punch and has Brian “BoMac” McIntyre in his corner, giving him access to the trainer who helped Terence Crawford beat Canelo.

“My dream now is to fight Canelo because he’s the champion,” Martinez said to Izquierdazo Boxeo in a quote shared by The Ring. His WBC interim title gives that ambition substance, although it does not establish that Canelo has been ordered to face him next.

The McIntyre connection makes this more interesting than another contender requesting a payday. BoMac knows what went into preparing Crawford for Canelo and could bring that knowledge into Martinez’s camp. The WBC lists McIntyre as Martinez’s trainer. wbcboxing.com

Crawford could also offer firsthand advice about Canelo’s timing, counterpunching and habits under pressure. His involvement in a potential camp has not been announced, but Martinez would have an obvious reason to seek his stablemate’s input.

Mbilli took too long to alter his approach when Canelo’s jab and head movement disrupted his pressure last weekend. He continued following Canelo without consistently changing how he attacked. Martinez would likely arrive expecting those tactics, with McIntyre preparing ways to get past the jab and vary his attack.

That would not make Lester immune to Canelo’s counters. It could, however, reduce the rounds spent trying to work out what to do next. BoMac could prepare alternatives before the opening bell and help Martinez adjust between rounds when Canelo starts frustrating him.

Martinez would still need to win with his own tools. He cannot copy Crawford’s performance. His route would involve sustained pressure, body punching and enough variation to prevent Canelo from anticipating each attack.

His 2025 draw with Mbilli gives him a relevant result against the man Canelo just defeated. Beating Canelo is another matter, but an aggressive puncher arriving with informed preparation would be a serious undertaking for the 36-year-old champion.

Sports.title: Deontay Wilder’s Power Puts Jai Opetaia’s Chin On Trial
Sports.content:
Deontay Wilder has plenty of reasons to believe he can catch Jai Opetaia. The unbeaten cruiserweight champion handles pressure well, but flush right hands consistently cause trouble. That crack in the armor turns their planned December 11 meeting into an explosive collision.

Trainer Stephen Edwards spotted the opening on the proposed Fury vs Joshua card in Cardiff. While he figures Opetaia enters as the favorite, he doubts the Australian stays out of danger for twelve full rounds.

I think Deontay Wilder has a chance vs Jai Opetaia. Opetaia will most likely be the favorite but he’s not refined or smooth defensively. If he doesn’t clip Deontay, he’s in serious danger throughout. Risky fight but I respect it. Especially for this era,” said Edwards on X.

The real test is Opetaia’s chin. Crisp southpaw boxing gives him an edge in ring generalship, yet recent cruiserweight defenses have shown concerning moments whenever opponents land cleanly.

Huseyin Cinkara rattled him during the second round of their clash in late 2025. Opetaia rallied to score an eighth round knockout, though the early scare arrived against an opponent everyone expected him to run through.

Noel Mikaelian produced an identical scare in September. A crisp right hook connected in round seven, forcing Opetaia to clinch immediately. He rallied once more, stopping Mikaelian in the ninth, yet the warning sirens rang out loud.

Opetaia is taking a risk here because a knockout loss wrecks the financial engine behind a David Benavidez clash. Benavidez wants Opetaia for legacy, unified belts, and a high-profile scalp. If Opetaia comes off a brutal stoppage, Benavidez gains almost nothing from beating him. The narrative shifts from “daring to be great against the division monster” to “picking up the pieces of damaged goods.”

Wilder must still land the equalizer. If Opetaia’s speed freezes the former heavyweight champion, Wilder might spend the night waiting for an opening that never arrives. His right hand remains the great equalizer, but banking on it to bail him out against Opetaia ignores what happened to his punch resistance and his trigger.

Zhilei Zhang needed only one clean counter right hand to completely turn Wilder around and leave him staring at the rafters.

Opetaia does not need to hit as hard as Zhang. He punches with devastating leverage from the southpaw stance, throws tight combinations rather than looping singles, and refuses to let opponents recover once they’re hurt.

When Cinkara and Mikaelian found Opetaia’s chin, Opetaia still walked through the fire to stop both men. Wilder, by contrast, has shown zero ability to absorb heavy contact and rally back since 2020.

Sports.title: Revitalization in Riyadh
Sports.content:
Saturday afternoon saw Saul “Canelo” Alvarez (64-3-2, 39 KOs) defeat Christian Mbilli (29-1-1, 24 KOs) by unanimous decision over 12 rounds. For all the talk of Canelo being washed after his dismantling at the hands of Terence “Bud” Crawford last year, Canelo looked quick, efficient, and energized on both offense and defense from beginning to end.

Some major differences in his performance included a low lead hand stance as his primary, with the high guard as a secondary; a return to the head movement that was once touted as among the best in boxing; and the most consistent and effective jab we’ve seen from him in close to a decade. He also threw a hell of a lot of feints and changed up the velocity of his punches rather than throwing everything hard as he has tended to do. This not only helped him conserve energy, but it also deterred Mbilli’s aggressiveness. In a fight that many expected to be a war, Canelo focused on pure boxing and high-level defense to slow the action down and prevent Mbilli from launching an all-out attack in the pocket.

In the early rounds, Canelo played a little rope-a-dope, laying against the ropes while slipping, ducking, and blocking the younger fighter’s shots. When the action made its way back to the center of the ring, Canelo popped Mbilli with sharp, well-timed jabs at mid-range. After four rounds, Mbilli had slowed enough for Canelo to begin finding big, clean counters in exchanges. Six rounds in, Canelo started circling more rather than going to the ropes. At times, he would touch the ropes with his back to bait Mbilli in, and then flurry with rapid combinations as Mbilli stepped in thinking Canelo was going back on defense.

From the seventh round on, it was a basic boxing clinic, with Canelo showing that he can still box his ass off when he isn’t in love with his power. The eleventh and twelfth rounds were competitive as Mbilli tried to finish strong, yet Canelo consistently landed the bigger, cleaner shots, even wobbling Mbilli toward the close of round 12.

Mbilli simply was never able to mount a consistent attack because Canelo had an answer for everything he attempted. Against Terence Crawford, Canelo simply sought to overpower what he perceived as a naturally smaller man, but Crawford was able to blunt everything coming from Canelo with sophisticated defense and control at midrange. When Canelo went back to the drawing board with his team, he must have been kicking himself for never attempting to establish the jab, failing to use his head movement, and allowing Crawford to maintain foot control all night.

When Mayweather dominated Canelo over 12 rounds with superior defense and intelligent punch selection, the takeaway was that brute force isn’t enough to topple the fighters at the top. Somewhere during his 168 lb undisputed run, he lost sight of that and locked into a seek-and-destroy mindset. It seems like the Crawford loss may have initiated a similar reboot, which could carry Canelo into a final run at undisputed before retirement.

One point of concern Saturday night took place outside of the ring, with the commentary team missing as much as Christian Mbilli was. Notably, Todd Grisham seemed intent on dragging Canelo. At one point, he implied that Canelo got the benefit of the doubt against Daniel Jacobs, which was actually a clear and decisive win for Canelo. He also mentioned a fight between Canelo and Derevyanchenko, which does not exist. In the opening rounds, when Mbilli would miss six or seven punch combinations, the commentary team would praise the guy who missed rather than the guy who made him miss.

In round eight, after multiple fouls, when Mbilli drove a palm into the back of Canelo’s head, the referee separated the two and walked Mbilli to the center of the ring. He clearly had Mbilli’s glove in hand, preparing to take a point, when Canelo tapped his shoulder to complain about the fouls as fighters often do. When the referee proceeded to dock the point, Grisham erupted into an accusation that Canelo had forced the referee to penalize Mbilli. The ref was clearly already preparing to take the point, but furthermore, Canelo has zero power to force a referee’s hand. What Canelo apparently stated was that if he was fouled again, he would kick his opponent. He didn’t use his name or influence to sway any decision-making; he simply made a statement out of anger.

Of course, many viewers who aren’t familiar with the intricacies of the sport rely on the commentary team to provide an accurate analysis of the fight. Much of the post-fight narrative following Saturday’s bout has been centered around the perception that Canelo had the referee in his pocket and that the fight was a robbery, simply because the commentators seemed to favor ineffective aggression over defensive prowess.

Outside of whatever bias he has against Alvarez, there wasn’t much technical analysis from Grisham. Sergio Mora, though he has experience as a fighter and sometimes points out strategies or techniques, is often unable to articulate what he sees clearly. Grisham frequently views fights as a casual fan might: “Throw punches = good. Not throw punches = bad. Move forward = good. Block punches = getting hit.” DAZN would do well to bring on an individual who truly understands the nuances of the sport and can convey them effectively to the common fan.

One thing that hasn’t been prevalent in the aftermath of the fight is anyone accusing Canelo of “running,” even though he more or less did to Mbilli what Crawford did to him. People who accuse boxers of running because they do not sit and slug it out at close range are generally uninformed or unwilling to give credit to certain styles of fighters like Crawford, Foster, or Mayweather. Canelo rarely sat still for exchanges, yet he is (rightfully) being praised for his high defensive IQ. Now, what could that double standard possibly be about?

So, what impressions did Saturday’s main event leave on us?

First, Canelo didn’t learn any new tricks; he simply brushed the dust off his old tool bag and returned to the basics. The jab was tweaked, but overall, the head movement, feints, and punch variety are elements fans have been asking him to bring back for years.

Secondly, DAZN needs to step up its commentary game. The broadcast should accommodate the casual viewer while remaining educated and informed enough for die-hard boxing fans. You simply cannot skimp on commentator quality at this level of production.

Lastly, Canelo’s future. Alvarez remains a polarizing figure. But love him or hate him, it is hard to deny that he has been boxing’s biggest star since Mayweather retired. What might his plans be moving forward, and how will the boxing world react? Given the promotional tagline of “Return of the King,” it seems reasonable to assume he will once again seek to become the undisputed champion of the 168 lb division before retiring. Ideally, he would collect all the belts and gain one more signature victory, though that is a steep path for a 36-year-old.

Wherever the future leads him, he has carried the sport at several key points in his career. He is a reminder that greatness and perfection are not one and the same, and are often at odds. Steadfast determination and a true, honest love for boxing have defined Canelo’s persona inside and outside the ring. Despite falling short against generational greats, he remains an example of how passionate dedication to a dream can endure long after achieving everything you set out for.

Ghana News.title: Parliament resumes with 2027 Budget, Anti-Gay Bill and Appropriation Bill in focus
Ghana News.content:
Parliament is set to reconvene on Tuesday, November 3, for the Third Meeting of the Second Session of the Ninth Parliament of the Fourth Republic, with the 2027 national budget and pending legislative proposals expected to feature prominently.

The meeting comes at a critical time as the House prepares to consider the government's fiscal programme for the 2027 financial year, alongside other matters relating to national governance and policy direction.

A key item on the parliamentary calendar will be the presentation of the 2027 Budget Statement and Economic Policy by Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson on November 12.

The budget is expected to set out the government's economic agenda for the coming year, including projected revenue, planned expenditure, fiscal targets and policy measures.

It will also indicate the government's approach to addressing prevailing economic difficulties, promoting economic growth, managing public debt and improving the welfare of citizens.

After the presentation, MPs will begin a detailed assessment of the proposed fiscal plan, with parliamentary committees reviewing budgetary allocations to ministries, departments and agencies under their respective oversight.

The exercise will allow lawmakers to evaluate the government's expenditure priorities, interrogate proposed allocations and submit recommendations before the House considers the Appropriation Bill.

The bill, once passed, will authorise the withdrawal of funds from the Consolidated Fund to meet approved government expenditure during the 2027 financial year.

Anti-Gay Bill

Beyond the budget, the Human Sexual Rights and Family Values Bill, popularly referred to as the Anti-Gay Bill, is also expected to attract attention during the meeting.

The proposed legislation has generated considerable debate locally and internationally, drawing reactions from politicians, religious institutions, civil society organisations and human rights advocates.

A possible return of the bill to the parliamentary agenda could revive discussions on sexual orientation, Ghanaian cultural and family values, human rights and the constitutional implications of the proposed law.

Supporters of the legislation maintain that it is intended to safeguard Ghana's cultural identity and traditional family values. However, opponents have questioned its compatibility with human rights protections and raised concerns about its possible legal implications.

The handling of the bill is therefore likely to attract considerable public attention as Parliament resumes its legislative business.

Ghana News.title: Dutch prosecutors offer €2m reward for arrest of fugitive linked to Ghana drug probe
Ghana News.content:
Leijdekkers, 35, is popularly known in the Netherlands as ‘Bolle Jos’, which translates as ‘Chubby Jos’. Dutch police say he is also known by the alias Omar Sherrif in Sierra Leone.

Dutch prosecutors have announced a €2 million reward for information that leads to the arrest of Jos Leijdekkers, a convicted cocaine trafficker considered one of Europe’s most wanted fugitives, whose alleged activities have come under investigation in Ghana.

In a statement issued on Monday, November 2, 2026, the prosecutors said the reward would be given to anyone whose information provides a decisive lead resulting in Leijdekkers’ arrest.

The bounty, worth approximately $2.2 million, is the largest ever offered by Dutch authorities.

The announcement comes amid investigations by Ghana’s Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) into three individuals suspected of representing and facilitating the fugitive’s alleged drug-trafficking operations in Ghana.

The suspects were arrested following the seizure of a significant cocaine consignment by French customs officials. The shipment is believed to be connected to a wider international drug-trafficking network.

NACOC has confirmed that the three individuals remain in its custody and are assisting with investigations into their alleged involvement.

The Commission says the arrests form part of broader efforts to dismantle international drug-trafficking networks operating within Ghana or using the country as a transit route.

Investigators are expected to establish the nature of the suspects’ relationship with Leijdekkers, their activities in Ghana and their possible connections to the wider criminal network.

The outcome of the investigation could shed light on whether Ghana served as a transit hub, operational base or coordination point for activities allegedly associated with the fugitive.

Who is Jos Leijdekkers?

Leijdekkers, 35, is popularly known in the Netherlands as ‘Bolle Jos’, which translates as ‘Chubby Jos’. Dutch police say he is also known by the alias Omar Sherrif in Sierra Leone.

He is regarded by Dutch prosecutors as a major figure in international cocaine trafficking and is suspected of accumulating tens of millions of euros through the illegal trade.

Last year, a Dutch court sentenced him in absentia to 24 years in prison for his role in smuggling more than seven tonnes of cocaine.

He is also facing several other ongoing criminal investigations in the Netherlands.

In Belgium, a court handed him a separate 79-year prison sentence.

Dutch authorities additionally suspect him of money laundering and involvement in serious acts of violence.

Ghana News.title: Ebola: Ghana to Monitor travellers from affected countries for 21 days
Ghana News.content:
Travellers arriving in Ghana from countries experiencing Ebola transmission will be placed under health monitoring for up to 21 days as the government steps up precautionary measures to prevent the disease from entering and spreading within the country.

The Ministry of Health, through the Ghana Health Service (GHS), has announced enhanced public health interventions at the country's international airports, requiring all arriving passengers to undergo health screening and provide information about their recent travel history and possible exposure to the virus.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, and signed by the Minister for Health, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, the Ministry said the monitoring requirement formed part of measures to minimise the risk of Ebola being imported into Ghana through international travel.

"Passengers arriving from countries with ongoing transmission will be monitored for up to 21 days. The Ghana Health Service will contact them for follow-up, and they must keep reachable contact details and report any symptoms immediately to the designated contact," the statement said.

The Ministry assured the public, however, that Ghana had not recorded any confirmed case of Ebola Disease, describing the interventions as precautionary measures that would be reviewed as the outbreak situation evolves.

"To date, Ghana has not recorded a confirmed case of Ebola Disease. These measures are precautionary and will be reviewed as the situation evolves," it added.

All passengers to undergo airport screening

Under the new arrangements, every passenger arriving in Ghana will be screened by Port Health officers at the country's international airports.

The screening will involve non-contact temperature checks, reviews of completed Health Declaration Forms and assessments of passengers' travel histories.

Port Health officers may also ask additional questions about symptoms and possible exposure to the virus where necessary.

Passengers who exhibit symptoms suggestive of Ebola, have recently travelled from or through affected countries, or may have been exposed to a suspected or confirmed case will be referred for immediate secondary assessment.

Such passengers will be taken to designated areas for temporary isolation and evaluation before being referred to a health facility where necessary.

Travellers required to declare exposure before arrival

The Ministry has directed all passengers to complete a Health Declaration Form before travelling to Ghana and truthfully disclose any visits to or transit through Ebola-affected countries within the preceding 21 days.

They must also declare close contact with suspected or confirmed Ebola patients, visits to health facilities managing Ebola cases, participation in funeral or burial rites involving suspected cases, and contact with the blood, bodily fluids or contaminated materials of an ill person.

Travellers experiencing symptoms such as fever, severe weakness, headache, vomiting, diarrhoea, unexplained bleeding or bruising have been advised to postpone their journeys and seek immediate medical attention.

"Travellers with fever, severe weakness, headache, vomiting, diarrhoea, or unexplained bleeding or bruising should postpone travel and seek medical attention immediately," the Ministry cautioned.

Hotels and conference centres to report guests

The precautionary measures also extend to hotels, conference venues and similar hospitality establishments hosting visitors from countries affected by the outbreak.

Under the directive, these establishments must report guests arriving from affected countries to the nearest district health directorate of the Ghana Health Service.

They are also required to maintain records and contact details of all individuals who access their facilities while such guests are being hosted.

The requirement is expected to strengthen public health surveillance and assist health authorities in identifying and following up on individuals who may have come into contact with travellers considered to be at risk.

False declarations could attract legal consequences

The Ministry has urged all arriving passengers to cooperate fully with Port Health officers, provide truthful health and travel information, comply with screening instructions and practise frequent hand hygiene.

Passengers are also expected to report immediately if they develop symptoms during their journey or while at the airport.

It warned that anyone who deliberately provides false information, conceals symptoms or refuses to comply with screening requirements would be subject to public health measures under Ghanaian law.

"Any passenger who knowingly gives false information, conceals symptoms or refuses to comply with screening will be subject to public health measures under Ghanaian law," the statement warned.

Measures follow Africa CDC meeting

Ghana's latest interventions are consistent with commitments made at a recent ministerial meeting of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) on the Ebola outbreak.

The meeting brought together representatives of all 55 African member states, including more than 40 ministers, to discuss coordinated preparedness and response measures.

Participating countries agreed to implement the preparedness actions discussed, strengthen surveillance at national borders and cross-border points, and keep borders open while investing in measures to prevent transmission.

The Ministry said the measures reflected Ghana's commitment to strengthening disease surveillance and preparedness while maintaining international travel and cross-border movement.

Public urged to rely on official information

Meanwhile, the Ministry has urged the public to rely on official information from the Ministry of Health and the Ghana Health Service for updates on the outbreak and the country's response.

It cautioned against spreading rumours and unverified information that could create unnecessary fear and confusion.

Members of the public with health concerns have been advised to contact the nearest Port Health officer at the airport or visit their nearest health facility.

Although Ghana has not recorded a confirmed case of Ebola Disease, the government says the precautionary measures are necessary to strengthen preparedness, improve early detection and reduce the risk of the virus being introduced into the country.

It also directed passengers to report immediately if they develop symptoms during their flights or upon arrival at the airport.

Warning against non-compliance, the Ministry said any passenger who knowingly provides false information, conceals symptoms, or refuses to comply with screening requirements would face public health measures under Ghanaian law.

The public has meanwhile been advised to rely on official information from the Ministry of Health and the Ghana Health Service and avoid spreading rumours.

Anyone with health concerns has been encouraged to contact the nearest Port Health officer at the airport or visit the nearest health facility.

Ghana News.title: Dignity, Faith and the Poverty of Envy
Ghana News.content:
Kwame Sowu, the writer

By Kwame Sowu

I have known Dr Mensa Otabil from afar since the 1990s, when my sister Annie worked in his office. I am not a member of his church, but my considered observation over the years is that his dignity is in a class of its own.

His intelligent, disciplined and refreshingly minimalist approach to Christianity has transformed lives, restored hope and given countless people a reason to believe again. One cannot underestimate the number of souls that might otherwise have been lost.

As a Christian, I have seen far too many spiritual entrepreneurs whose ministries are built on fear, fabricated prophecies, hallucinations, superstition and the commercialisation of people's desperation. Dr Otabil, in my honest assessment, stands apart. A modest man, preaching the Word, encouraging personal responsibility, faith and prosperity without unnecessary theatrics.

Anyone, including the bleached gentleman taking aim at him, who mistakes another man's success for an offence should take a step back. Envy is not discernment, noise is not wisdom, and attacking another man's dignity does not elevate yours.

Forgiveness is Christian. But so is the obligation to seek knowledge, exercise restraint and, where necessary, seek counselling. Some battles are best abandoned before they expose the poverty of the person fighting them.

Ghana News.title: Tenerife striker De Miguel dies after on-field collision with Equatoguinean goalkeeper
Ghana News.content:
Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel has died after the 30-year-old suffered a serious injury during a Spanish second-division match.

The forward suffered head and chest injuries during a match against Andorra on Monday, in a heavy collision with goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who was sent off for his challenge.

De Miguel's condition was described as 'stable but serious' on Monday but his health deteriorated on Tuesday morning, with the Spaniard passing away at 07:00 GMT (08:00 local time).

"Heartbroken, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe this is true, CD Tenerife announces the tragic death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," a club statement said.

"There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can lessen this overwhelming sadness. We stand with his grieving family, with his loved ones, with all of Tenerife who mourn this cruel loss today.

"The family of Jesus de Miguel is grateful for each and every expression of support received, and also requests, from the bottom of their hearts, the utmost respect for their privacy during these terrible times."

Andorra, who are co-owned by former Barcelona defender Gerard Pique, said: "With broken hearts and devastated, we want to send our most sincere condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, to all his team-mates, friends, and to CD Tenerife."

Tenerife and Andorra were drawing 2-2 seven minutes into stoppage time when the incident occurred.

Owono ran towards the centre circle to clear a long ball when his knee appeared to collide with De Miguel.

The striker lay motionless on the pitch as medical staff treated him before he was taken by ambulance from Tenerife's Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez to hospital.

Players from both teams were visibly distressed by the incident, with a number of De Miguel's team-mates in tears.

The referee showed Owono a straight red card before abandoning the match.

Spanish media, including Marca, reported De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest in the ambulance and was resuscitated by paramedics on the way to hospital.

Tenerife described his condition on Monday night as "serious but stable" but a further update on Tuesday morning said De Miguel's condition had "worsened neurologically".
