"One way or the other, we will do something, but there is no rush. We crippled them financially," he told news outlet Axios. "They have no money, no gasoline and their people are getting very tired of it."

He also said the US "might need to go after Pickaxe [Mountain]", an underground site linked to Iran's nuclear programme, in an interview with Fox News on the eve of the midterm elections.

This was "not a big deal" and could be done in "one hour", Trump added.

There has been mounting speculation in the last few days that the US may resume significant strikes in Iran again after the midterms. But asked by a reporter on Monday if that was the case, Trump said "no".

Iran's Foreign Minister, Abbas Araghchi, told Irna that "very intensive" talks to try to end the war were under way with the US via mediators.

He also said Iran was prepared for both diplomatic and military scenarios "more than ever before" and that it was up to the US to choose between a "wise path" of negotiation or the "mistake of military aggression".

World.title: Supreme Court rejects Trump's request to stop California counting disputed votes
World.content:
The US Supreme Court has rejected a last-minute request by the Trump administration asking it to intervene in California's midterm election vote count.

The justice department wanted 20,000 ballots to be set aside that it alleged may have been issued to non-US citizens in the state.

Two lower courts had already rejected the request. State election officials had questioned the federal government's claims - saying the process used to identify alleged non-citizens was inaccurate.

The Monday ruling comes on the eve of the midterms, which will determine which political party controls the US Congress for the last two years of President Donald Trump's second term.

The Supreme Court announced its decision in a one-line order, saying it was denying the justice department's request for an injunction.

"The application for injunction pending appeal presented to Justice Kagan and by her referred to the Court is denied," it reads.

Its means rulings made in lower courts will stand and essentially ends the Trump administration's bid to disqualify the ballots.

California is the most populous state in America with some 23 million people on its voting register. As of Sunday night, more than six million mail-in ballots had already been received, according to the California secretary of state's office.

World.title: Russian bombing kills 29 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says
World.content:
At least 29 people were killed after Russian bombs hit an aid distribution centre, in an attack that Ukraine's leader has called "utterly horrific".

Another 10 people were injured and 48 were reported missing after at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit the village of Komyshuvakha in the southern Zaporizhzhia region, regional head Mykhailo Semikin said.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said that after the first strike on the local school "used for humanitarian needs", there was a second attack on the place where people were sheltering.

He posted a video showing a huge crater left after Monday's attack, and rescuer teams searching through the rubble.

The Russian military has not publicly commented.

World.title: Tenerife striker De Miguel dies after on-field collision
World.content:
Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel has died after the 30-year-old suffered a serious injury during a Spanish second-division match.

The forward suffered head and chest injuries during a match against FC Andorra on Monday, in a heavy collision with goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who was sent off for his challenge.

De Miguel's condition was described as 'stable but serious' on Monday but his health deteriorated on Tuesday morning, with the Spaniard passing away at 07:00 GMT (08:00 local time).

"Heartbroken, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe this is true, CD Tenerife announces the tragic death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," a club statement said.

"There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can lessen this overwhelming sadness. We stand with his grieving family, with his loved ones, with all of Tenerife who mourn this cruel loss today.

"The family of Jesus de Miguel is grateful for each and every expression of support received, and also requests, from the bottom of their hearts, the utmost respect for their privacy during these terrible times."

Andorra, Tenerife's opponents on Monday, said: "With broken hearts and devastated, we want to send our most sincere condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, to all his team-mates, friends, and to CD Tenerife."

Former Barcelona defender Gerard Pique, who co-owns Andorra, said: "I am sorry with all my soul. Rest in peace, Jesus."

De Miguel's former club, Castellon, said: "It's hard to find words when reality strikes in such an unfair way.

"We join with all our affection in the grief of his family and loved ones, whom we embrace in these terribly difficult moments and to whom we extend our most heartfelt condolences."

Tenerife and Andorra were drawing 2-2 seven minutes into stoppage time when the incident occurred.

Owono ran towards the centre circle to clear a long ball when his knee appeared to collide with De Miguel.

The striker lay motionless on the pitch as medical staff treated him before he was taken by ambulance from Tenerife's Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez to hospital.

Players from both teams were visibly distressed by the incident, with a number of De Miguel's team-mates in tears.

The referee showed Owono a straight red card before abandoning the match.

Spanish media, including Marca, reported De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest in the ambulance and was resuscitated by paramedics on the way to hospital.

Tenerife described his condition on Monday night as "serious but stable" but a further update on Tuesday morning said De Miguel's condition had "worsened neurologically".

De Miguel, who was born in Madrid, started his career at Leganes in 2015 and went on to play for eight different clubs in Spain.

After spells with Lugo Fuenlabrada and Internacional Madrid, he returned to Fuenlabrada before stints at Union Adarve, Navalcarnero and Unionistas.

He joined Castellon in 2023 and scored 16 goals as the club achieved promotion to Spain's second division a year later.

The Spaniard joined Tenerife on a three-year deal in 2025 and scored 11 goals in 29 appearances for the side.

De Miguel is survived by his daughter, Carla de Miguel Fernandez, who was born in 2025.

World.title: Plane may have broken apart ahead of deadly Florida jet crash, say investigators
World.content:
It confirmed that, after the jet took off from Austin, the crew transmitted to air traffic control that they were encountering ice and moderate turbulence.

"We are picking up precipitation, requesting to climb to 37,000 feet if able," the crew said.

NTSB member Tom Chapman said that less than 30 seconds later, the plane began to descend and the crew issued a mayday call.

The transmission then became "unintelligible", he said, adding that: "Sadly, all aboard were lost."

The NTSB said that ice and turbulence were factors in the crash but that determining its probable cause will be a "lengthy investigatory process".

Thunderstorms had been reported in the area at the time.

Officials are also trying to find out whether a cockpit voice recorder was on board at the time of the crash and if it can be recovered.

As part of the investigation, the NTSB is working with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), representatives from Learjet as well as meteorologists and air traffic control experts.

Recovering the wreckage from the crater on the roadway will be a "daunting challenge", said Timothy Monville, an air safety investigator with the safety board.

World.title: Asian Cup postponed in wake of attacks on Saudi Arabia
World.content:
The 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia has been postponed because of a series of deadly attacks on the host country.

The 24-team tournament was scheduled to take place from 7 January to 5 February but has been rescheduled to run from 23 December, 2027 to 21 January, 2028.

In October, a missile attack by Yemen's Houthi movement on Riyadh's airport killed 13 people and wounded more than 300.

A statement from the the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), external said the decision to reschedule had been taken "in light of the current exceptional circumstances arising from developments in the region, including substantial logistical complexities and travel disruptions".

It added: "The new dates of the tournament will be presented to Fifa for approval."

A number of events in Saudi Arabia have been cancelled recently, including the Six Kings Slam tennis exhibition event, which was scheduled to be in Riyadh.

The Asian Tour has also indefinitely postponed it's season-ending golf tournament, which was scheduled to take place from 18-21 November.

This is the second successive Asian Cup to be postponed after the 2023 tournament was moved to 2024 and to Qatar from China because of the Covid pandemic.

World.title: Thousands of European troops to rehearse Ukraine deployment in event of peace
World.content:
Britain and France are to lead a military exercise to test a multinational force's ability to deploy to Ukraine, if there is a peace deal.

Nearly 3,000 military personnel from 12 European nations will take part in the rehearsal in neighbouring Poland this month.

Plans for a reassurance force for Ukraine were set out last year as one of the long-term security guarantees being proposed by European nations.

But there are still more questions than answers as to how such a military force might work in practice. Western officials stress that any force sent to Ukraine would not take part in offensive operations or be involved in peacekeeping or ceasefire monitoring missions.

Nor would they be operating under the command of Nato or on the front line.

Officials say their presence would be to provide reassurance to Ukraine and to help rebuild its armed forces.

The US has been involved in discussions, but is not contributing to the mission.

Russia has already voiced opposition to foreign troops being stationed in Ukraine and, last year, President Vladimir Putin said they would be "legitimate targets".

Western officials have declined to spell out the rules of engagement if any international troops were to be attacked in Ukraine. Though they say the force would be able to defend itself.

UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said the exercise showed Britain, France and their allies were stepping up preparation for the day when peace came to Ukraine.

He said: "This is not a hypothetical plan, it's a real force, ready to help Ukraine once the fighting stops."

Lt Gen Tom Bateman, the UK commander of the Multi National Force â Ukraine (MNF-U), said the exercise represented an important step in translating political commitments into credible military readiness.

He said it was a "real, capable, readily deployable force that represented a serious commitment from Coalition of the Willing nations to Ukraine's long-term stability and security".

World.title: 20th coronation Anniversary: Gov Lawal hails Sultan as beacon of unity and stability
World.content:
The Sultan of Sokoto, Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III and Governor Dauda Lawal during the coronation anniversary in Sokoto on Monday.

Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal has described His Eminence, the Sultan of Sokoto, as a humble leader who brings people together and provides stability.

On Monday, the governor attended the 13th Shaikh Usmanu Bin Fodiyo Week and the 20th anniversary of the coronation of His Eminence, the Sultan of Sokoto, Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, at the International Conference Centre in Sokoto.

This year’s ceremony, with the theme ‘Reviving Ethical Leadership and Social Harmony: Lessons from Sokoto Jihad Leaders’, brought together notable figures from Nigeria and beyond.

In his goodwill message, Governor Lawal said the government and people of Zamfara State have been greatly inspired by the Sultan’s wisdom, guidance, and steady leadership, especially during difficult social and security times.

He said, “With immense joy, respect, and gratitude to Almighty Allah (SWT), on behalf of the government and people of Zamfara State, I congratulate His Eminence Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, 20th Sultan of Sokoto and leader of the Ummah, on the historic 20th anniversary of his coronation.

“We remain deeply grateful for your recent presence and support at our coronation and presentation of staff of office to our 19 Emirs in Gusau, which further underscores your commitment to strengthening the traditional institutions across our region.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“This year’s celebration reminds us that the Sokoto Caliphate’s legacy transcends borders. Its enduring values, knowledge, justice, moral discipline, responsible leadership and human dignity remain relevant to today’s challenges.

“Closer to home in Zamfara State, this legacy carries a particularly compelling message. At a time when insecurity, moral decline, poverty and youth vulnerability threaten our communities, we must draw inspiration from the teachings of Sheikh Usmanu Dan Fodiyo to promote peace, justice, education and social responsibility.”

Earlier, the Sultan thanked everyone who played a part and contributed during his 20 years as the Sultan of Sokoto. He encouraged religious, traditional, and community leaders to work even harder to promote peace.

World.title: UNILAG VC threatens N1bn defamation suit over report on alleged financial irregularities
World.content:
The Vice-Chancellor of the University of Lagos (UNILAG), Folasade Ogunsola, has threatened to sue an online media organisation, Naija OnPoint, for N1 billion over a report alleging financial irregularities at the university.

In a letter dated 29 October, addressed to the editor-in-chief and publisher of Naija OnPoint, Mrs Ogunsola demanded that the organisation remove the publication, retract it and apologise to Mrs Ogunsola within 48 hours of receiving the letter.

The letter, signed by Taiwo Osipitan, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), of Bayo Osipitan & Co., was made available to PREMIUM TIMES on Saturday.

The disputed report, titled “Citadel of Criminals: Under VC Folashade Ogunsola, UNILAG Staff Pocketed N397million In Irregular Payments While N434million In Cash Advances Went Unretired”, was published on Naija OnPoint’s website and its accounts on X and LinkedIn, according to the letter.

However, PREMIUM TIMES could not independently find the report on Naija OnPoint’s website. A report with the same headline was published by Secrets Reporters on 24 October.

The Secrets Reporters investigation alleged that university staff received N397.5 million in irregular payments, while N434.8 million in cash advances remained unretired.

It also reported that N355.6 million in payments had no supporting documents and that N178 million was paid to staff as unapproved allowances.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The publication also reported N121.7 million worth of store items allegedly missing from the university’s inventory records, N116.4 million in payments said to have violated the federal government’s e-payment policy and N82.9 million in cash advances granted above the approved limit.

The report also listed unaccounted withdrawals from university accounts, unapproved travel grants and payments for international trips allegedly made without approval.

It was the third in a series of reports by Secrets Reporters into the university’s financial management under Mrs Ogunsola.

In two earlier reports, the publication alleged that UNILAG failed to disclose N7.83 billion worth of contracts on Nigeria’s Open Contracting Portal, did not remit N3.89 billion in internally generated revenue to government coffers and paid N7 billion for contracts whose execution auditors could not verify.

The publication linked the alleged financial irregularities to Mrs Ogunsola, who was vice-chancellor during the financial year covered by the audit.

But her lawyer said the report wrongly associated their client with alleged financial misconduct by unidentified university staff.

Mr Osipitan, a professor, argued that its headline and contents portrayed her as a dishonest administrator who condoned the misappropriation of public funds and presided over a university populated by criminals.

The lawyer stated that Mrs Ogunsola did not object to investigative journalism or responsible reporting on matters of public interest but rejected “false and unverified allegations” capable of damaging her reputation.

He said she denied engaging in, authorising, participating in or knowingly facilitating any criminal conduct or financial impropriety.

The lawyer also cited laws on defamation and cybercrime, specifically referring to Section 24 of the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, Etc.) Act, as amended.

He demanded that Naija OnPoint publish a retraction and apology with prominence comparable to the original report. The organisation was also asked to provide a written undertaking not to republish the allegations and to take steps to prevent their further circulation.

The lawyer warned that failure to meet the demands within 48 hours would lead to legal action against the organisation and other persons responsible for circulating the publication.

He also threatened to refer the matter to law enforcement authorities for investigation and possible prosecution.

In the proposed suit, Mrs Ogunsola is seeking N500 million in general damages and another N500 million in exemplary damages.

She is also seeking a court declaration that the publication is defamatory, an order compelling its removal from the website and social media platforms, and a perpetual injunction restraining further publication of the allegations.

Reaction

NaijaOnPoint’s Head publisher, Anthony Balogun, said the publication had removed the report from its website and social media platforms, including X and LinkedIn.

In an email to PREMIUM TIMES on Monday, Mr Balogun said the article was culled from Secrets Reporters and was not an original investigation by NaijaOnPoint.

He added that the publication had informed Mrs Ogunsola’s lawyer of the removal and received an acknowledgement of its response.

“We consider the matter resolved,” he said.

World.title: Family seeks closure of son’s betting accounts over alleged gambling addiction
World.content:
A family in Jalingo, Taraba State, has appealed to sports betting companies to suspend or permanently close the betting accounts of a young man, Paul Matudi, over concerns about his alleged gambling addiction.

The family said Mr Matudi’s involvement in sports betting had become excessive, raising concerns about its impact on his education, finances and the emotional well-being of relatives.

The appeal was contained in a letter dated 30 October and addressed to the management of betting companies operating in Jalingo and Ardo-Kola Local Government Areas of the state.

The letter, signed by Abraham Matudi, who identified himself as the young man’s family representative, urged betting operators to immediately suspend, freeze or permanently block Paul Matudi’s accounts to prevent further betting activities.

“The situation is affecting Paul’s ability to concentrate on his education and exercise control over his betting activities,” the family said in the letter.

The family also urged betting companies to enforce responsible gambling measures, particularly in cases involving customers suspected to be under 18 or showing signs of compulsive gambling.

It warned that it would not accept responsibility for any financial losses or other consequences arising from betting activities on the accounts after the formal request for their closure.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We will not accept responsibility for any financial losses or other consequences arising from continued betting activities after the formal request for account closure,” the letter stated.

Mr Abraham further appealed to operators who receive the letter to circulate it among other betting outlets and companies in the two local government areas to ensure that the request reaches all relevant platforms.

The family said it expected the companies to cooperate and provide confirmation once the accounts had been disabled.

The appeal comes amid growing concerns about the effects of sports betting among young Nigerians, particularly its potential consequences for education, financial stability and family relationships.

World.title: DevReporting appoints UNILAG VC, former LASU VC as foundation’s advisory board chairs
World.content:
The Vice-Chancellor of the University of Lagos (UNILAG), Folasade Ogunsola, and former Vice-Chancellor of Lagos State University (LASU), Olanrewaju Fagbohun, have been appointed as chairs of the advisory board of the Development Reporting Africa Foundation (DRAF), the non-profit arm of DevReporting.

Ms Ogunsola, a professor of medical microbiology, and Mr Fagbohun, a professor of environmental law, were appointed alongside four other members of the six-member advisory board.

Samson Ademola, DevReporting’s Project Manager and Associate Editor, has also been appointed the pioneer Executive Director of the foundation.

The appointments were announced on 29 October, during the unveiling of DRAF at the University of Lagos.

The event also featured the premiere of LG’s Billion in the Dark, an investigative documentary by DevReporting examining the prolonged local government leadership crisis in Osun State, as well as a fundraising initiative to support the foundation’s activities.

Human rights lawyer Femi Falana delivered the keynote address, while publisher of PREMIUM TIMES and CEO of the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID), Dapo Olorunyomi, chaired the event.

New foundation

DRAF is the non-profit arm of Development Reporting Services Limited, publishers of DevReporting.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The foundation said it was established to strengthen development journalism, advance research, promote public accountability and foster partnerships that contribute to sustainable development across Africa.

The foundation is governed by a Board of Directors chaired by Mojeed Alabi, Team Lead and Editor-in-Chief of DevReporting.

Apart from Ms Ogunsola and Mr Fagbohun, other members of the advisory board are Blessing Ahmed, Managing Partner of Blue Diamond Law Firm; Oluwole Alabi, an obstetrician and gynaecologist; Theophilus Abbah, Director of Daily Trust Foundation; and Bolaji Abimbola, Managing Director of Integrated Indigo Limited.

The organisation said the advisory board would provide strategic guidance and support the foundation’s institutional development and partnerships.

Ademola takes charge

Mr Ademola brings more than a decade of experience in programme management, research, journalism and media capacity development, including managing donor-funded initiatives across Nigeria, Ghana and South Africa.

He previously spent about eight years at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Investigative Journalism (WSCIJ), where he managed programmes supported by the MacArthur Foundation, Gates Foundation and Open Society Initiative for West Africa (OSIWA), including grant-making to more than 25 media organisations.

Reacting to his appointment, Mr Ademola thanked the Board of Directors for the confidence reposed in him.

“I am grateful for the confidence reposed in me to lead the Foundation. I accept this responsibility with humility, a strong sense of purpose and a commitment to building an institution that makes meaningful contributions to development journalism and sustainable development across Africa.”

He said he looked forward to working with the board, advisers, partners and other stakeholders to translate the foundation’s vision into programmes with measurable impact.

Mr Ademola also outlined proposed programmes, including youth civic engagement through campus documentary screenings, training, mentorship and youth-led accountability projects across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones.

He said the fundraising initiative would help mobilise resources for these programmes and other activities aimed at strengthening public-interest journalism and citizen participation in governance.

Foundation seeks partnerships

Building on DevReporting’s experience in investigative journalism, media capacity development and collaborative reporting, DRAF said it aims to strengthen the role of evidence-based journalism in promoting accountability and improving development outcomes.

The foundation is seeking partnerships and support from institutions and individuals committed to public-interest journalism and sustainable development.

World.title: WAFCON: Tinubu fulfils $100,000 cash reward promise as Super Falcons players begin receiving payments
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has fulfilled his promise to reward members of the Super Falcons with the naira equivalent of $100,000 each following Nigeria’s record-extending 10th Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) title in 2025.

The players have begun receiving payments estimated at ₦140 million each, according to a statement issued by the National Sports Commission (NSC) on Monday and signed by Kola Daniel, special assistant on media to the Director-General.

The payment represents the cash component of the reward Mr Tinubu promised after the Super Falcons defeated hosts Morocco 3-2 in a dramatic final in Rabat on 26 July 2025.

The NSC said the payment was a fulfilment of the president’s commitment to recognise the team’s achievement and reward sporting excellence.

Nigeria produced a remarkable comeback in the final after trailing 2-0 at half-time, with Esther Okoronkwo converting a penalty in the 64th minute before setting up Folashade Ijamilusi for the equaliser seven minutes later.

Substitute Jennifer Echegini completed the turnaround with an 88th-minute winner, handing Nigeria its 10th continental title and extending the Super Falcons’ record as the most successful team in the history of the women’s competition.

The victory was particularly significant as Nigeria reclaimed the African crown after losing to Morocco in the semi-finals of the 2022 edition, which was played in 2023.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Team captain Rasheedat Ajibade thanked Mr Tinubu for fulfilling the financial commitment, describing the gesture as recognition of the team’s achievement and contribution to Nigerian sports, the statement said.

The NSC said the payment reflected the administration’s commitment to rewarding athletes for their performances on the international stage.

The Super Falcons’ reward follows a similar arrangement for Nigeria’s senior women’s basketball team, D’Tigress, after their triumph at the 2025 FIBA Women’s AfroBasket in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire.

D’Tigress defeated Mali 78-64 in the final on 3 August 2025 to win their fifth consecutive AfroBasket title and seventh overall, becoming the first team to achieve five successive victories in the competition.

Mr Tinubu subsequently promised each player $100,000, alongside three-bedroom apartments in Abuja and national honours. Members of the coaching and technical crew were also promised financial rewards and other benefits.

In September 2026, the NSC confirmed that the cash component of the presidential reward had been paid to D’Tigress, with each player receiving the naira equivalent of $100,000 and team officials receiving $50,000 each.

For the Super Falcons, the NSC said the latest payment followed the earlier presentation of title documents for three-bedroom apartments in Abuja and certificates of national honours of Officer of the Order of the Niger (OON).

The commission is led by its chairman, Shehu Dikko, and Director-General, Bukola Olopade, who have overseen the administration’s sports development programmes.

In Monday’s statement, the NSC commended Mr Tinubu for his support for Nigerian athletes, saying fulfilling the reward commitments would strengthen confidence among athletes and sports administrators.

The commission also said its efforts were focused on improving athlete welfare, expanding international opportunities and attracting investment into the country’s sports sector.

World.title: Lawmakers propose 74 additional seats for women in Nigeria’s National Assembly
World.content:
The National Assembly’s Constitution Review Committee has proposed the creation of 74 additional seats for women in the Senate and House of Representatives as part of efforts to increase women’s participation in politics and governance.

The committee also proposed three additional seats reserved for women in each state House of Assembly, without displacing any existing electoral seats.

The Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, disclosed this at the 2026 Law Week organised by the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA), Ekiti State Chapter, on Monday.

Mr Bamidele, vice chairman of the Senate Committee on Constitution Review, said the proposals were designed to strengthen women’s participation in Nigeria’s political and governance processes.

“A Bill for an Act to alter the provisions of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 to provide for special seats for women in the National and State Houses of Assembly and for related matters is receiving our attention at the National Assembly.

“The proposal, as it stands, is meticulous in its design. It seeks to add 37 seats in the Senate and 37 seats in the House of Representatives. This suggests that if finally approved, each state of the federation, including the FCT, will have one additional seat in each of the Houses of the National Assembly,” he said.

Mr Bamidele, who represents Ekiti Central Senatorial District, said the proposed arrangement would run for 16 years, covering four electoral cycles, before a comprehensive review.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The Constitution Review Committee has already proposed three additional seats for each State House of Assembly, all specifically reserved for women, without displacing any existing electoral seats.

“This arrangement is proposed to run for a period of 16 years, four electoral cycles, before a comprehensive review. This is a sunset clause designed to ensure sustainability and to allow for the organic development of a more inclusive political culture,” he added.

The Senate leader said federal lawmakers had also begun engaging their counterparts at the state level to facilitate the proposals’ approval by state assemblies once they are passed by the National Assembly.

“We are actively and strategically engaging with the State Houses of Assembly, as their concurrence is a constitutional sine qua non for bringing this reform to fruition. However, let me add a crucial point that speaks to the very essence of our democratic journey and the Renewed Hope Agenda.”

Special seats not partisan

Mr Bamidele said the proposal for special seats for women was not a partisan initiative, arguing that creating additional seats for women was necessary to strengthen Nigeria’s democracy.

“The special seat initiative is not a partisan endeavour. It is a historic imperative. The rationale is anchored on a simple, yet profound, principle of constitutional law: the foundational precept of representative democracy. A democracy that systematically excludes over half of its population from the decision-making tables that determine their futures is, at best, a flawed democracy and, at worst, a veiled oligarchy.

“We were mindful of the reality that the state must intervene to provide a robust safety net where the market and tradition fail. This recognition is translated into legislative support for healthcare initiatives, educational access, and social protection programmes that are meticulously targeted at the most vulnerable demographics: our women, our children, and persons with disabilities.”

Mr Bamidele also said the proposed special seats would strengthen protections for women and help reduce domestic violence.

“A woman who suffers domestic violence must be able to seek protection without intimidation or social condemnation. A child who experiences abuse must be heard, protected from further harm, and provided with appropriate support.

“Victims must have access to legal assistance, medical care, and psychosocial services, while perpetrators must be held accountable in accordance with due process and the rule of law.”

The proposal for special seats for women

The proposal for special seats for women comes amid concerns over the underrepresentation of women in Nigeria’s political institutions. Women have historically occupied only a small proportion of seats in the National Assembly, despite making up nearly half of the country’s population.

Supporters of reserved seats argue that the measure would address structural barriers to women’s political participation, including the high cost of elections, party nomination practices, discrimination and gender-based violence. They say increasing women’s representation would make the legislature more inclusive and improve the consideration of issues affecting women and children.

However, critics of affirmative action have questioned whether reserved seats could undermine the principle of equal representation or create a class of legislators with a different electoral mandate. Others argue that the reform should be accompanied by measures to address barriers within political parties and the electoral system.

If approved, the proposal would expand the legislature and could increase women’s influence in lawmaking and oversight. Its effectiveness would depend on the electoral arrangements, the selection process for the reserved seats and whether the reform is accompanied by political reforms. The proposed 16-year duration would also make the arrangement temporary, with a review expected after four electoral cycles.

World.title: 2027 Politics Watch: Battle for place on ballot, Kano question INEC yet to answer
World.content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) wants a court to stop some of its former members from contesting next year’s elections under opposition parties in Niger State.

Among those whose nominations it is challenging are the governorship candidates of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and Social Democratic Party (SDP), both of whom left the ruling party after disagreements over its primary.

If the APC succeeds, candidates already nominated by opposition parties could be prevented from appearing on the ballot.

In Kano, another dispute raises a question for the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC): why was a governorship candidate’s name missing from a list published on 10 October when the court order subsequently cited to explain his exclusion was reportedly issued on 27 October?

The candidate, Aminu Gwarzo of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), is demanding an explanation. He says his party has taken INEC to court and is preparing to challenge the restraining order.

In Ogun, the PDP is preparing legal action over the omission of governorship candidate Ladi Adebutu, while Accord is defending its nominations against a lawsuit brought by its national secretary.

APC challenges former members’ nominations in Niger

The Niger APC has filed a suit at the Federal High Court in Minna against PDP governorship candidate Mohammed Nami, SDP candidate Mohammed Ndarani Mohammed and several other politicians who defected from the party.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

INEC is the first defendant in the case, which LEADERSHIP reported was filed by 11 Senior Advocates of Nigeria led by Jacob Usman.

The suit names INEC, the PDP, SDP, ADC and NDC, alongside several politicians, including Senator Peter Jiya, NDC senatorial candidate Sadiq Rabiu and ADC deputy governorship candidate Musa Mamman.

The APC alleges that the politicians joined other parties without formally resigning their membership of the ruling party. It wants the court to refuse recognition of their defections and restrain INEC from recognising them as candidates or members of their new parties.

Mr Nami and Mr Ndarani emerged as governorship candidates of their respective parties after leaving the APC following disputes over its primaries.

The suit follows the Supreme Court’s judgement of 24 September, which restored Sections 77(5)–(7) and 84(2) of the Electoral Act 2026 governing party membership registers and candidate nominations.

The court held that the membership-register provisions do not automatically disqualify individual candidates. Whether the APC’s separate allegations about the politicians’ defections justify the orders sought remains for the Federal High Court to determine.

Kano’s disputed timeline

INEC omitted Aminu Gwarzo and his running mate, Mustapha Kwankwaso, from its governorship candidates’ list published on 10 October.

The omission was reported by PREMIUM TIMES the following day, when the NDC said commission officials had attributed it to a computer problem.

On 27 October, a Federal High Court in Kano reportedly issued an interim order restraining publication of the candidates’ names. INEC subsequently said Mr Gwarzo had satisfied its nomination requirements but that the court order prevented it from publishing his name.

Mr Gwarzo has questioned why his name was missing before the order was issued. He says the proceedings began on 17 October, although that filing date has not been independently confirmed.

During an interview with ARISE News, reported by LEADERSHIP, he accused officials linked to the Kano State Government and APC of working to prevent his participation in the election.

He alleged that the proceedings began without the candidates being served and said the NDC would seek to join the case and challenge the interim order. His allegation of political interference has not been independently substantiated.

The NDC has also approached the Federal High Court in Abuja, seeking an order compelling INEC to include its governorship ticket on the candidates’ list.

The dispute has prompted protests by party supporters and criticism from former Kano governor Rabiu Kwankwaso, who accused political opponents of attempting to prevent the NDC from contesting.

INEC’s updated list still excluded the NDC ticket, citing the court order.

The commission has not publicly explained the original omission. The certified court order and INEC’s correspondence with the party would help establish the reasons for its decisions.

Ogun and Accord: Two more nomination battles

The PDP in Ogun State says it will approach the court after INEC declined to include Ladi Adebutu in its final list of governorship candidates.

The party’s publicity secretary, Kayode Adebayo, said proceedings would begin during the week but did not provide a filing date.

Mr Adebutu and his running mate were omitted from the 10 October list, although the PDP maintains that they satisfied the nomination requirements.

INEC subsequently reviewed petitions from political parties over excluded candidates but did not restore Mr Adebutu’s name.

The commission approved other requests, including PDP governorship candidate Isa Pantami’s in Gombe State.

That difference prompted questions from Ogun PDP supporters and the Egba Integrity Group, which accused INEC of applying the relevant legal requirements inconsistently.

The group threatened separate legal action unless INEC reconsidered its decision.

Accord, meanwhile, is defending its nominations against a suit brought by National Secretary Adebukola Ajaja.

The party has filed a preliminary objection challenging her standing to bring the action and arguing that the case was instituted outside the statutory period.

The dispute concerns who had authority to conduct and submit nominations on the party’s behalf.

It follows a Federal High Court judgment on 5 October ordering recognition of Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim as Accord’s presidential candidate.

The preliminary objection does not overturn the earlier Federal High Court judgment recognising Mr Olawepo-Hashim as Accord’s presidential candidate.

Unlike the Niger suit, which challenges politicians who changed parties, the Kano and Ogun disputes concern INEC’s treatment of nominations. Accord’s case turns on who was authorised to submit its candidates.

Kebbi demolition dispute, South-west ADC response

The Kebbi State Government has denied ordering the demolition of property associated with ADC governorship candidate Abubakar Malami.

The denial followed allegations that suspected APC supporters demolished the property on government instructions.

The state government rejected the accusation, saying the matter involved a private land dispute and was being misrepresented as political intimidation.

Reports identified the property as being opposite Azbir Hotel along Sani Abacha Bypass in Birnin Kebbi. A businessman, Umaru Gulumbe, was named as another claimant to the land.

The ADC had earlier called for an independent investigation, maintaining that the property was lawfully acquired and developed.

Neither the government’s denial nor the ADC’s allegations establish who authorised the demolition. Ownership records and any demolition notice would be needed to determine responsibility.

Elsewhere in the ADC, the party’s South-west leadership issued a collective statement rejecting reports of a rift with presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar.

National Vice Chairman Akin Omole and the six state chairmen reaffirmed their support for Atiku and rejected claims that the regional leadership had held a virtual meeting with him on 5 September to resolve an internal crisis.

They said an earlier gathering in Ibadan concerned party organisation and mobilisation, not opposition to the presidential candidate.

The statement followed complaints about the exclusion of party officials from campaign consultations. Atiku’s campaign had previously said state councils were yet to be inaugurated and nominations were still being collected, but no inauguration date has been announced.

Bayelsa disagreement, Rivers charter and Katsina defections

In Bayelsa, former governor Seriake Dickson criticised his successor, Douye Diri, for moving from the PDP to the APC.

Mr Dickson made the remarks during political activities associated with NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi’s visit to the state.

He accused Mr Diri of abandoning the party that brought him to office and urged voters to reject the APC in 2027. An aide to the governor reportedly declined to respond.

In Rivers, the APC and NDC explained the absence of their governorship candidates from a ceremony where five other candidates signed a 13-point citizens’ charter.

APC spokesperson Chibike Ikenga questioned whether Kingsley Chinda had been invited. The NDC said Dumo Lulu-Briggs received an invitation but couldn’t attend because of an engagement in Bayelsa.

The organisers maintained that both candidates were invited and could sign separately. Neither campaign said it opposed the charter.

In Katsinana, members of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) declared support for PDP governorship candidate Yakubu Danmarke at a rally on Sunday.

Organisers put the number of defectors at about 5,000, a figure that has not been independently verified.

What comes next

The Niger APC’s suit remains before the Federal High Court, while the NDC is pursuing legal action over the exclusion of its governorship ticket in Kano.

In Ogun, the PDP says it will approach the court this week over Ladi Adebutu’s omission from INEC’s list.

Atiku’s presidential campaign, meanwhile, is scheduled to launch in Sokoto on Wednesday, 4 November, following an earlier postponement.

World.title: Army destroys kidnappers’ hideout, recovers ammunition in Kogi
World.content:
Troops of the Nigerian Army have destroyed a suspected kidnappers’ hideout in Edimogbo Forest, Igalamela/Odolu Local Government Area of Kogi State, recovering 1,000 rounds of ammunition and other items.

Troops of the 21 Battalion Quick Reaction Force carried out the operation following intelligence about suspected kidnappers operating from the forest, the Army said.

In a statement on Monday, the Acting Director of Army Public Relations, Appolonia Anele, said the suspects fired a shot to alert other members of their group when they sighted the advancing troops before fleeing deeper into the forest.

She said the troops pursued the suspects but did not make contact with them. They subsequently destroyed the camp and its supporting structures.

Items recovered included 1,000 rounds of 7.62mm x 54 ammunition, seven bandoliers, six motorcycles, two shovels, a hand pump, a mobile phone and a Glo modem.

The troops also recovered soap, a jerrycan of petrol, clothing and shoes, according to Ms Anele.

She said troops were still searching the surrounding area to track down the fleeing suspects.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Army urged residents to provide security agencies with timely information to support operations against kidnappers and other criminal groups.

The operation comes days after troops of the Joint Task Force Operation WHIRL STROKE reported killing two suspected bandits during an intelligence-led ambush along the Adankolo–Apata Road in Kogi State.

In a statement on 31 October, the task force’s Acting Media Information Officer, Ahmad Zubairu, said troops had received intelligence about the movement of suspected bandits around communities in Kabba-Bunu and Lokoja local government areas.

He said troops laid an ambush along a suspected supply route and later recovered the bodies of two suspected bandits in the direction of Adankolo Forest. A locally made pistol, a cartridge and an empty case of 7.62mm special ammunition were also recovered.

The Force Commander of Operation WHIRL STROKE, Moses Gara, commended the troops and urged residents to continue providing security agencies with credible information.

World.title: DSS frees four suspected IPOB members, pays ₦20m compensation
World.content:
DSS

By Soni Daniel

The Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi, has approved the release of four persons detained over their alleged involvement with the proscribed Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB), alongside ₦20 million in compensation.

The four beneficiaries are Emele Uduma Ibe, Berefgagha Appah, Ondokeyilemi Aggry and Oyeinmokebebeton Aggry.

Security sources disclosed that they were arrested in May 2022 while allegedly attempting to establish an IPOB camp in Sampou and Akeddei communities in Kolokuma/Opokuma and Sagbama Local Government Areas of Bayelsa State.

According to the sources, investigations by the DSS established that the four men were still at the recruitment stage before their arrest.

One of the sources said the investigation revealed that they had been misled into believing that they would each receive a monthly payment of ₦100,000 under the Federal Government’s Amnesty Programme.

The sources added that their remorse and good conduct while in detention, alongside the findings of the investigation, influenced the DSS DG’s decision to release and compensate them.

The latest development follows similar decisions by Ajayi to release other persons detained over alleged involvement in IPOB activities and approve financial compensation for them.

Last November, the DSS DG ordered the release of Kenneth Okechukwu Nwafor, who was arrested in July 2022 over his alleged involvement in IPOB activities. He also approved ₦5 million compensation for him.

Before Nwafor’s release, three other men from Abia State — Augustine Udemba, Nelson Onyedikachi Udemba and Ifesinachi Eze — were also freed and each awarded ₦5 million in compensation.

Earlier, in October 2025, Ajayi ordered the release of an Abuja-based businesswoman, Mrs Chineze Ozoadibe, and approved ₦10 million compensation for her.

A security source said the DSS had acknowledged that, like other human institutions, the Service was not immune to mistakes.

The source said Ajayi had also pledged that whenever such mistakes were identified, the Service would acknowledge them, offer compensation and take steps to improve its operations in line with the rule of law.

World.title: North Korea test fires strategic cruise missiles
World.content:
A man walks past a television screen showing a news broadcast with file footage of a North Korean missile test, at a train station in Seoul on October 22, 2025. North Korea fired at least one ballistic missile on October 22, Seoul’s military said, its first such launch in months. (Photo by Jung Yeon-je / AFP)

North Korea test-fired strategic cruise missiles, state media reported Tuesday, in the latest display of its weapons capabilities as tensions persist on the Korean peninsula.

The Monday launch came a day after North Korea tested cluster bomb warheads, as tensions with Seoul have risen after a landmine blast along their heavily fortified border wounded three South Korean soldiers.

“The middle-sized dispersal warhead tipped on the cruise missile is capable of turning into ashes a target area of 5 to 6 hectares with its highest-density power,” the official Korean Central News Agency reported Tuesday.

The test “perfected the capability to deliver a vertical strike against the target by improving the terminal maneuverability of the cruise missile,” KCNA said, “taking into consideration the natural and geographical characteristics of the targeted area.”

A North Korean official was quoted as saying the test was conducted “because our armed forces should defend the security of the country and deter all sorts of threats.”

“Various combat functions of such strongest weapon system will help defend the DPRK from potential threats from outside and renew the military capabilities of the state,” the general director of the Missile Administration said, using the acronym for North Korea’s official name.

The nuclear-armed North recently trialled a range of weaponry including attack drones, a new precision-guided torpedo system and an intermediate-range hypersonic missile.

South Korea’s military did not announce the cruise missile launch, as it had also not done with Sunday’s test.

Unlike ballistic missile launches, North Korean cruise missile tests are not prohibited by UN Security Council sanctions.

Asked Monday about Sunday’s reported test, Joint Chiefs of Staff spokesperson Jang Do-young said South Korea and the United States were “closely coordinating and conducting a highly detailed analysis of its characteristics and specifications”.

“Our military does not announce all projectiles launched by North Korea,” said Jang.

“Whether to make an announcement is determined through a comprehensive military assessment, taking into account the protection of surveillance and reconnaissance assets and capabilities, operational security and other factors,” he added.

World.title: Abia picked for regional stroke, neurovascular centre
World.content:
Abia State Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu

. As Otti govt secures int’l recognition for health reforms

By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA — Abia State has emerged as the preferred location for a proposed stroke and neurovascular centre to serve Nigeria and West Africa, following its participation in the 2026 Sweden-Africa Neurosurgery Symposium in Gothenburg, Sweden.

The state Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, disclosed this while briefing newsmen on the outcome of this week’s State Executive Council meeting presided over by Governor Alex Otti at Government House, Umuahia.

Kanu said the selection was in recognition of Abia’s strides in healthcare delivery and the availability of qualified medical specialists, describing it as another milestone in the state’s ongoing health sector reforms.

He said the proposed centre would address the rising incidence of stroke across Africa, particularly Nigeria, by providing specialised facilities for comprehensive treatment and management of neurovascular conditions.

According to him, the state government had approved the participation of the Ministry of Health in the international symposium to explore strategic partnerships and opportunities for specialised healthcare development.

The Commissioner said Abia’s health sector reforms were also showcased at the symposium, adding that the Ministry of Health had recently been recognised as a national self-care champion.

He said the recognition underscored the state’s growing capacity to promote preventive healthcare and healthy lifestyles among residents.

On public health preparedness, Kanu disclosed that the government had established a multi-sectoral frontline technical working group to strengthen emergency response mechanisms.

He said the group had developed an Ebola preparedness and response plan, while the government had expanded the deployment of modern medical technology in specialised healthcare.

Kanu further disclosed that the Infectious Disease Hospital in Aba had been completed, alongside an infectious disease facility and specialist hospital in Umuahia, as part of efforts to strengthen the state’s capacity to tackle Ebola and other infectious diseases.

He, however, said no cases of Ebola, Lassa fever, COVID-19, diphtheria, cholera or avian influenza were recorded in Abia.

The Commissioner also announced progress in the agricultural intervention programme being implemented across the state’s 17 local government areas in partnership with the councils.

He said the initiative was designed to attract investments, boost food production, develop viable agricultural enterprises and create employment through strengthened agricultural value chains.

The Commissioner disclosed that Arochukwu LGA had a plantation plantation of over 86,000 trees, describing it as highly commendable.

On housing, Kanu said the government’s residential development at Pocket Layout had attracted overwhelming interest, with applications exceeding available units.

He disclosed that the government was considering a lottery system to ensure fairness, transparency and equity in allocating the houses.

Responding to questions, the Commissioner for Housing, Architect Chiemela Uzoije, said the project had been oversubscribed, with more than 530 applications received for 173 housing units.

“We have a total of 173 units of residences coming up there, but at the last count, up to 530-something have applied.

“It is not going to be what it used to be in the past. It is going to be in a very free and transparent manner,” Uzoije said.

Kanu also disclosed that a comprehensive assessment of existing housing estates and layouts was underway to identify infrastructure gaps and prioritise government intervention.

He said the exercise would address deficits in internal roads, utilities, security infrastructure and other essential facilities needed to improve living conditions in the estates.

On abandoned federal housing projects, the Governor’s Special Adviser, Mr Ferdinand Ekeoma, urged the media to hold public officials accountable, particularly over projects initiated by the Federal Government but left uncompleted.

Ekeoma said the Abia State Government had been executing some federal projects, stressing that providing land and fulfilling other fundamental requirements remained critical to their implementation.

World.title: NDC names Ibezi, Umeh, Nwoye to Anambra campaign council
World.content:
By Vincent Ujumadu

The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has appointed former member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Ifeanyi Ibezi, as coordinator of its Anambra State campaign council ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The campaign council also features Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central; Senator Tony Nwoye, representing Anambra North; and Chief Ebuka Onunkwo, the party’s senatorial candidate for Anambra South.

Other members include Emeka Kissinger Osisi as State Director of Youth Mobilisation, Barr. Ogechukwu Ekweozor as Director of Women Mobilisation, DIG Celestine Okoye (rtd) as Director of Security and AIG Innocent Ndubueze Anene (rtd) as Director of Election Monitoring and Vote Protection.

The appointments were announced in a statement signed by the party’s State Director of Media and Publicity, Dr. Tony Onyima.

The statement also named Chief Egwuoba Okika Innocent as Deputy State Coordinator, former Speaker of the Anambra State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Ikem Uzoezie, as State Chairman, and Barr. Paulinus Akabogu Izuchukwu as State Campaign Secretary.

Campaign coordinators for the three senatorial districts are Hon. Kingsley Nwafor for Anambra South, Hon. Chuka Ezenwunne for Anambra Central and Hon. Chigbo Enwezor for Anambra North.

All serving federal and state lawmakers elected on the party’s platform are also members of the campaign council.

The council will operate through various directorates covering media and publicity, finance, logistics, women and youth mobilisation, security, grassroots mobilisation, election monitoring and vote protection, new media, protocol, policy research and documentation, and special duties.

Onyima will serve as State Director of Media and Publicity, with Paschal Azubuike as his deputy, while Hon. Lady Azuka Enemuo and Mrs. Chika Ezeali will oversee finance as director and deputy director, respectively.

The council also has coordinators for the 21 local government areas of the state as part of efforts to extend the party’s campaign activities to the grassroots.

The NDC Anambra State Campaign Council is scheduled to be inaugurated on Wednesday, November 4, in Awka.

World.title: Soludo confirms Peter Obi’s wife as child’s godmother
World.content:
Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has confirmed that the wife of former governor Peter Obi is the godmother of one of his children, months after a public disagreement over the relationship between their families.

Soludo also disclosed that his wife, Nonye, is the confirmation godmother of Obi’s daughter, clarifying the family relationship that became a subject of public discussion in September.

The governor made the disclosure in an interview with BBC News Igbo on Monday, describing Obi as a close friend and insisting that their families remained on good terms despite their political differences.

“Peter Obi and I are good friends. Our two families are on good terms. His wife was the godmother of my child at baptism, and my wife was the godmother of his child at confirmation,” he said.

Soludo explained that their differences were political, particularly over their preferences for who should govern Anambra State.

He said he did not hold Obi’s political position against him, despite their disagreement over the state’s leadership.

“I have a different vision of who should be governor of Anambra State. I am contesting, and he supported whoever he felt should be governor. I prevailed by the grace of God, and I don’t hold it against him,” the governor said.

World.title: Odii condemns reprisal killings, offers to pay victims’ bills
World.content:
By Chinedu Adonu

The 2027 Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ebonyi State, Chief Ifeanyi Chukwuma Odii, has condemned reported reprisal killings involving residents of Ebonyi and Anambra states, offering to pay the medical bills of victims and provide food assistance to affected families.

Odii, popularly known as Anyichuks, also appealed to residents of both states, particularly youths and community leaders, to shun retaliatory attacks and allow the law to take its course.

He expressed sadness over the killing of Miss Mmesoma and subsequent reports of the killings of two Ebonyi men, describing attacks on innocent people in the name of revenge as unacceptable.

In a statement issued by his spokesperson, Emma Igwe, the governorship candidate said no community should be made to suffer for the alleged actions of an individual.

“There can never be any justification for taking innocent human lives under the guise of revenge. No community should be made to suffer for the alleged offence of an individual,” he said.

Odii described Anambra and Ebonyi as sister states with longstanding cultural, commercial and family ties, warning against allowing the actions of individuals to undermine their relationship.

He called on the Anambra State Government, led by Governor Chukwuma Soludo, to take urgent security and administrative measures to prevent further violence, protect vulnerable residents and ensure that those responsible were arrested and prosecuted.

He also urged security agencies to intensify surveillance and guarantee the safety of residents irrespective of their state of origin.

As part of his humanitarian intervention, Odii offered to settle hospital bills incurred by victims receiving treatment on both sides of the crisis.

He also pledged to provide bags of rice and other essential food items to affected families and communities to alleviate the hardship caused by the violence.

According to him, the intervention was motivated by compassion and concern for human life, rather than political, ethnic or geographical considerations.

“This gesture is not an endorsement of violence or an attempt to interfere with ongoing investigations. Rather, it is a demonstration that human life and suffering transcend ethnic and state boundaries,” he said.

The businessman further appealed to traditional rulers, religious leaders, community leaders and youth organisations in both states to promote reconciliation and restore confidence among residents.

He urged Ebonyi indigenes living in Anambra and Anambra residents in Ebonyi to remain calm and avoid actions capable of escalating the crisis.

Odii also cautioned media organisations and social media users against circulating unverified reports and inflammatory statements that could trigger further attacks.

“Any political ambition, ethnic sentiment or personal grievance is not worth the blood of an innocent Nigerian.

“Let the law take its course. Let the innocent be protected. Let the wounded receive treatment. Let the hungry be supported. Let peace return to our communities,” he appealed.

He added, “Anambra and Ebonyi are brothers, not enemies.”

World.title: Utomi faults APC over alleged extravagance amid hardship
World.content:
Pat Utomi

Political economist, Prof. Pat Utomi, has criticised the All Progressives Congress (APC) administration over what he described as extravagant lifestyles among public officials amid economic hardship in the country.

Utomi said it was contradictory for government officials to describe Nigeria as poor while allegedly displaying luxury vehicles, including Maybachs, G-Wagons and Rolls-Royces, and travelling in private jets.

He made the remarks in a post on his X account on Tuesday, arguing that the lifestyles of public office holders should reflect the economic realities confronting ordinary Nigerians.

“You cannot stand before the world and declare that Nigeria is poor, then turn around and parade your ministers in million-dollar Maybachs, G-Wagons and Rolls-Royces, while public officials fly around in private jets. Your optics contradict your narrative, your lifestyle contradicts your statistics,” he said.

The former presidential candidate said if Nigeria was indeed poor, government spending and the management of public resources should reflect the country’s economic circumstances.

He argued that members of the executive and legislature should demonstrate fiscal restraint, particularly when citizens were being asked to endure economic difficulties.

According to him, public office should not be treated as a licence for extravagance, adding that government officials had a responsibility to show restraint in the use of public resources.

“The APC needs to understand that public office is not a licence for extravagance. If citizens must endure economic hardship, those entrusted with their taxes must also demonstrate restraint,” Utomi said.

He added that displaying luxury lifestyles while asking Nigerians to endure economic hardship could deepen public resentment and reinforce perceptions that government officials were insensitive to the plight of ordinary citizens.

World.title: Police rescue 11 kidnapped victims, arrest 19 suspects
World.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

The Nigeria Police Force has rescued 11 kidnapped victims, arrested 19 suspects and recovered 91 rustled livestock, including 48 cows and 43 sheep, in security operations conducted across several states in the last 48 hours.

The operations also led to the recovery of firearms, stolen valuables and motorcycles, while several attempted bandit attacks were foiled.

The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, disclosed the operational breakthroughs in a statement on Tuesday, saying the operations were part of sustained efforts to combat kidnapping, terrorism, armed robbery, cultism, cattle rustling and other criminal activities.

He said investigations and follow-up operations were ongoing to apprehend fleeing suspects, rescue more victims and recover stolen property.

In Zamfara State, police tactical operatives, working with local vigilantes, rescued five elderly women abducted by armed bandits while harvesting beans in Dansadau, Maru Local Government Area.

The victims were freed following a gun battle that forced the abductors to flee. However, a 35-year-old farmer was killed during the attack.

In Niger State, a joint security team comprising police, military personnel, Department of State Services operatives, special hunters and vigilantes rescued six farmers abducted at Mahangi village, near Pandogari in Rafi Local Government Area.

The victims were subsequently taken to a police division for documentation and reunion with their families.

In Kebbi State, joint security forces repelled an attack by suspected Lakurawa terrorists on Ribah town in Danko Wasagu Local Government Area on October 30, after the attackers attempted to block Rambo Junction.

The operation followed an earlier attack on Dan-Indo village in Fakai Local Government Area, where nine people were killed, while two vehicles and several motorcycles were set ablaze.

The police said security operatives had been deployed to maintain order and sustain operations against the suspected terrorists.

Also in Zamfara, police and soldiers have launched a coordinated search-and-rescue operation following the abduction of nine persons at Upa, near Kurya Madaro in Kaura Namoda Local Government Area. Bush-combing operations are ongoing in surrounding forests to secure their release and apprehend the perpetrators.

In Kano State, operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Squad arrested five suspects accused of harbouring criminals in connection with the abduction of the APC Chairman of Rogo Local Government Area, Alhaji Abdu Fanka.

Although the principal suspects reportedly escaped, the police recovered 48 cows, 43 sheep and two Bajaj Boxer motorcycles from the location.

In Katsina State, tactical teams foiled an attempted bandit attack on Karofi village in Dutsin-Ma Local Government Area after responding to a distress call. The gunmen reportedly retreated into the bush following an exchange of gunfire. No casualty was recorded.

In Lagos State, police arrested a 28-year-old suspected cultist, Ojo/Ojomu Bolanle, also known as Burna, in connection with an armed robbery at Desa Bus Stop, Ibeju-Lekki, which resulted in the killing of a Point-of-Sale operator, Ibrahim Adewale Moronfade.

Items recovered from the suspect included a locally made pistol, an expended cartridge and charms.

In Benue State, two suspects were arrested over the alleged sexual assault of a 16-year-old girl in Naka, Gwer West Local Government Area.

The police said a medical examination conducted at General Hospital, Naka, confirmed penetration, while efforts were ongoing to apprehend the principal suspect, who was still at large.

In the Federal Capital Territory, two suspects, Mensur Abdullahi, 20, and Gambo Salisu, 30, were arrested following a violent clash in Gwagwalada over a stolen Tecno phone.

A 19-year-old passer-by, Zaharadenu Awalu, who sustained a deep cut on his left hand during the incident, was treated at the University of Abuja Teaching Hospital. The police said other suspects were being trailed.

In Anambra State, two persons were arrested over the death of a man allegedly tortured and detained overnight by vigilante members at Odorober, Odekpe, over an allegation of stealing a vehicle battery.

In Oyo State, police arrested a 30-year-old suspected cattle rustler, Yali Isiya, following a gun duel between a police-vigilante patrol team and a four-man gang along the Maya-Adekola village axis in Lanlate.

A vigilante member sustained injuries during the encounter and was taken to hospital, while other members of the gang escaped.

In a separate incident in Ogbomoso, three students were arrested following an alleged invasion of Methodist Grammar School by students armed with cutlasses, knives and stones.

One student was injured, while solar panels and classroom roofing materials valued at about N500,000 were reportedly damaged. Police recovered two cutlasses, a catapult and stones.

In Ogun State, two suspected burglars, Bidemi Akinola, 23, and Qudus Adebayo, 22, were arrested over a burglary at Igbehinadun Street.

The suspects allegedly confessed to stealing property valued at N4.085 million, including a 55-inch television, air conditioners, generators and electrical wires. Tools and stolen cables were also recovered.

Meanwhile, in the FCT, police patrol teams responded to an attack by suspected cattle rustlers on a Fulani settlement in Phase 5, Kurudu, on October 30.

Four persons sustained gunshot injuries and were taken to Nyanya General Hospital. Three were treated and discharged, while the fourth victim died.

The Force reiterated its commitment to intelligence-driven operations and collaboration with other security agencies and local communities to curb criminal activities and improve public safety nationwide.

World.title: Nigerians in Northern England Call for Regular Passport Services
World.content:
Sunday Okobi



The Nigerian Community in Greater Manchester (NCGM) has called on the Nigerian government to establish regular passport and consular services in Northern England following the remarkable response to a recent passport intervention exercise in Manchester, United Kingdom.

According to a statement, the appeal was made by NCGM Chairman, Otunba Abayomi Bashiru-Kaka, at the organisation’s celebration of Nigeria’s 66th Independence anniversary, held in Manchester last month.

In the statement signed by its Public Relations Officer, Joy Adetona, and made available to THISDAY yesterday, NCGM described the intervention as a welcome development that had eased the difficulties faced by Nigerians accessing passport services outside London.

The event attracted community members, civic leaders, representatives of Nigerian institutions and other distinguished guests.

In the statement, Bashiru-Kaka commended the Nigerian High Commission in London, the Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS), and the federal government for improving services for Nigerians in the Diaspora.

He particularly acknowledged the Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo; the Comptroller-General of the NIS, Mrs. Kemi Nanna Nandap, and the officers involved in the exercise.

The intervention covered four UK locations: Manchester, London, Cardiff and Aberdeen, with the initial phase commencing in Manchester and London.

Addressing the challenges faced by Nigerians outside London, according to the statement, Bashiru-Kaka noted that Manchester recorded 1,709 passport enrolments within the first six operational days, compared with London’s 587, according to NIS figures released on September 14, 2026.

He observed that Nigerians in Greater Manchester, Liverpool, Leeds, Sheffield, Bradford, Newcastle and surrounding communities often face significant costs and inconvenience travelling to London for passport services, particularly families, elderly residents, students, and working professionals.

Consequently, he urged the Nigerian High Commission, the NIS and other relevant authorities to establish a more regular and sustainable passport and consular service arrangement in Northern England, with Manchester as a suitable regional base.

He cited Manchester’s accessibility, established Nigerian community networks, and demonstrated demand as reasons for considering the arrangement, while emphasising the need for timely announcements and clear application guidelines.

Beyond consular services, Bashiru-Kaka highlighted Nigerians’ contributions to their homeland through family support, investment, professional expertise and community development. He noted that improved access to essential government services would further strengthen ties between Nigeria and its citizens abroad.

He reaffirmed NCGM’s commitment to working with the Nigerian High Commission, the NIS, mayors, councillors, public institutions and community organisations across Greater Manchester to advance the welfare of Nigerians.

He also encouraged Nigerians to remain proud of their heritage while contributing positively to British society.

NCGM appreciated the Nigerian authorities and personnel involved in the intervention, pledging continued cooperation with relevant stakeholders to improve communication, coordination and awareness of available services.

The organisation expressed hope that the Manchester exercise would provide a foundation for more accessible and sustainable passport and consular services for Nigerians across Northern England.

World.title: Bandits Ambush, Kill 5 Policemen on Sokoto–Gusau Road, Abduct Others
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto



Suspected bandits yesterday ambushed police officers on the Sokoto–Gusau road, killing five police officers and abducting others.

The attack occurred yesterday when the officers were travelling on a Zamfara State mass transit bus, popularly known as Bazamfara, en route to Gusau, the state capital.

A source at the scene disclosed that some of the police officers aboard the bus lost their lives during the ambush.

However, the exact number of casualties could not be ascertained as of the time of filing this report.

Sources within the police force indicated that the officers were on their way to provide security for the ongoing All Progressives Congress (APC) primary election for the Zamfara North senatorial district in Kaura Namoda Local Government Area of the state.

The sources further disclosed that in addition to those reportedly killed during the ambush, some of the officers were abducted by the bandits.

The circumstances surrounding the attack and the identities of the victims remain unclear.

When contacted, the Zamfara State Police Command’s Public Relations Officer said the Command was not authorised to comment on the matter, as it falls under the jurisdiction of the Zonal Command.

The Zone 10 PPRO, Abdullahi Ambursa, who confirmed the incident, however, said he was currently in the hospital and would not be able to comment further, but promised to issue an official statement later.

The attack has heightened tension in Zamfara, coming at a time when political activities and security operations are ongoing across the state.

Security agencies are yet to issue an official casualty figure, while residents have called for increased patrols on the Sokoto–Gusau highway.

World.title: Onafowokan Urges Entrepreneurs,  Professionals to Develop Clear Long-Term Visions
World.content:
Kayode Tokede

The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Coleman Technical Industries Limited, George Onafowokan, has advised entrepreneurs and professionals to develop clear long-term visions, remain focused and uphold strong ethical standards, warning against the pursuit of quick money and shortcuts to success.

He maintained that vision helps individuals identify what they want to build, the problems they intend to solve and the lasting value they hope to create.

Onafowokan, who was delivering his keynote address at the first international conference of the Pan-Atlantic University (PAU) Alumni Association 2026 international conference held recently at the Ecobank Pan African Centre in Lagos, urged Nigerian youths to embrace mentorship, integrity, discipline and patience as essential ingredients for building successful businesses and careers.

He said success should not be measured only by an individual’s personal achievements but also by the number of people empowered to succeed through their knowledge and experience.

According to him, business leaders should be willing to share what they have learnt rather than withhold knowledge for fear that those they mentor might eventually become more successful than them.

Onafowokan said: “Success should be seen not by what you have built as an individual, but how many people around you have actually become successful through what you have shared and expressed with them.”

He said the reluctance of some successful Nigerians to share their experiences was a setback to business development and the growth of future leaders.

He said mentorship had helped people develop their abilities, build wealth and take on greater responsibilities, adding that experienced business leaders should support others in achieving similar progress.

The special guest of honour, Mrs. Olajumoke Cecilia Ajayi, who is the Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, West African Exploration and Production (WAEP) Company, offered practical guidance on family and personal development.

She advised parents to counsel their children while allowing them the freedom to express themselves, emphasising that competence must be paired with confidence.

She also urged young people to discuss their ambitions openly with their partners before entering marriage.

Earlier, the Vice- Chancellor of Pan-Atlantic University, Professor Enase Okonedo, said the university’s approximately 15,000 alumni from its business school and university had the capacity to make a significant contribution to society if they worked together.

She said the university’s emphasis on knowledge, values and responsible leadership was aimed at producing graduates who could contribute to national development.

According to her, the university has grown from its beginnings in a living room in Victoria Island 34 years ago to operating across two campuses, while its alumni have spread across different industries and professions.

She said: “Think about 15,000 well-formed people who can make a difference in Nigeria. Our focus is on the transformation of society. But we cannot do it alone.”

Okonedo urged the graduates to act as ambassadors of the institution by demonstrating integrity, responsibility and leadership in their workplaces and communities.

She said the conference theme, ‘The Advantage: Connecting People, Ideas and Opportunities’, highlighted the potential of alumni to develop new businesses, partnerships and approaches to solving societal problems.

The vice-chancellor added that such opportunities would only be realised if alumni engaged with one another, shared experiences and turned conversations into practical collaborations.

The President of the Pan-Atlantic University Alumni Association, Dr Onyebuchi Odianjo, said the association was working to build a more connected and active alumni community that could provide professional support, strengthen industry relationships and create opportunities for students and graduates.
