She said the conference grew out of discussions about how the university’s alumni network could be used to connect people, ideas and industries, turning relationships into partnerships and ideas into opportunities.

Odianjo said the association had continued to promote alumni engagement, student support, professional networking and community impact, adding that its ambition was to translate the strength of the network into tangible benefits.

She said her own experience at the university had provided practical knowledge and opportunities that helped her career, reinforcing her commitment to giving back to the institution.

World.title: FinTribe Finance Fair 2026: NGX Group Advances Women’s Financial Empowerment, Investor Protection
World.content:
Nigerian Exchange Group Plc (NGX Group), through its regulatory subsidiary, NGX Regulation Limited (NGX RegCo), has reaffirmed its commitment to advancing women’s financial empowerment, investor education and protection against investment fraud at the 2026 FinTribe Finance Fair, which attracted over 10,000 participants across Lagos and regional viewing centres.

The fourth edition of the Fair, themed ‘I Can’, brought together women, entrepreneurs, financial experts and business leaders to explore investment opportunities, entrepreneurship and long-term financial independence. The event also reached participants through viewing centres in Abuja, Port Harcourt, Enugu and Akwa Ibom State.

Through its EquipHER initiative, NGX RegCo engaged participants on practical approaches to wealth creation, responsible investing and fraud prevention, reinforcing the importance of financial knowledge in building lasting economic independence.

The engagement also aligned with the objectives of the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) World Investor Week 2026, particularly its focus on investor resilience, digital deception and fraud awareness.

Speaking during a session titled ‘The Smart Investor: Grow Your Wealth, Guard Your Money,’ Chief Executive Officer, NGX RegCo, Olufemi Shobanjo, emphasised that financial empowerment requires more than earning an income or accumulating savings.

“Financial empowerment must go beyond earning and saving money. Women need the knowledge, confidence and opportunities to acquire assets, invest responsibly and build lasting economic independence,” he said.

Shobanjo highlighted investment opportunities across equities, bonds, exchange-traded funds and mutual funds, while cautioning participants against unrealistic returns, unlicensed investment operators and financial decisions influenced by social media hype.

He urged participants to adopt three essential principles for protecting their investments: “Research before you invest. Verify before you transact. Report when you suspect fraud.”

The session featured an interactive financial literacy quiz designed to reinforce participants’ understanding of investment principles and investor protection. The four highest-scoring participants received gifts in recognition of their performance.

Beyond the main session, the EquipHER Booth provided opportunities to engage directly with participants exploring capital market investment options and gain practical insights into identifying investment risks and avoiding fraudulent schemes.

The engagements also highlighted the importance of regulatory oversight and market surveillance in maintaining investor confidence.

Founder of FinTribe, Jennifer Awirigwe, commended the continued collaboration with NGX RegCo and its contribution to strengthening women’s financial literacy.

“We value NGX Regulation’s continued partnership with FinTribe through EquipHER. Every year, this collaboration helps more women understand not only how to grow their money, but also how to protect it. That combination of opportunity, knowledge and investor confidence is central to the financial independence we want women to achieve,” she said.

The Fair also featured prominent personalities, including filmmakers and entrepreneurs such as Funke Akindele and Omoni Oboli, actress Bamike Olawunmi (BamBam) and financial literacy advocate, Sola Adesakin, who shared insights on financial discipline, entrepreneurship, business growth and translating financial knowledge into action.

Through EquipHER and its ongoing investor education and protection initiatives, NGX RegCo continues to strengthen financial literacy, promote responsible investment practices and reinforce market integrity, contributing to NGX Group’s broader ambition of expanding inclusive participation in Nigeria’s capital market.

World.title: 2027: Accord Party Files Objection to Suit Seeking its Candidates’ Disqualification
World.content:
Alex Enumah in Abuja

The Accord Party has asked a Federal High Court, Abuja to dismiss the suit seeking the disqualification of all its candidates in the 2027 general election.

The party, in a preliminary objection, argued that the suit has become statute barred, having been filed outside the 14 days prescribed by law.

The suit marked: FHC/ABJ/CV/2524/2026, was filed by the party’s National Secretary, Adebukola Ajaja.

However, the party, in its objection filed through its lawyer, Musibau Adetunbi (SAN), is also querying the jurisdiction of the court to entertain the suit on the grounds that it relates to the issue of candidates’ nomination, which falls within the internal affairs of a political party.

Besides, the party is also challenging the plaintiff’s locus standi to file the suit for not being an aspirant in the primary election conducted on May 29, and that the proper parties were not included.

It argued that while the plaintiff wants the court to nullify the nomination of its candidates, none of the candidates to be affected by the outcome of the suit were made parties to afford them the opportunity of being heard.

The party also faulted the competence of the suit on the grounds that it is allegedly premature because the plaintiff failed to give it the required 21 days pre-action notice.

Accord, listed as the second defendant, argued that its primary was conducted in accordance with all relevant laws and guidelines, adding that the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has since recognised its outcome and the list of candidates duly submitted to the electoral umpire in the prescribed format.

It further argued that, as against the plaintiff’s contention, the National Chairman and the National Organising Secretary could validly sign and submit candidates’ lists and forms to INEC where the National Secretary is unavailable in line with Article 18 of the party’s constitution and Regulations 25(3), 28(2) of INEC’s Guidelines.

Accord Party added:”INEC Regulations and Guidelines for Political Parties did not in any way specify that the plaintiff herein must sign the forwarding letter, neither did the constitution of the second defendant require her (the plaintiff) to sign.

“The National Executives of the party expressly authorized the fourth defendant to co-sign with the 3rd defendant. No wrong has been done.”

Relying on the Supreme Court’s decision in the case of Jegede v. INEC, Accord Party argued that even if it was only its national chairman that signed, “the plaintiffs case is still bound to fail because the signature of the national chairman suffices on the authority of Jegede v. INEC.”

Accord Party’s National Chairman, Maxwell Mgbudem, stated in a counter-affidavit, that contrary to the plaintiff’s claim that her responsibilities were usurped by the National Organising Secretary, she actually abandoned her duties.

World.title: INEC and Controversies Around Candidates’ Clearance for 2027 Polls
World.content:
The dream of some candidates to participate in the 2027 governorship and state Houses of Assembly elections may be gradually slipping away following their inability to make the final list of candidates released by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and even with the subsequent review of cases of affected candidates. Adedayo Akinwale reports.

With less than 100 days to the February 6, 2027 governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections, the controversies and uncertainty concerning the participation of some candidates in the elections continued following the refusal of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to clear some candidates to contest the elections.

On September 24, 2026, a Supreme Court judgement restored Sections 77(5), (6), (7) and 84(2) of the Electoral Act 2026. The provisions bar parties from fielding candidates whose names were not in the membership register submitted to INEC within the stipulated time.

In a unanimous judgement, a seven-member panel of the apex court allowed the appeal filed by the INEC and set aside the July 16 judgement of the Court of Appeal which had voided the provisions.

The apex court held that the provisions are not inconsistent with the 1999 Constitution, thereby restoring the May 5 decision of the Federal High Court, Abuja, which had dismissed the challenge brought by the Zenith Labour Party (ZLP) in suit FHC/ABJ/509/2026. It also awarded N2 million costs against ZLP.

Section 77(5) of the Electoral Act provides that only persons whose names appear in a party’s membership register submitted to INEC not later than 21 days before a primary, congress or convention are eligible to participate in that exercise.

Also, Section 77(6) requires political parties to use the membership register submitted to INEC for their primaries, congresses and conventions; while Section 77(7) provides that a party that fails to submit its membership register within the stipulated period shall not be eligible to field a candidate for an election.

While Section 84(2) provides that political parties shall nominate candidates through direct primaries or consensus.

Though, the electoral body clarified that the judgement does not automatically disqualify individual candidates, but relates to the eligibility of political parties to participate where they fail to comply with statutory requirements on membership registers.

However, on October 10, 2026, the electoral body dropped the names of some governorship, as well as State Houses of Assembly candidates when it released the final list of candidates for the 2027 governorship election 2027 in line with the Supreme Court ruling.

Notable names that were dropped from the list by INEC included the former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Prof. Isa Pantami and Ladi Adebutu, both of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

Pantami emerged as the candidate of PDP after quitting the All Progressives Congress (APC) on May 19. But one of the aspirants who sought the PDP ticket, Ahmed Mailantarki challenged Pantami’s victory in court.

A Federal High Court sitting in Gombe nullified the election and ordered a fresh primary, which Pantami won again.

In the case of Adebutu, he was the governorship candidate of the PDP in Ogun State. Also, the governorship candidate of the New Nigerian Peoples Party (NNPP) in Oyo state, Adebiyi Adedapo was also dropped from the INEC’s list.

On October 29, INEC announced that it had reinstated 66 governorship and state Houses of Assembly candidates after the review of the final list for the 2027 general election.

INEC National Commission and Chairman of Information and Voter Education Committee (IVEC), Mohammed Haruna, in a statement issued last Thursday said the commission received complaints bordering on omission of political parties, wrongful inclusion of candidates whose names were not in the membership registers submitted by their parties, and alleged multiple nominations.

He explained that after reviewing the complaints in line with relevant records and legal provisions, it found merit in some petitions and approved the inclusion of the affected candidates and parties, while others were declined for lacking merit.

Haruna confirmed that some names wrongfully published in the final list have been removed after verification showed they were not on their party registers, while other candidates were removed for non-compliance with legal requirements for nomination.

Giving a breakdown, he revealed that a total of 69 petitions were received from 12 political parties across 26 states in respect of the Governorship election, out of which 41 succeeded and 28 failed.

The National Commissioner noted that for the State Houses of Assembly, 61 petitions were received from 11 political parties across 11 states, with 25 succeeding and 36 failing.

He stated: “Following a review of the complaints, relevant records and applicable legal provisions, the Commission found merit in some representations and approved the inclusion of affected candidates and their political parties, while complaints found to be without merit were declined.”

The commission assured that the affected candidates, political parties and states would be reflected in the updated list on the Commission’s website.

While INEC did not give names of the candidates reinstated in its statement, there were indications that Pantami eventually scaled the hurdle, while Adebutu’s fate remains unknown.

In the case of NNPP’s Adebiyi, he was sold out by the Chairman and Secretary of the party who allegedly wrote a letter withdrawing from the race and having him replaced by another candidate.

Adebiyi told THISDAY that his signature was allegedly forged, an affidavit written in his name without his consent.

The development surrounding the candidates that are yet to be cleared by the electoral umpire has prevented some candidates from campaigning or scheduling their electoral activities despite the election coming up in less than 100 days.

This has put the ambition of some of the candidates in jeopardy. With the recent review of the final list of candidates, the political ambition of some of the candidates as far as 2927 general election is concerned is all but over.

World.title: 115 Support Groups Back Mutfwang As APC Begins 2027 Campaign
World.content:
Plateau State Governor Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang has formally launched the APC’s 2027 campaign machinery, expressing confidence that his administration’s achievements and ongoing development programmes will secure renewed mandates for President Bola Tinubu and APC candidates across the state.

Inaugurating the campaign council on Monday, November 2, 2026, at Government House, Rayfield, Jos, Mutfwang charged members to pursue a disciplined, peaceful and issue-based campaign anchored on performance, grassroots mobilisation and the collective development of Plateau State.

The campaign will seek the re-election of President Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima, Governor Mutfwang and Deputy Governor Ngo Josephine Piyo, alongside APC candidates for the National and State Assemblies.

Mutfwang expressed appreciation to Plateau residents for their support, acknowledging the challenges confronting the state while insisting that his administration had recorded progress that deserved consolidation.

He described governance as a continuous process requiring consistency, saying no administration could complete every development project within a single term.

“There is no government that ends everything. Every government is a relay. Our duty is not to make others look bad; it is to see how we can collectively make Plateau State look better,” he said.

On security, the Governor acknowledged the challenges facing the state but disclosed fresh measures to strengthen protection in vulnerable communities. These include plans to deploy at least 800 trained forest guards and commission another batch of retrained Operation Rainbow personnel.

He also revealed that efforts were underway to facilitate the safe return of internally displaced persons to their ancestral communities, reaffirming his administration’s commitment to restoring peace.

Defending the economic reforms of the Tinubu administration, Mutfwang urged Nigerians to consider the difficult fiscal and structural conditions inherited by the Federal Government in 2023. He cited improvements in foreign reserves and fuel availability as signs of progress.



The Governor also highlighted interventions by his administration to cushion economic hardship in Plateau, including the Tin City Metro buses, revival of metropolitan rail services, a 50 per cent reduction in tuition fees in state-owned tertiary institutions and a 300 per cent increase in student allowances.

He further acknowledged the benefits of federal student loan and scholarship programmes for Plateau indigenes pursuing higher education.

On party organisation, Mutfwang urged APC stakeholders to put aside internal differences and concentrate on building a formidable grassroots structure, stressing that electoral victories were secured at polling units rather than political gatherings in Jos.

The Director-General of the Mutfwang/Piyo 2027 Governorship Campaign Council, Sir Joseph Ari, pledged a disciplined and coordinated campaign, disclosing that 115 support groups had already expressed interest in the political project.

He also cited expressions of solidarity from traditional rulers, religious leaders, women, youths and other organised groups, describing inclusive mobilisation and peaceful coexistence as essential to the campaign’s success.

Ari commended the Governor’s “Time Is Now” policy direction, promising that the campaign would focus on verifiable achievements, constructive engagement and development priorities.

Plateau APC Chairman Rufus Bature described the inauguration as an important step towards building a coordinated campaign structure, urging members to demonstrate commitment, loyalty and accountability across their respective constituencies.

The campaign council also called on party supporters and residents to turn out for the scheduled November 14 visit of President Tinubu, Vice President Shettima, APC National Chairman Professor Nentawe Yilwatda and other party leaders.

With security, education, transportation and economic welfare featuring prominently in its message, the APC campaign leadership says it intends to make continuity and consolidation the central arguments for its 2027 electoral bid.

World.title: In Makkah, Tinubu Puts His Re-election in Allah’s Hands
World.content:
• Prays for wisdom, strength

•Recommits to building a prosperous nation, says Nigeria will overcome challenges

Deji Elumoye, Chuks Okocha in Abuja and Benjamin Nworie in Abakaliki





In supplication and total submission to the Almighty, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, yesterday, at the Holy Ka’abah, Mecca, where he had gone to observe Umrah, the lesser hajj, handed his re-election challenges to Allah, in whom he trusted.

With a tinge of drama, Tinubu, who held and kissed the Al-Hajar al-Aswad otherwise called the Black Stone, in a symbolic sunnah, often performed in emulation of the Prophet Mohammad, however, prayed for wisdom and strength.

The Black Stone is one of the most sacred objects in Islam, embedded in the southeastern corner of the Holy Ka’abah in Makkah, Saudi Arabia, surrounded by a silver frame.

Muslims hold it in great reverence because Islamic tradition teaches that it came from paradise and that Prophet Mohammad kissed it. It is therefore an expression of faith and reverence, not an act of worshipping the stone.

The president, who concluded his five-day visit to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, reflected on his spiritual journey to the Holy land, during which the Custodian of the Holy Mosques of Makkah and Madinah, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, granted him a rare privilege of leading Nigeria’s delegation to pray inside the Holy Ka’abah.

At the Holy Ka’abah, Tinubu offered prayers of gratitude to the Almighty Allah for the privilege of serving as Nigeria’s President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces.

Sheikh Dahlulah Muthawal of Masjid al-Haram led the president into the Ka’abah.

Tinubu thanked the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, for granting him and members of his delegation the opportunity to enter the Holy Ka’abah in Makkah and offer prayers to Almighty Allah.

The president described the honour as a historic and deeply cherished spiritual experience, reflecting the longstanding bonds of friendship, mutual respect and cooperation between Nigeria and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

“I want to say a big thank you for the faith, for the recognition. I can’t believe the fencing of the Ka’abah is in Green-White-Green, which reminds us of the Nigerian identity.

“I thank the Crown Prince and all the administrators of the holy land. I thank them for the hospitality and recognition given to me as the leader of the delegation and the country.

“We are all facing challenges and hostility around us. We will overcome them with faith in God Almighty. I’m grateful forever. I thank the King and the royal Crown Prince.

“It is an honour that I enjoyed, and it is gracious of them to have allowed me to enter inside the Ka’abah. This is history.”

Tinubu said he asked Allah for wisdom and resilience to continue serving Nigerians, and expressed confidence that his prayers have been answered.

According to him, “I asked for wisdom and resilience to continue to serve the people. I know that prayer has been granted. Before the 2023 election, I did the same thing. I asked Allah to bless my Umrah then, and He did. And I promised that I would come back to thank Him.”

He reflected on the message from the Holy Qur’an in Surah Aal-Imran, Verse 26, which affirmed that Almighty Allah is the Owner of all sovereignty, granting power and authority to whom He wills and taking them away from whom He wills.

The president said power is a trust that must be exercised responsibly, with humility and in the service of the people, recognising that no position of authority is permanent and that ultimate sovereignty belongs to Almighty Allah.

“There is no other God but Almighty Allah. He is the giver and the taker. He owns power and authority. He says, ‘If I give you, use it well. If you don’t use it in accordance with my dictates, I can take it from you and give it to another person. I am the only One who has that authority,” the president said, quoting the Qur’an.

Tinubu said faith in Allah had strengthened his conviction that his emergence as Nigeria’s leader was an extraordinary blessing that must be matched with dedicated service to the country.

“I have faith in that, and I believe extremely well that He has done me and my country a great favour. Out of many millions of people, to be the President and Commander-in-Chief is a favour that only Almighty God can do to a human being,” he stated.

Tinubu reiterated his commitment to Project Nigeria and his determination to build a prosperous nation, invest in the future of young Nigerians, and pursue development in line with the will of Almighty Allah and the people’s aspirations.

He emphasised that his commitment to Project Nigeria had become even stronger, assuring Nigerians of his resolve to pursue policies and programmes that would promote prosperity, national development and shared progress.

“My commitment to Project Nigeria is higher. I am determined to usher in prosperity and fully develop the country, consistent with the wish of Allah and the support of the people.

“It is important to put Allah first, then move on. Follow your conscience. Follow the right path that will lead Nigeria to that greatness,” Tinubu said.

On the nation’s economic outlook, the president expressed optimism about the progress made under his watch, describing the economic foundation as solid and the country’s emergence from a difficult period as encouraging.

“The foundation is solid, and the economy has come out of the dark tunnel. This is inspiring.”

He maintained, however, that nation-building required sustained investment in young Nigerians’ future, noting that today’s leaders’ decisions would determine how future generations remember them.

“We need to build a future for our youth. If we don’t invest in their future, how do we want to be remembered as leaders 50 years from now? That’s the main thing. So this is a rare privilege to lead the country,” he added.

Tinubu reiterated that his administration would remain focused on strengthening the country’s economic foundations, expanding opportunities for young people and creating the conditions necessary for Nigerians to realise their potential.

The president thanked Almighty Allah for the opportunity to lead Nigeria and reaffirmed his determination to justify the confidence the Nigerian people have placed in him through purposeful leadership and an enduring commitment to national progress.

Earlier, the President, had disclosed on X @OfficialPBAT, that he had concluded his visit to Saudi, adding that he used the opportunity of the visit to pray for peace, unity and prosperity to reign supreme in Nigeria.

Tinubu, according to the four-paragraph post, stated: “I have concluded my visit to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, where, together with members of my delegation, I had the rare honour of entering the Holy Kaaba to pray, and of performing Umrah.

“I am deeply grateful to the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud @KingSalman, and to Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman for extending this privilege to us, and for their gracious hospitality and brotherly care.

“It reflects the enduring bonds of faith and friendship between Nigeria and Saudi Arabia. In those sacred moments, I prayed for peace, unity and prosperity for our dear nation and for all Nigerians.”

Seized by emotions, Minister of Justice Lateef Fagbemi, his Health and Social Welfare counterpart, Prof Ali Pate, Governors of Borno, Sokoto, Jigawa, Kaduna, Yobe and Kwara States as well as captains of industry, including Chairman of BUA, Abdulsamad Rabiu and CEO of Oando, Wale Tinubu, expressed gratitude to Allah and the president for allowing them to enter and pray with him in the most holy mosque and sacred ground in Islam.

Makinde-Daura Campaigns Berates Tinubu over False Economy Claims in Mecca, Saudi

The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organization (MDPCO) has berated President Bola Tinubu for allegedly falsely claiming in Mecca that Nigeria’s economy has “come out of the dark tunnel” when in reality the economy was worsening by the day.

The Makinde/Daura presidential campaigns said it was profane that President Tinubu could stand before the Holy Ka’abah in Makkah to make such a spurious claim despite the damming indices showing that the nation was sinking deeper into poverty under him with over 140 million citizens (63% of the population) living in abject poverty.

In a statement, the Director of Strategic Communication of the Makinde/Daura presidential campaign, Richard Ihediuwa, said, ‘’While President Tinubu made his false claims in Mecca, hundreds of businesses are closing on daily basis in Nigeria due to the adverse effect of his punishing economic policies and harsh taxes.

“This is just as mass unemployment has become a new normal with over 60 million Nigerians facing acute food insecurity and going to bed on empty stomach with no hope in sight under the Tinubu administration.’’

The Director of Strategic Communication of the campaign, further said, ‘’Under President Tinubu’s rule, insecurity continues to fester to the extent that citizens can no longer freely move around the nation to ply their trades, go to their farms and engage in other commercial activities, an ugly situation with attendant negative implication on the economy.

‘’Despite being an oil producing country, fuel price in Nigeria remains unaffordable at N1,500 to N2,000 per liter in various parts of the country, driving high costs of living, harsh business environment and eroded purchasing power of citizens.

‘’Today, under President Tinubu’s voodoo economy Nigeria’s infrastructure deficit has hit an estimated $2.3 trillion, with experts stating that the gap would require approximately $100 billion annually over the next 30 years to fix.

‘’It is ironic that President Tinubu claims that the economy has come out of the dark tunnel when he is mortgaging the future of the nation with reckless borrowing from foreign creditors with no verifiable investments in projects or programmes and no clear-cut plan to repay the N166.7 trillion debt accumulated under his watch,’’ the campaign council said.

The APM presidential campaign said Nigerians expected President Tinubu to use the sacred precincts of the Holy Ka’abah, to seek genuine contrition before the Almighty Allah, shed the trappings of presidential power and confront the damning record of his administration against the crushing hardship and widespread misery its policies have inflicted on nation.

‘’The fact that President Tinubu can, in the face of the current economic quagmire, claim that the nation economy has come out of the dark tunnel, only goes to confirm that he has come to his wits end and has nothing more to offer as president.

‘’His affirmation in the Holy Land that the Almighty Allah gives power and can take from him to whom He wills, comes to Nigerians as an answered prayer given their earnest desire and supplication for a breath of fresh air under a new leadership,’’ the statement said.

2027: S’East CAN, Others Endorse Tinubu

The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), South East zone as well as the Hausa and Yoruba communities in Ebonyi State, have endorsed President Tinubu for re-election in the 2027 elections.

The different bodies made the endorsement yesterday in Abakaliki during a Town Hall meeting powered by the Directorate of Infrastructure, Mobilisation and Sensitisation of All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council (PCC).

Addressing members of the association, the President of the Christian Fellowship of Nigeria (CFN), South East zone, Rev. Fr. Abraham Nwali, appreciated the president for uplifting the zone through massive infrastructure.

He urged the members of the association and the entire people of the zone to support Tinubu’s re-election as mark of appreciation for his love for the region.

“We are owing our leader the president and Minister of Works, His Excellency, Senator David Umahi, appreciation, and the only way we can show the appreciation is to support the president in the 2027 general election,” Nwali stated.

A former President of the Women Wing of the association, Mrs. Uche Charity Ujunwa, said Tinubu has brought reforms to the country which was impacting positively on the people and called for support of the President in the 2027 general election.

Leader of the Youth Wing of CAN South East, Peter Onyeabor, assured the president that the entire Christian youths in the zone would deliver the president in the general election.

On their parts, Kazeem Bankole, leader of Yoruba community in Ebonyi and Alhaji Danjuma Gambo, leader of Hausa community in the state, declared that they would mobilise the communities to deliver Tinubu and all the APC candidates in the general election.

World.title: ‘Either I win, or none of us do’: Hamilton unhappy with Leclerc after costly first-lap battle
World.content:
Lewis Hamilton has taken a swipe at Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc following a dramatic Mexican Grand Prix, questioning the Monegasque’s mentality after their first-lap battle.

Hamilton, who secured his first pole position in Ferrari colours, looked set for a strong result after making a good start; however, Leclerc launched an aggressive move into Turn 4, forcing Hamilton down to third place.

Leclerc braked late and failed to make the corner, taking to the run-off area in the process. Hamilton subsequently lost another position to Max Verstappen.



Although Leclerc took the lead, his manoeuvre was deemed illegal and he was handed a five-second penalty. The sanction proved costly as Verstappen moved ahead after the first pit stops.

Leclerc eventually finished fourth, while Hamilton recovered to claim second place after overtaking his teammate during the second restart.

Following the race, several fans and pundits felt Ferrari could have secured a comfortable one-two finish had Leclerc avoided such an aggressive battle with Hamilton on the opening lap.

Hamilton was particularly critical of his teammate, suggesting that Leclerc’s approach to racing alongside him was unnecessary.

“The guy is 28 years old, so I don’t think it’s an age thing. I think it’s a mentality thing. It’s like do or die. Like, either I win, or none of us do, and it shouldn’t be that. It should be us having got that one-two, which is still a good feeling,” Hamilton said.

Hamilton not happy with Leclerc’s turn 4 move

The seven-time world champion also brought up Leclerc’s previous battles with former Ferrari teammate Carlos Sainz, suggesting that the Monegasque had a history of getting involved in unnecessary fights that compromised the team’s results.



“Before I joined this team, when I was in Mercedes, I watched and witnessed the back-and-forth between Charles and Carlos. Several races where they were battling so much that the person ahead just pulled away, and they had the pace to actually win the race,” he added.

Hamilton and Leclerc clashed in Monza and Mexico

Hamilton then pointed to his own approach during their battle at Silverstone, insisting he could have been more aggressive but chose not to compromise Ferrari’s result.

“At Silverstone, I could have gone all kamikaze on him and taken him off and lost us the win, but instead a one-two was there, and I think we got a one-two, or was it a one-three? I’m happy for the team to have experienced that. I’m hopeful we’ll work towards a better place in the future.”

Hamilton’s comments suggest that the relationship between Ferrari’s two drivers could become an interesting storyline as the team looks to strengthen its position.

With Hamilton fighting for wins again this season, Leclerc has been second best for most of the campaign.

Did Leclerc deny Lewis the win?

World.title: Shock as top Betway Premiership coach resigns
World.content:
Polokwane City head coach Willy Moloto has resigned just a day after returning to training following a lengthy absence due to health complications. Image: Polokwane City

Polokwane City head coach Willy Moloto has resigned just a day after returning to training following a lengthy absence due to health complications.

The 2026/27 Betway Premiership campaign has taken another unexpected turn for Rise and Shine, with the Limpopo club now searching for a new coach after just nine league matches.

READ | Hlungwani identifies major refereeing errors in Orlando Pirates’ win over Kaizer Chiefs



Moloto’s resignation was confirmed to players on Tuesday morning ahead of their training session.

The highly rated tactician took charge at the beginning of the season following the departure of Phuti Mohafe, who left to join Marumo Gallants.

Moloto’s health scare and sudden resignation

Moloto had been sidelined since September after suffering a health scare during Polokwane City’s Betway Premiership clash against AmaZulu FC at Old Peter Mokaba Stadium on 19 September.



Rise and Shine lost the match 1-0.

During the game, a member of the club’s technical team assisted Moloto to the dressing room while play continued.

He reportedly collapsed shortly afterwards and was rushed to a private hospital in Polokwane, where he spent a week receiving treatment.



The former University of Pretoria coach subsequently remained away from his duties while recovering, missing the club’s last three matches across the Betway Premiership and Carling Knockout Cup.

In a surprising turn of events, Moloto returned to training on Monday, 2 November, for the first time since his hospitalisation.

However, he tendered his resignation the following day.



Moloto was absent from Tuesday’s training session at Polokwane Rugby Club, the team’s training base.

He has also reportedly bid farewell to some of the players, bringing his latest spell at Rise and Shine to an abrupt end.

Moloto’s short spell at Rise and Shine

Polokwane City have managed just one victory under Moloto, alongside five draws and three defeats.



The club have collected eight points from their opening nine league matches and currently sit in 11th position on the table.

His resignation marks his second departure from Rise and Shine, having previously resigned alongside co-coach Innocent Mayoyo during the 2021/22 season when the club was competing in the National First Division.

Moloto subsequently worked alongside Kwanele Kopo at Pretoria Callies, having previously served with him at the University of Pretoria.



He also had a stint with Ghanaian side Real Academicals in 2024.

Who will take over at Polokwane City?

During Moloto’s absence, Mkhuseli Sentane took charge of three matches, assisted by Mpho Ndlovu.

The interim technical team suffered two defeats to Siwelele FC in the Betway Premiership and Carling Knockout Cup, while drawing 0-0 with TS Galaxy.



Polokwane City are next scheduled to face Durban City in a league encounter on 24 November.

The FIFA international break gives the club time to assess its coaching options and identify a replacement for Moloto.

Former coach Phuti Mohafe has also been linked with a return after being spotted in the VIP section during the Carling Knockout clash against Siwelele.



However, Mohafe has since dismissed speculation about a potential comeback.

World.title: Rassie Erasmus explains having just one specialist hooker on tour
World.content:
When Rassie Erasmus named the Springboks’ 37-man squad for the upcoming November internationals, one aspect of his selection flew under the radar, and that was the rather unusual decision to only select two hookers for the tour.

In fact, Malcolm Marx is the only specialist hooker considering that Jan-Hendrik Wessels has previously been deployed as a utility player, capable of slotting in at loosehead prop or hooker.

With Bongi Mbonambi currently not in the national mix, Deon Fourie out with injury, and Johan Grobbelaar omitted from the tour group, it leaves regular flanker Marco van Staden as a stop-gap option at hooker if the need arises.



However, Erasmus has explained why Grobbelaar was left at home for this end-of-year tour as Wessels will clearly be given more opportunities to gain experience at hooker rather than prop.

“We were very honest in the conversations we always have with Grobbies; if I had to give the team man-of-the-year award to someone this year, it would be him,” Erasmus said on Monday.

“We feel like we know 100% where Grobbies is,” the Bok coach added. “But we don’t want to put Grobbies on a tour and Marco doesn’t get a chance.

“We know that Grobbies is there, Grobbies can go to the World Cup, but we’re going to bring the other two hookers. That’s just the way it is.

“Grobbies doesn’t deserve not to be chosen.”

Rassie Erasmus continues careful balancing act

Commenting on the six uncapped players in the travelling squad – Riley Norton, Emmanuel Tshituka, Luan Giliomee, Yaqeen Ahmed, Markus Muller, and Sebastian de Klerk – Erasmus said there was a plan in place.



“They all joined us in camp today and are excited about the tour ahead, so we’ll expose them to our structures this week and monitor how they progress and hopefully we’ll be able to give them a chance to show what they can do at this level against top opposition in the next few weeks.

“They are special players, who all bring something different to the team, and we have full faith in their talent and skillsets.”

Backing for Salmaan Moerat

Having also opted to start Moerat at lock this weekend, Rassie Erasmus said he didn’t subscribe to the opinions of some fans who criticise the veteran forward.

“I’ve never really listened to people who talk nonsense about Salmaan, because he’s not the kind of guy you see doing the flashy work on the field, and we don’t expect him to. We expect him to do what he always does for us.

“He’s been our captain four or five times, I’m not 100% sure, but I think he’s won every single time.

“We need a grinder, like a Jean Kleyn, like an RG Snyman. I think that’s a bit flashy as well, but it’s something we need in the team, and Salmaan brings it to us.”

World.title: Hlungwani identifies major refereeing errors in Pirates’ win over Chiefs
World.content:
Former PSL referee Victor Hlungwani believes Orlando Pirates were fortunate to keep their opening goal in their 2-1 Soweto Derby win over Kaizer Chiefs.

The Buccaneers claimed bragging rights at FNB Stadium this past weekend in a dramatic encounter that drew scrutiny of referee Luxolo Badi for several controversial decisions.

Pirates’ first goal was among the biggest talking points, with Hlungwani ruling that Evidence Mbuthuma was in an offside position when he scored.



Hlungwani on Pirates goal against Chiefs

Speaking on SoccerZone, the former referee explained his decision after analysing the incident using the offside line.

“Here we see Mbuthuma scoring a goal. Did he score a goal in line with the FIFA laws of the game? Let’s go and draw the line,” Hlungwani said.

“If you look at the line, Mbuthuma’s leg is on the line and Miguel’s leg is outside the line, so therefore, this puts who? It puts Mbuthuma in an offside position. It’s very tight, but Mbuthuma here is offside. So this goal shouldn’t have stood.



“But you know they always say if you’re in doubt, give the benefit to the attacking team.”

Hlungwani, though, felt Pirates’ second goal, scored by Moremi after a pass from Mokobodi, was correctly allowed to stand.

“Moremi scored a beautiful goal after Mokobodi gave him a nice pass.”



“Let’s go back and draw the line to see if it’s offside. Here you can see the same Miguel, putting Mokobodi onside,” he explained.

Hlungwani also believes Orlando Pirates were denied a legitimate goal when Oswin Appollis found the net in the dying minutes, only for the effort to be ruled out for offside.

The former referee further questioned Badi’s handling of the Simphiwe Selepe incident, arguing that the Pirates midfielder should have been sent off in the first half.



Hlungwani says Pirates should have been a man down

According to Hlungwani, Selepe committed a foul involving contact with an opponent’s face before making another reckless challenge and subsequently stopping a promising attack.

“Selepe did what we call hand on the face. This is not hand on the face but elbow to the face. If you elbow or hand on the face, it’s a yellow card. He was not given a yellow card in this instance. What does he do minutes later? He comes with a leg challenge, it was reckless. A yellow card was given,” Hlungwani added.

“The last one, he stopped a promising attack. A yellow card should have been issued. Incorrect decision not to award a red card in that instance.”



Hlungwani’s assessment suggests that Pirates benefited from the officials’ decisions despite also having a legitimate goal ruled out during the derby.

Did Pirates rob Chiefs?

World.title: Beloved member of All Blacks management team dies
World.content:
The All Blacks head of security, Logan Cadwallader, has died in Edinburgh following a medical event. Image: X/@ChalynRugby

It has been confirmed early this week that long-serving All Blacks Head of Security Logan Cadwallader passed away following a ‘medical event’ at the team hotel in Edinburgh on Sunday morning.

Logan had been part of the All Blacks environment for 10 years, travelling with the team throughout that time and becoming a much-loved and respected member of the All Blacks group.

Reacting to the news on the eve of the All Blacks’ upcoming November internationals, coach Dave Rennie said the team was struggling to come to terms with the news.



“Logan has been a big part of the All Blacks family for a long time. He was the ultimate team man, loved and trusted by all and a true professional. He looked after all of us, players and staff, and he was a good mate to many in this team. We are all devastated.

“Our thoughts are with his wife, Nannette, his children, Trey, Brooke and Mia, and his wider family and friends. As a team, we will honour Logan and the legacy he has left on the All Blacks.”

Condolences pour in after sudden death of the All Blacks team member

New Zealand Rugby also acknowledged Logan’s service to the country, at the highest level of the New Zealand Defence Force.

Logan served in the New Zealand Army and New Zealand Special Air Service Regiment (NZSAS), with deployments to some of the world’s most demanding environments including Bosnia, East Timor, Afghanistan and the Solomon Islands.

“His service to his country, and the values he carried from it, were reflected in everything he did for the team,” a statement read.

“New Zealand Rugby is supporting Logan’s family, as well as All Blacks players and staff.”



‘Deepest sympathies’

With the All Blacks currently on tour, New Zealand Rugby Chief Executive Steve Lancaster said Cadwallader would ber sorely missed, but fondly remembered.

“Logan was a valued and trusted member of the management group over the past decade, and he will be greatly missed by everyone who worked alongside him. On behalf of New Zealand Rugby, I extend our deepest sympathies to his family and friends at this very difficult time.”

World.title: Gauteng GBV response plan: Where the help is going and how to reach it
World.content:
Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi outlines the province’s response to gender-based violence and femicide. Image: X @GautengProvince

The Gauteng GBV response plan, the province’s strategy to tackle gender-based violence (GBV), is taking shape, and some of the province’s hardest-hit communities are first in line.

The plan promises new teams on the ground, extra social workers and more support for survivors.

A progress update released by Premier Panyaza Lesufi on Sunday, 1 November, shows how far it has come.



The update comes about 33 days into the 90-day period President Cyril Ramaphosa set in his address on gender-based violence and femicide (GBVF) on 29 September.

It also follows the murders of at least 12 women in Ekurhuleni and other parts of the province since July.

“Gauteng bears a significant share of our nation’s gender-based violence and femicide crisis, and we fully accept our duty to act,” Lesufi said.



The Gauteng Provincial Government has completed 21 of the 67 directives aimed at strengthening the provincial response to gender-based violence and femicide (#GBVF), with a further 38 underway.https://t.co/oyGHl1geO4#GovZAUpdates — @SAgovnews (@SAgovnews) November 1, 2026

What the Gauteng GBV response plan includes

At the centre of the plan, the province will deploy 1,022 GBV response teams across 122 high-risk areas.

In October, Lesufi first described them as GBV “brigades” that the province would deploy across 122 high-risk police precincts with tools of trade.



The province has used GBV brigades before.

Under former premier David Makhura, they included safety volunteers working at ward level to raise awareness and link survivors to support.

The province is also adding 56 social workers within the Department of Social Development to support victims and survivors.



Other measures include:

strengthening seven Thuthuzela Care Centres , where rape survivors receive medical care and help to open a case

, where rape survivors receive medical care and help to open a case supporting sexual offences courts , which house 144 victim-friendly rooms

, which house involving all 19 of the province’s Medical Legal Clinics to help safeguard forensic evidence.

Gauteng has also added a fifth priority to Ramaphosa’s four directives, focused on strengthening places of safety and support services for survivors.

Which communities is the Gauteng GBV response plan targeting?

The province has singled out the 10 police stations recording the highest numbers of rape cases for extra support.



They include Rietgat, Alexandra, Mamelodi, Diepsloot, Ivory Park, Dobsonville, Redhill, Midrand and Tembisa.

Lesufi said reported cases had already declined at these stations since the plan began.

Visible policing has also been stepped up in high-risk areas.



How the Gauteng GBV response plan aims to make public spaces safer

Municipal safety audits are 60% to 80% complete in most municipalities.

The provincial government said it would repair urgent hazards found during the audits, or add them to funded action plans, within 90 days.

It will also publish detailed audit results online so the public can monitor progress.



Each metro has started acting on its findings:

Johannesburg has mapped major risk zones and prepared 10 previously hijacked buildings for public reuse.

has mapped major risk zones and prepared for public reuse. Tshwane has cleared overgrown vegetation around high-risk transit stations.

has cleared overgrown vegetation around high-risk transit stations. Ekurhuleni has inspected all its taxi ranks and flagged broken CCTV systems for repair.

Authorities have also carried out 7,322 liquor outlet inspections, closed 20 outlets, issued 459 non-compliance noticesand run 41 joint enforcement operations.

Tackling the forensic backlog

The province has recovered crime kits from Thuthuzela Care Centres in all five districts and sent them to the Forensic Science Laboratory.



Investigating officers must now carry crime kits to medical examinations, so evidence is not left behind.

An Identification Task Team has also been set up to run a digital fingerprint audit of unidentified women and children.

When will the Gauteng GBV teams arrive?

This is where questions remain.



Of the 67 directives in the province’s response, only 21 have been fully completed. Another 38 are under way, and eight have not yet started.

Reports differ on whether all 1,022 teams are already on the ground, and no full deployment date was given.

The province admits that challenges remain, especially with forensic backlogs and speeding up municipal safety work.



“Protecting our women and children is an absolute priority that demands immediate action, as delayed justice is no justice at all.”

How to get help now

Survivors do not need to wait for the new teams.

Gauteng has 18 shelters with 363 beds, and new referral tools have been rolled out at all 43 protection-order courts. Technical problems with the e-Panic Button app have been fixed, and CCTV networks have been expanded.



These services are available 24 hours a day:

GBV Command Centre: 0800 428 428

0800 428 428 “Please call me”: dial 1207867# for free to request a social worker

send “help” to 31531 SAPS emergency: 10111

World.title: Americans vote in midterms set to upend Donald Trump presidency
World.content:
Americans deliver their verdict on Donald Trump's tumultuous second presidency on Tuesday in midterm elections. Image: RICARDO ARDUENGO / AFP

Americans deliver their verdict on Donald Trump’s tumultuous second presidency on Tuesday in midterm elections that threaten to shatter his grip on Washington, with Democrats poised to seize the House and challenge for control of the Senate.

Republicans losing the House would give Democrats the power to stall Trump’s legislative agenda and launch sweeping investigations of his administration.

A Senate defeat would also threaten his ability to appoint Supreme Court justices and senior officials.



READ | AGOA BLOW: SA hits back at Donald Trump over trade decision

Mood turning sharply

The election amounts to a nationwide judgment on Trump, with the mood turning sharply against Republicans amid anger over soaring living costs and the war against Iran.

All 435 House seats and 35 of the 100 Senate seats are at stake, along with governorships in 36 states.



Democrats need only three House gains and a net four seats in the Senate to wrest both chambers from Republican hands.

Trump returned to office last year promising to bring down prices, but inflation, tariffs and fuel costs inflated by the Middle East conflict have squeezed Americans.

The 80-year-old’s approval rating has hovered near the low 30s.



In the suburbs of Atlanta, Georgia, retired teacher Jane Callum, 77, was among Democrats canvassing for Senator Jon Ossoff who framed the race as a watershed moment for the country’s future.

“I really feel an obligation to do everything that I possibly can to change the direction that our country is going in now, and put it more on the path to democracy and away from autocracy,” she told AFP.

Economic discontent

Republicans insist that Trump’s tax cuts and immigration crackdown will benefit Americans and they are portraying Democratic candidates as left-wing radicals.



But in his final public campaign appearance on Monday, Trump barely touched on the economy and spent most of the time in a rambling talk about his problem-plagued renovation of Washington’s Reflecting Pool.

“This is the last day before the midterm elections, the most important midterm I believe in our lifetime,” he said, 26 minutes into the speech, before quickly returning to talking about renovations.

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer branded it a “pathetic closing message.”



Some Republican supporters remain confident.

“We’re going to win. As a matter of fact, we’ve probably already won,” Texas military veteran Yvonne Clouser told AFP.

But while Republicans hold a 53-47 Senate majority, the battlefield is extending into conservative states like Kansas, Texas, Iowa, Ohio and Alaska.



Democrats must also defend competitive seats, including in Michigan, where a bitter internal dispute saw congresswoman Haley Stevens endorse Republican Mike Rogers rather than the Democratic nominee, Abdul El-Sayed.

Decision Desk HQ’s final forecast forecasted 241 House seats for Democrats against 194 for Republicans, and a narrower 52-48 Democratic Senate majority.

Disputed results?

Polls can underestimate one party’s support, and Republicans hope their voters turn out in force on Election Day.



More than 57 million Americans had already voted early before Tuesday, indicating the high energy.

The campaign has attracted more than $11 billion in political advertising, while billionaire Trump ally Elon Musk has poured hundreds of millions of dollars into Republican political efforts.

As soon as polls close, concerns will mount over whether results will be accepted by the Republicans.



Trump, who tried to overturn his 2020 election defeat, has repeatedly alleged widespread voter fraud and accused Democrats – with no evidence – of cheating.

The Justice Department, run by a close Trump ally, has already sued to potentially block certification of Alaska’s Senate race if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan narrowly loses, although a court ruled against the effort on the eve of the election.

And the Supreme Court rejected on Monday an emergency bid to force California to set aside the mail-in ballots of more than 20 000 people on the grounds they may not be American citizens.



Trump, who will watch the midterms results at the White House on Tuesday night, signaled that if he does lose control of Congress he could simply defy Democrats.

“I veto everything,” he told a podcast on Monday, although he said he might strike deals with Democrats eventually.

World.title: Two arrested in Limpopo for election-related offences
World.content:
POLOKWANE - Two people have been arrested in Limpopo in connection with alleged election-related offences, including the unlawful removal of election posters and intimidation.

In the first incident, a man was arrested in the Mankweng policing area for allegedly unlawfully removing election posters. The incident was reportedly captured on video. The accused has since appeared in court, with the matter postponed to 30 November 2026.

In a separate incident in the Sekhukhune District, another man was arrested on charges of assault and intimidation.

It is alleged that the man’s political party T-shirt was forcibly removed and set alight during an incident involving individuals allegedly affiliated with a political party.

A case was registered at Sekhukhune Police Station, and investigations are ongoing.

Limpopo Provincial Commissioner of Police, Lieutenant General Jan Petrus Scheepers, reiterated that SAPS will not tolerate intimidation, violence, or the unlawful removal or destruction of election material.

He urged political parties, their supporters, and communities to respect the law, exercise political tolerance, and resolve their differences peacefully.

World.title: AGOA exclusion not a catastrophe for SA agriculture, says Sihlobo
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africa’s exclusion from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) is not entirely unexpected, agricultural economist Wandile Sihlobo says.

The Office of the United States Trade Representative announced on Monday that South Africa and Rwanda would be excluded from the programme, which provides eligible African countries with duty-free access to the US market.

The decision is a blow to both economies, which the US has accused of engaging in practices inconsistent with AGOA’s eligibility criteria.

The US is an important market for South African agriculture, accounting for about 4% of the country’s agricultural exports, according to Sihlobo.

South Africa’s main agricultural exports to the US include citrus, berries, grapes, raisins, wine, fruit juices, apples, pears, apricots and nuts.

However, Sihlobo says losing AGOA benefits will not be catastrophic for the agricultural sector.

“For some time, many South Africans have been thinking that this day would come,” he said.

“Not only because of the current political environment, but you can go back to 2014, which was a period when these conversations were taking place about whether South Africa qualified,” he added.

Sihlobo argues that South Africa, as an upper-middle-income country, should have transitioned out of AGOA years ago and pursued a full bilateral trade agreement with the US.

World.title: Power outage interrupts water supply in Ekurhuleni, Tshwane metros
World.content:
PRETORIA – A widespread power outage in Ekurhuleni has disrupted water supply from Rand Water’s Mapleton Pumping Station, leaving at least six municipalities affected.

The municipalities include Lesedi, Govan Mbeki, Victor Khanya and Thembisile Hani, as well as the Ekurhuleni and Tshwane metros.

The Boksburg pumping station has been unable to operate since the electricity interruption was reported on Monday.

Rand Water said the failure to repair a faulty breaker and restore power had left it unable to resume pumping water to the affected municipalities.

READ | Pressure mounts on Joburg Water amid ongoing supply disruptions

“Despite repeated enquiries throughout the night, Rand Water has received no firm commitment from the City of Ekurhuleni on when electricity will be restored,” the bulk water supplier said in a statement on Tuesday.

“Rand Water remains unable to resume pumping and has no control over the restoration of the city’s electricity supply. At the time of this statement, the city had not communicated an estimated restoration time.”

World.title: eNCA MarkData| Tshwane's political landscape could shift
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Leadership in the City of Tshwane has changed hands over the years, with the ANC governing the metro for an extended period before the Democratic Alliance took over and ActionSA later assumed leadership.

As South Africa heads into the local government elections, the contest for the mayoral chain and control of council remains open.

In Tuesday’s MarkData survey, conducted on the eve of the elections, we look at the north-western part of the metro, where voting patterns in some wards could point to possible changes.

World.title: Three alleged extortionists killed in Eastern Cape
World.content:
ZWELITSHA - Three suspects have been killed following a shootout with members of the Tactical Response Team (TRT) in Ngqeleni in the Eastern Cape on Monday.

The three suspects were allegedly involved in extortion, collecting money from local shops.

According to police spokesperson Brigadier Nobuntu Gantana, TRT members were traveling along the Nothintsila gravel road when they spotted the suspects who fit the description to the alleged extortionists.

They stopped their vehicles and approached the suspects. The suspects opened fire on the police, who retaliated. All three suspects died at the scene.

Three firearms belonging to the suspects, with their serial numbers filed off, were recovered at the scene. According to Gantana, the suspects have not yet been identified.

Cases of attempted murder and possession of unlicensed firearms and ammunition have been opened.

The police are appealing for anyone with information regarding the suspects' identities or alleged extortion activities to come forward.

World.title: Pressure mounts on Joburg Water amid ongoing supply disruptions
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Residents are demanding answers from Joburg Water as ongoing supply disruptions leave communities struggling with dry taps.

The People's Water Forum has taken its demands to the utility's offices, calling for equal access to water and accountability over unreliable supply.

Meanwhile, frustrated residents say they are tired of paying for a service they are not receiving.

After days of dry taps in several parts of the city, the People's Water Forum took its grievances to Joburg Water's offices.

Civil society organisations say residents can no longer be expected to live without reliable access to water.

With local government elections around the corner, some groups say service delivery, particularly access to water, must be a priority.

Midrand and North Riding are among the areas affected by ongoing water supply problems.

Residents in Midrand say poor communication from Joburg Water has added to their frustration.

In North Riding, water shortages are compounded by another service delivery problem -- uncollected rubbish.

The frustration is growing, with some residents warning that communities are reaching a breaking point.

Small businesses are also feeling the impact, with some struggling to operate without a consistent water supply.

Joburg Mayor Dada Morero says improvements in system capacity have resulted in a gradual recovery in some of the affected areas.

But for many residents still struggling with dry taps, that recovery has yet to translate into reliable water supply.

World.title: Elections 2026 | Eastern Cape police boost deployments
World.content:
GQEBERHA - Authorities are leaving nothing to chance as South Africa prepares for Wednesday's Local Government Elections.

With concerns over possible criminal activity and election-related violence, Eastern Cape police are stepping up deployments, particularly in identified hotspot areas.

The aim is to ensure voters can cast their ballots safely and without intimidation.

Police have warned that any attempts to disrupt the electoral process will not be tolerated.

Provincial Police Commissioner Vuyisile Ncata says that while more than 850 officers from Nelson Mandela Bay will be deployed to OR Tambo District, the metro will not be left without adequate policing.

Police have identified three voting stations in OR Tambo District as among the country's high-risk areas for possible election-related violence.

With additional officers on the ground, police say they are determined to ensure a safe and peaceful voting process.

World.title: AGOA | US raised issues not discussed during trade talks, says govt
World.content:
PRETORIA - Government has accused the United States of introducing new issues into trade negotiations after Washington notified Pretoria of its intention to withdraw South Africa's benefits under the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA).

On Monday, Washington announced that it would exclude South Africa and Rwanda from the major Africa-US duty-free trade programme, citing practices it said were “inconsistent” with the deal’s eligibility criteria.

“These concerning and pervasive practices include, but are not limited to, barriers that undermine American trade and investment and practices that pose a threat to US national security and foreign policy interests in the region,” US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement.

The exclusions will take effect on January 1, according to the statement.

However, in a statement on Tuesday, the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (DTIC) said Washington was introducing issues that had not formed part of discussions during negotiations, which began in 2025.

The department said Pretoria had made concessions beyond those offered in 2015 through the appropriate channels, while safeguarding its biosecurity, constitutional imperatives and obligations under World Trade Organisation rules.

READ MORE | SA's AGOA future hangs in the balance as US reviews eligibility

Trade, Industry and Competition Minister Parks Tau said Washington's decision did not define the broader relationship between South Africa and the United States.

“The solution depends on the willingness of both parties to find a solution,” Tau said.

He acknowledged the concerns the decision could raise for communities linked to AGOA-supported value chains.

“As a responsible government, South Africa has proactively retained measures that were available as a response to the reciprocal tariffs,” he said.

Tau added that government would continue to accelerate efforts to diversify South Africa's export markets.
