World.title: Kenyans stranded after Saudi Arabia blocks entry over Ebola concerns
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

More than 300 Kenyans who travelled to Saudi Arabia in search of employment have been forced to return home after authorities blocked their entry over Ebola-related restrictions, leaving them stranded at the airport for two days.

The group, which departed Kenya on October 30, had travelled to the Gulf country on valid work visas but was denied entry upon arrival and subsequently repatriated, arriving back in the country on Monday.

The return follows a warning by Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale on Saturday, October 31, over restrictions imposed by Saudi Arabia on travellers from countries flagged over Ebola concerns.

Speaking to the media at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) on Monday, the affected workers recounted their ordeal, accusing authorities at the airport of subjecting them to harsh conditions as they waited to be repatriated.

“We were treated so harshly as though we had leprosy. We only took one meal per day and slept on the cold floors at the airport in Saudi Arabia,” said Kanyi Njau, one of the affected workers, claiming that some have even lost their luggage.

Beyond the difficult experience at the airport, the workers said their biggest concern was the financial loss incurred while preparing for the promised jobs.

Some said they had sold land, household belongings and other property, while others borrowed money to pay recruitment agents, process visas and secure travel documents in preparation for their departure.

Njau said the abrupt disruption had shattered the hopes of many who had invested heavily in securing employment abroad.

“Some of us sold things in our houses, even land. Some even took loans from shylocks just so that we could travel over there for the jobs, but now we are back with no hope,” she said.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The workers are now appealing to the Kenyan Government to intervene and resolve the standoff with Saudi authorities before their visas expire, allowing them to return and take up the jobs they had secured.

Meanwhile, recruitment agencies have called on the Government to urgently clarify the restrictions, warning that uncertainty over a 21-day provision could disrupt the country's labour mobility programme.

Monika Mwema, the Secretary General of the Association of Skilled Migrant Agencies of Kenya (ASMAK), said recruiters had been caught off guard, with some workers already repatriated while others had confirmed tickets and were scheduled to travel.

“We are caught off guard. We have people who are coming back because they could not be allowed to enter Saudi Arabia, while others have confirmed tickets and are even supposed to leave tonight and tomorrow,” she said.

Mwema said the association was seeking clarification on what the 21-day provision meant for workers holding stamped Saudi work visas, including whether they would be required to undergo quarantine in Kenya or in a third country before being allowed into the Kingdom.

“Does it mean we have to quarantine our people here for the 21 days, then they are allowed to enter the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia? Or does it mean that we need to seek an alternative quarantine area where there is no case of Ebola?” she asked.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

She said recruiters were also concerned about the 90-day period within which migrant workers are required to travel after their visas are stamped, warning that delays could result in significant losses for agencies and prospective employees.

Mwema added that some workers had already undergone training and completed examinations in preparation for their deployment, while recruitment partners in Saudi Arabia were demanding to know when the workers would arrive.

“The losses are just too many. We have people who have already gone to school for training; others have done their examinations and are waiting to go. Our partners are calling us, asking when these people are coming, but we are all in the dark,” she said.

ASMAK is now seeking urgent engagement with the Kenyan Government and Saudi authorities to establish a clear way forward.

Mwema said the association was ready to engage the Government, including through a meeting with President William Ruto, to discuss the future of labour mobility between the two countries.

Saudi Arabia remains Kenya's biggest market for labour mobility, with recruiters warning that continued uncertainty could affect workers awaiting deployment and agencies with visas already processed.

World.title: Gachagua dismisses Uhuru reconciliation calls, says 'we are one team'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua received at PCEA Kamangu in Kikuyu constituency by former Kiambu governor James Nyoro on November 1, 2026. [George Njunge, Standard]

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed calls for mediation between him and former President Uhuru Kenyatta, insisting that the two leaders remain in contact and have no differences requiring reconciliation.

Gachagua said attempts by Mount Kenya elders to broker peace between them were unnecessary, maintaining that he and the former Head of State continue to communicate, meet and share meals despite perceptions of a political fallout.

He challenged elders calling for reconciliation to instead focus on uniting the Mount Kenya community, warning that internal divisions could weaken the region's political voice and influence.

“On unity, as a community we have to remain united. Our unity is strength. Nimeona some elders in the newspaper wakisema tunataka to reconcile Rigathi Gachagua and Uhuru Kenyatta. How do you reconcile two brothers, who love one another and work together?” he posed.

The former Deputy President maintained that he and Uhuru were still on the same team, dismissing claims that their relationship had deteriorated to a point requiring third-party intervention.

“President Uhuru Kenyatta and I are one team. We work together. Please elders don’t reconcile us because there is no need for reconciliation. We are working together. There is no work there, we are one. We talk the same language, we meet, talk, we agree,” he said.

Gachagua further urged Mount Kenya elders to resist attempts to divide the community along political lines and instead promote dialogue and cohesion among its leaders.

“Our unity is our strength as a community. Please help me to unite Mount Kenya elders and tell people not to accept to be divided,” he added.

His remarks come amid growing calls by sections of Mount Kenya elders for reconciliation among influential political figures from the region following political differences that have emerged since the 2022 General Election.

Uhuru, who served as Kenya's fourth president from 2013 to 2022, remains an influential political figure in the region, while Gachagua has continued to position himself as a key voice in Mount Kenya politics.

World.title: Sifuna rallies opposition leaders to unite against Ruto in 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi leader Edwin Sifuna adresses a rally at Ukunda in Kwale County on 31st October, 2026. [Omondi Onyango, Standard]

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna’s Linda Mwananchi movement took its grassroots mobilisation tour to Kwale County, a day after unveiling its secretariat and leadership, with leaders urging the opposition to unite behind one candidate to face President William Ruto in 2027.

The unveiling had been marred by disagreement, with Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka jeered. Addressing a rally at Masai Grounds in Ukunda town, Sifuna said Kenyans were yearning for a single, strong opposition candidate and asked other leaders not to let them down.

“To send Ruto home, we need a strong team and a strong presidential candidate. I will ask other leaders to listen to the voices of the people politely because this is the voice of God,” he said.

The team made stopovers in Samburu, Kinango, Kwale town and Kombani during the day-long tour. Unlike earlier rallies in Mombasa, the Kwale events drew modest crowds, amid claims that local organisers had failed to mobilise supporters.

The mobilisation tour covered Samburu Town, Kinango Town, Kombani Junction, Lunga Lunga Town, and culminated in a major public rally at the Ukunda Showground.

The movement officially opened its new Kwale County office as part of a push to build county-level structures ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Addressing supporters in the rain, Sifuna declared that he will continue to build consensus among the opposition to ensure that they are united to send Ruto home in 2027. he said that divisions of the opposition leaders will guarantee Ruto a second term.

He warned against schemes to elbow local leaders out of the front lines, stressing that Kwale residents and local aspirants must drive the agenda on regional issues like water shortages and mineral exploitation. The Kwale tour marks the first public rallies after weeks without a large-scale county mobilisation exercise.

It has previously held gatherings in Mombasa and Taita Taveta as part of its plan to reach all 47 counties. The tour took place the same day the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) was holding a rally at Jacaranda Grounds in Nairobi's Embakasi East constituency.

Embakasi East MP Babu Owino urged Sifuna, Musyoka, DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua and Jubilee leader Fred Matiang’i to agree on one presidential candidate, warning that time was running out.

“We are urging all opposition leaders to sit down and talk. We only have nine months to the General Election, and you should agree on one presidential challenger to President Ruto,” he said. “Sifuna, Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang’i should come together now. United we stand, divided we fall.”

isii Senator Richard Onyonka said it was time for opposition leaders to lock themselves in a room and emerge with a single candidate to face Mr Ruto. The call was backed by Linda Mwananchi chairman Godfrey Osotsi and Secretary General Caroli Omondi.

Trans Nzoia Governor George Natembeya, however, said Sifuna was best placed to challenge the President and asked Mr Gachagua and Mr Musyoka to back him.

“I want to urge Gachagua and Kalonzo to back Sifuna for the opposition to secure an easy win against Ruto. I want to assure you that there will be no rigging of the election,” he said.

Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza said Kenyans would reject Ruto at the ballot for failing to honour pledges, including those on women’s empowerment.

Sifuna accused the President of failing to protect the Constitution and the rights of Kenyans. “He has focused more on building houses and markets and failed to protect lives,” he said.

He also claimed the government had issued title deeds for smaller parcels than residents used to own, while land was stolen. He further alleged that the government was plotting to plunder mineral resources at Mrima Hill in Kwale and demanded that an agreement with American investors be made public.

World.title: Musonye to lead AFCON 2027 preparations
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya with Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee chairperson Nicholas Musonye on October 29, 2026. [Jonah Onyango, Standard]

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya has unveiled the Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON PAMOJA 2027), with Nicholas Musonye appointed chairman to oversee Kenya’s preparations for the continental football tournament.

Musonye will be deputised by Hussein Mohammed, while Anthony Lung’aho Inzihuli, also known as Antony Emmanuel Inzahuli Lung’aho, will serve as head of the secretariat and chief executive officer.

The committee is tasked with coordinating Kenya’s preparations, including stadium renovations, infrastructure development, operational planning and logistical arrangements ahead of the tournament, which Kenya will co-host with Uganda and Tanzania.

Mvurya said the committee brings together individuals with experience, professional expertise and leadership to help deliver a successful competition that meets the expectations of football fans, participating teams and the Confederation of African Football (CAF).

“I have unveiled the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) PAMOJA 2027 LOC Standing Committee, entrusting its members with the national responsibility of coordinating and overseeing Kenya’s preparations towards delivering a world-class, memorable and successful continental football tournament,” Mvurya said.

He challenged members to move from planning to implementation, emphasising operational readiness, coordination, strategic partnerships, financial accountability and adherence to delivery timelines.

“With less than eight months to kick-off, I challenged the committee to move decisively from planning to execution,” he said.

Besides Musonye, Mohammed and Lung’aho Inzihuli, the listed committee members include Football Kenya Federation (FKF) Vice-President McDonald Mariga and FKF National Executive Committee representative Robert Macharia.

Other members named in the roster are Timothy Nabea, a former FKF NEC member; Gabriel Mghendi; Peter Kamau; Kerubo Momanyi; Benard Lagat; Collins Kalee; Caleb Amwayi; Ken Rungu; and Dan Shikanda, the former AFC Leopards chairperson.

The list also includes Charles Njagi, Thomas Karugu, Evelyn Cheluget, Miriam Chepkoech, Rodgers Chimega, Diana Injendi Manyengo and Collins Were.

The 38 committee members also comprises representation across functional areas, including finance, technical matters, refereeing, legal affairs and youth development.

The committee is expected to coordinate the different aspects of tournament preparation and ensure that the relevant agencies and stakeholders work towards agreed targets.

Kenya’s preparations also include the development of Talanta Sports City, officially known as the Raila Odinga International Stadium, which is expected to strengthen the country's capacity to host major international football matches.

Mvurya said the planned high-profile encounter between German giants FC Bayern München and Dutch powerhouse AFC Ajax, scheduled for January 5, 2027, would provide an opportunity to assess the country’s readiness.

The event is expected to test security arrangements, transport and logistics, crowd management, operational systems and the overall fan experience.

The CS also disclosed that representatives of the two European clubs had visited Kenya to assess its capacity to host the proposed fixture.

He said the government was adopting a whole-of-government approach, involving relevant agencies responsible for security, immigration, tourism, travel and hospitality.

AFCON 2027 is expected to attract thousands of supporters, officials and international visitors, creating opportunities for hotels, airlines, tour operators, transport businesses and other service providers.

The government is also positioning the tournament as an opportunity to promote tourism, attract investment, develop sporting infrastructure and inspire young footballers.

Mvurya said the committee carries the responsibility of delivering an event that would bring national pride while creating a lasting legacy for the country.

“I reaffirmed their mandate and reminded them that they carry the hopes and aspirations of over 55 million Kenyans to deliver a tournament that brings pride and joy to the country while securing a lasting legacy in sports development, tourism, investment and economic opportunities,” he said.

World.title: Not so fast! Court blocks Bomas expansion
World.content:
Contractors hired are barred from clearing vegetation, cutting trees, excavating, grading, fencing, constructing routes, and undertaking any works at the disputed site. [File, Standard]

The Environment and Lands Court has blocked the government from continuing with the construction of a car park inside the Nairobi National Park.

Justice Grace Kemei, in her ruling, said that the contractors hired are barred from clearing vegetation, cutting trees, excavating, grading, fencing, constructing routes, and undertaking any works at the disputed site.

World.title: Kikuyu PCEA church loses 2.7-acre illegally acquired land
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Justice Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent. [Courtesy, EACC]

The Presbyterian Church of East Africa (PCEA) has lost its 2.7-acre piece of land to a school.

This is after the Environment and Lands Court at Thika established that the land under the church's Ruguthi Women's Guild was a school playground and was illegally allocated.

Presiding Judge Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property, and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent.

According to her, the land had been reserved for use as a playground by Kanyiha, Lusigetti and Njumbi Primary Schools.

The verdict follows a case filed by the Law Society of Kenya, with the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) participating as an interested party.

In a statement on Monday, EACC's head of Corporate Affairs and Communication Stephen Karuga said the anti-graft agency presented evidence demonstrating that the land had been reserved for public use and therefore, any allocation to third parties was irregular. Justice Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent. [Courtesy, EACC]

"Our investigations established that the land was set aside in 1957 by the former County Council of Kiambu for use as a school playing field," Karuga said, adding, "the investigations further revealed that there was no letter of offer or acceptance, no evidence of payment of rent rates and no proof that the Women's Guild had paid any consideration to the council for the land."

According to Karuga, the judgement safeguards a vital public facility used by more than 1,300 pupils, ensuring that the playground remains available for learning, sports and recreation for the current and future generations.

As a result, the judge said the allocation, transfer and registration of the land LR. NO KARAI/350 and subsequent issuance of a title deed in 2001 was unprocedural, illegal, null and void.

"An order of Mandamus is hereby issued directing the 3rd respondent, the Land Registrar, Kiambu Chief Land Registrar, to forthwith cancel and revoke the Title Deed and all register entries in respect of the land issued to the 1st respondent on Dec 6, 2001, or at any subsequent date," the Judge said.

The judge further ordered that the said parcel of land be handed over to the Board of Management of the two schools and the Education Ministry.

"An order of permanent injunction is hereby issued restraining the 1st respondent, whether by herself, her church officials, agents, servants, assigns or anyone claiming through her, from entering into, taking possession of, fencing, depositing construction materials upon, transferring, charging, developing or in any other manner dealing or interfering with the land," she ordered.

World.title: Sakaja protests release of 14 suspects linked to Eastleigh collapsed building
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja has protested the release of suspects linked to the collapsed building in Eastleigh.

While pushing for the county to have prosecutorial powers, Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court.

Sakaja in statement posted on his X account (formerly Twitter) said City Hall had taken enforcement action against those involved after establishing change of user from a residential property to a commercial had been approved.

According to Sakaja, architectural plans required to authorise construction had not been approved.

The Governor said County officers arrested the suspects and handed them over to Kamukunji Police Station because county governments no longer hold prosecutorial powers they previously held.

“We enforced the law and arrested those involved. However, because we do not have prosecutorial powers, the suspects were handed over to Kamukunji Police Station. They were reportedly released on a cash bail of Sh50,000 without being taken to court,” Sakaja said.

“We want the police to explain why the suspects were released without being presented in court and why construction was allowed to continue. These are serious questions that must be answered,” he added.

A police occurrence book entry from Kamukunji Police Station indicates that 14 suspects were booked into custody on June 17, 2026, over the alleged offences relating to contravention of city planning laws.

Enforcement action and arrests were made severally by the county officials and most recently in July after failing to comply with the enforcement order below. However the suspects were released on a 50k bail at Kamukunji police on the very same day. Prosecution of the same was also denied. We have repeatedly asked for the resumption of the power to prosecute such violations of such county and county related laws after this was taken away from County governments in 2024 (one such letter to the office of the DPP is attached). Meanwhile, several such cases have either been rejected by prosecutors (who are independent of the County), dismissed by the justice system or have had minimal fines imposed. Fining a developer 50k for an illegal development with hundreds of millions without orders to stop and remove the offensive development is completely unreasonable. I raised this in the Senate a fortnight ago and we shall keep pushing for a review of this position. All of these instances, where enforcement action has been curtailed, blocked or interfered with, will be published to the public. October 25, 2026

The entry, recorded under OB No. 98/17/06/2026, names the suspects and states that they were booked by Nairobi City County officers before being placed in police cells.

A separate Kenya Police Service record indicates that 10 suspects were subsequently released on a cash bail of Sh50,000.

The entry, recorded at 9.44pm, states that the release was carried out on the instructions of the Officer Commanding Station (OCS), identified in the record as C.I. Onyapidi, through Corporal Awadh.

The record references receipt number 2039434 and states that the suspects left the station without complaints.

However, the documents do not, on their own, establish the specific charges against the suspects, the legal basis for the bail arrangement or whether they were subsequently presented in court.

The discrepancy between the 14 suspects recorded as booked into custody and the 10 named in the release entry also raises questions about the subsequent status of the other suspects. Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Sakaja said a June 2025 enforcement notice adds another dimension to the questions surrounding the property and the enforcement of planning regulations.

The notice, issued by Nairobi City County over alleged construction works undertaken without the required development permission, cited the Physical and Land Use Planning Act, 2019, and county by-laws.

It directed the recipient to stop the works and remove the development described as illegal, warning that the County could undertake the required action and recover the costs if the directives were not followed.

The notice also provided for an appeal to the County Physical and Land Use Planning Liaison Committee.

Sakaja clarified that approval to change a property’s use from private to commercial-cum-residential does not amount to approval of architectural plans authorising construction.

He said the County approved the change of use but did not approve the architectural plans, yet construction proceeded.

I have seen some people peddling a fake approval document alleging that the Eastleigh development was approved. It is telling that this is the same document that the Eastleigh developer used to get NCA approval. They allege that the development was approved in January of 2024. This is not true. The application for development as shown below was made in November of 2024, it could not have been approved in February of the same year. Also, there is a difference between a change of user approval and a development approval. The developer applied for change of use from residential to residential & commercial in August of 2024. Change of user was approved in October of 2024. Development approval has never been granted. The developer went on to build with impunity and without building approvals despite enforcement action by the county and arrests. — Sakaja Arthur Johnson (@SakajaJohnson) October 25, 2026

“If the building had been approved for construction, I would have named the officers who approved it so that action could be taken against them,” he said.

Sakaja, in his argument, said the current arrangement creates a gap between enforcement and prosecution, leaving counties dependent on other agencies after taking action against alleged offenders. Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Under his proposal, appropriately authorised county prosecutors would be able to pursue qualifying county offences through the courts, subject to the law and the constitutional authority of the Director of Public Prosecutions.

He said county prosecutors previously had a better understanding of technical offences involving planning, construction and other county regulations, enabling them to handle such cases more directly.

“We want to be able not only to enforce regulations and make arrests, but also to take offenders to court and prosecute them. When counties had prosecutorial powers, we had prosecutors who understood the nature and seriousness of county offences and could ensure that appropriate legal action was taken,” he said.

World.title: Egypt-Sudan sign agreement to defend water security
World.content:
Egypt and Sudan affirmed their total rejection of any unilateral actions in the Eastern Nile Basin.

They agreed that the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD) – constructed unilaterally in violation of international law – carries grave consequences, and poses a persistent threat to the downstream Nile Basin states, particularly given Ethiopia’s unilateral management of the GERD and the absence of a binding legal mechanism for its governance.

During the third round of the “2+2” consultative meetings, involving the foreign and irrigation ministers of Egypt and Sudan – along with their respective delegations – both sides reviewed developments regarding the Nile River issue.

They emphasized that the water security of Sudan and Egypt is inextricably linked.

Furthermore, they agreed on the necessity of defending the water security of the downstream Nile states, upholding the full water rights and usage entitlements of both nations as stipulated in the 1959 agreement, and ensuring that no infringement upon these rights is permitted.

The two sides called on Ethiopia to abandon its unilateral policy and restore cooperation in accordance with applicable international law, specifically the principles of avoiding harm, providing prior notification, engaging in consultation, and reaching consensus, to ensure the sustainability of the Nile River.

They further emphasized that the issue of the Ethiopian dam concerns only the three Eastern Nile Basin states—Egypt, Sudan, and Ethiopia—and rejected Ethiopia’s attempts to involve other Nile Basin nations in the matter.

Memorandum of understanding

The governments of Egypt and Sudan on Monday signed a memorandum of understanding to implement development projects related to water resources in Sudan, as part of an Egyptian initiative for the development of Nile Basin countries.

The signing took place in the presence of Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and his Sudanese counterpart, Mohieddin Salem.

Egypt’s Minister of Water Resources and Irrigation, Hany Sewilam, emphasized that the primary challenge in the Nile Basin is not a scarcity of water resources, but rather a lack of cooperation among the basin countries.

Vast water resources

The minister noted that the region possesses vast water resources; the core of the dispute lies in the management and control of the Nile’s waters, even though technical solutions exist that could address both water and energy needs.

Sewilam explained that the 11 Nile Basin countries receive approximately seven trillion cubic meters of rainfall annually, a figure that encompasses the water resources of the Nile River, the Congo River, and other rivers within these nations.

He added that the Nile Basin alone holds an estimated two trillion cubic meters of water resources, of which Egypt receives only about 2.7 percent.

Sewilam added that Ethiopia receives over 1,000 billion cubic meters of rainfall annually and possesses more than 80 billion cubic meters of renewable groundwater that can be tapped into and is replenished each year.

The dispute with Ethiopia concerns the issues of water and energy, he said, noting that technical solutions exist for both.

Sewilam pointed out that Ethiopia has significant potential in solar energy, reaching up to 50 gigawatts, and wind energy, ranging between 30-50 gigawatts, yet it insists on building mega-dams.

World.title: Goldman Sachs raises 2027 oil price forecast to US$ 88 per barrel
World.content:
Goldman Sachs has raised its oil price forecasts for the near future, citing escalating geopolitical risks and an increased likelihood of crude supply disruptions from the Middle East.

The bank now expects Brent crude to reach US$ 105 per barrel by this coming December, up from its previous estimate of $90, and has also increased its average price forecast for 2027 to $88 per barrel, a 10 percent rise from its earlier projection.

According to Bloomberg, Goldman Sachs analysts noted that risks to oil supplies could keep the “risk premium” elevated in the near term.

This comes as market concerns grow regarding potential geopolitical escalation following the US midterm elections.

Analysts added that the escalation of attacks on ships and damage to infrastructure, combined with the repercussions of the Russia-Ukraine war, could lead to further disruptions in oil markets.

In its baseline scenario for 2027, the bank included the possibility of a disruption to global supplies amounting to approximately one million barrels per day.

In the most optimistic price scenario, Brent crude could rise to $140 per barrel, with an average price of around $130 per barrel over the coming year, provided that production from Gulf states remains approximately 3.5 million barrels per day below 2025 average levels, according to Reuters.

Conversely, in a bearish scenario oil futures prices could fall below $ 70 per barrel if production in the region recovers more rapidly and supplies return to the market at a faster pace.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Temperatures across Egypt continue to rise slightly on Tuesday: EMA
World.content:
The Egyptian Meteorological Authority (EMA) announced that temperatures will continue to rise slightly across most parts of the country on Tuesday.

Hot weather is expected during the day in most regions, becoming very hot in southern Upper Egypt, while conditions will range from cool to cold at night and during the early morning hours.

Forecast maximum temperatures are 30C in Greater Cairo and Lower Egypt, 28C along the northern coasts, 33C in northern Upper Egypt, and 37C in southern Upper Egypt.

Weather maps indicate the potential for low-level clouds to form across various parts of the north, extending to Greater Cairo and the Suez Canal cities.

This may result in light, inconsequential drizzle in some areas.

There is also a very slight chance of intermittent light rain in parts of the Matrouh desert.

Satellite imagery has detected occasional wind activity, with speeds ranging between 30-35 km/h, affecting areas in Greater Cairo, South Sinai, and southern Upper Egypt at intervals.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Houthis announce attacks on Dammam and Jazan airports
World.content:
The Houthi group announced on Monday that it had targeted Dammam Airport in Saudi Arabia with two drones, as part of their ongoing military operations against the kingdom, Reuters reported.

The group also claimed to have targeted a military aircraft at Jazan Airport in Saudi Arabia – however, there has been no confirmation from the Saudi side regarding these claims.

The extent of any damage or the outcome of the reported attacks remains unclear.

Earlier on Monday, the Saudi Ministry of Defense announced the interception and destruction of two drones in the Riyadh region.

The Ministry’s official spokesperson, Turki Al-Maliki, said on the X platform that two drones had been “intercepted and destroyed in the Riyadh region.”

World.title: Egypt’s Parliament grants final approval to amendments on ‘Fund for Honoring Martyrs’
World.content:
Egypt’s House of Representatives granted the final approval by a standing vote, during its plenary session on Monday, to amendments to the law governing the Fund for Honoring Martyrs and Victims of Military and Security Operations.

The Chair of the Committee on Social Solidarity, Family, and Persons with Disabilities, MP Randa Mostafa, presented the committee’s report on the draft law.

Mostafa said that the legislation aims to provide support, care, and protection to the families of those killed and injured in the line of duty in recognition of the immense sacrifices these martyred soldiers have made and to ensure the well-being of their families thereafter.

The implementation of the law has highlighted an urgent need for legislative intervention to amend certain provisions, she added, ensuring the law achieves its intended objectives.

She explained that this includes removing obstacles that might prevent eligible individuals from receiving their entitlements, specifically by addressing financial burdens associated with certain medical services and documentation – as well as refining the regulations governing compensation for disabilities and other related provisions.

Furthermore, the amendments aim to simplify procedures for eligible beneficiaries, ensuring they can effectively access the support and compensation to which they are entitled.

They also involve restructuring the regulations concerning disability compensation, thereby providing greater organization and clarity regarding the procedures for claiming such compensation, alongside adjustments to other provisions that govern the operations of the Fund.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: World’s largest crypto exchange hit by suspected North Korean hack in world’s largest heist
World.content:
Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, has suspended withdrawals after hackers broke into its digital wallets and stole six billion dollars in what appears to be the biggest crypto heist ever.

The exchange said Friday that it has begun recovering affected assets and was continuing to work with law enforcement and blockchain intelligence firms to trace additional funds.

An initial investigation suggested the hack went through an engineer’s laptop, “which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions,” Binance said late on Thursday. Blockchain evidence suggests the hack originated in North Korea, according to multiple crypto-tracing firms.

A team of cryptocurrency firms managed to freeze about three billion dollars of the stolen loot amid a frenetic battle with the hackers to find and control the digital money.

Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said on X that the attack was not a “one-click” action, but rather a complex process. The investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual nor found evidence of any wallet private key leak.

Binance said it would cover all losses from the company’s funds and an emergency assets fund, adding “user funds are safe.” The crypto exchange said it had temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals to allow security checks to be completed and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover funds. The crypto exchange expects withdrawal services to resume by Sunday morning.

Crypto-tracing firm TRM Labs attributed the heist to an elite North Korean hacking unit “based on robust on and off-chain intelligence,” pointing out that “several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists.”

Pangolin Intelligence, another blockchain-tracking firm based in Singapore, said it also believed that a North Korean hacking unit was behind the heist.

“Analyzing the on-chain activity related to this hack and correlating with information gathered from previous known incidents” led to the attribution, said an analyst with Pangolin Intelligence, who did not want to be named for privacy reasons.

“I think the cat and mouse game has barely begun yet,” the Pangolin Intelligence analyst told CNN, adding that North Korea was likely poised to tap a network of money laundering organizations to try to cash out the stolen funds.

Chainalysis, another crypto-tracking company, said it was monitoring stolen funds “moving across multiple blockchains,” including bitcoin and ethereum. A Chainalysis spokesperson told CNN the firm had “high confidence” North Korea was behind the hack.

CNN has reached out to North Korea’s mission at the UN for comment. Pyongyang has previously denied hacking allegations.

In past investigations of big crypto hacks, the FBI has had an on-call team of analysts that worked to freeze some of the money.

The FBI said in a statement Friday that it is “aware of the incident and is engaged with relevant public and private partners to understand the scope of the activity, evaluate potential impacts, and coordinate appropriate investigative steps.”

A spokesperson for the US Secret Service, which also investigates cybercrime, said the agency’s “investigators are working around the clock with our private-sector partners, including Circle [the company behind the US dollar-backed stablecoin USDC], to identify, freeze, trace, and recover funds stolen from Binance on Thursday. We are also coordinating closely with the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia and law enforcement partners to identify the cyber criminals responsible and bring them to justice.”

If North Korea is proven to be the culprit, it would be little surprise to US law enforcement officials and private experts. North Korean hackers were blamed for the previous record-high crypto hack, when they allegedly stole $1.5 billion from Bybit, another major cryptocurrency exchange. In that case, the attackers stole an amount equal to a significant portion of North Korea’s reported annual gross domestic product in a matter of minutes.

North Korea’s formidable hacking teams are a key source of revenue for the nuclear-armed, sanctions-battered regime, according to current and former US and South Korean officials. Pyongyang-linked hackers have stolen billions of dollars from banks and cryptocurrency firms in the last several years, according to reports from the United Nations and private firms.

A 2023 CNN investigation spotlighted how the South Korean intelligence service worked with private crypto-tracking experts to seize about $1 million in cryptocurrency that North Koreans had stolen from a victim.

Unlike platforms for trading stocks, cryptocurrency exchanges tend to hold digital assets on their users’ behalf, which make them more vulnerable to hackers and theft, particularly given a lack of regulatory oversight within the relatively nascent industry.

Binance was co-founded in 2017 by Canadian national Changpeng Zhao, becoming the world’s largest crypto trading platform within a year of its launch.

However, Zhao stepped down in 2023 after pleading guilty to violating anti-money laundering laws in the US. He was sentenced to four months in federal prison, and was pardoned by President Donald Trump in October last year.

Zhao, who no longer manages the platform but remains its largest shareholder, said on X that he expects user funds to be fully covered by the exchange, pushing back against any suggestion to the contrary in a spat on X with Elon Musk.

Prices of bitcoin and ether, the most widely traded cryptocurrencies, plummeted following news of the Binance breach, but regained some losses to trade about 2-3% lower midday Friday in Hong Kong.

This story has been updated.

World.title: Coffee’s new status symbol is a machine without plastic
World.content:
New York —

For decades, it was the all the bells and whistles that was the selling point for a fancy coffee machine. Now, consumers are looking for what it lacks.

Growing concern over microplastics and sustainability is sparking a wave of plastic-free coffee pods and machines.

Coffee companies and appliance makers have released new machines and redesigned capsules in recent months. Keurig and Lavazza’s new pods ditch the traditional plastic cups for compostable coffee tablets. Caraway’s new machine uses traditional coffee grounds, but unlike a conventional drip machine, the stainless steel and glass machine doesn’t have plastic in its brew path.

More research is needed to determine the actual harm microplastics cause. But nine in 10 Americans are concerned about the effect of the miniscule plastic pieces on the planet and their bodies, according to a 2025 poll conducted by environmental group 5 Gyres; and studies have shown that pods shed microplastics.

The growth in pricey equipment and plastic-free pods fits a broader pattern of consumers trading up on home coffee equipment since the pandemic, said Peter Giuliano, senior advisor for research at Specialty Coffee Association.

The appeal and growth combine three things: health worries about microplastics, concern about plastic in the environment and the “feeling that metal and glass are more ‘luxury’ than plastic,” he told CNN.

New pods

In June, Lavazza introduced Tablì in the US, a $129 machine that uses only single-serve espresso tablets made with compressed ground coffee — a shift from its capsules made from plastic and aluminum.

The tablets are made by a custom technology that “compresses precisely dosed, ground, and tamped coffee into a solid, ready-to-use tab,” Lavazza said in a press release.

The Italian company says the new machine is its “largest investment yet” in the United States as it looks to double revenue to $1 billion by 2029, unlocking the stranglehold Keurig Dr. Pepper has on the coffee market.

Tablì is aimed at customers that want a sustainable alternative to the traditional pod, according to Daniele Foti, vice president of marketing for Lavazza North America.

The first release of the new Lavazza Tablì machine quickly sold out. Lavazza

“Consumers want to enjoy their coffee without the waste that usually comes with single-serve,” she told CNN.

Keurig, which ushered in the boom of plastics with their K-Cups back in the 1990s, launched in October a new line of compostable pods with a specially designed machine called the Alta. (The new pods don’t fit in the old machines.)

Called AltaRounds, the pods have been in development since 2020 in response to consumers’ shifting sustainability and health preferences.

The new pods represent a “significant reduction in plastic compared to our K-Cup pods,” said Phil Drapeau, senior vice president for Keurig’s Future Coffee Systems unit.

“We’ve heard clearly from customers that they want more sustainable products and specifically less plastic and plastic waste,” Drapeau told CNN. “Our data shows that drink variety, quality, and less plastic waste are high priorities across almost every group.”

Keurig has come under fire in the past over its pods, agreeing in 2022 to pay $10 million to settle a class-action lawsuit alleging it misled consumers by marketing its plastic K-Cups as recyclable, though it denied any wrongdoing.

But while the pods and the machine contain less plastic, they are considerably more expensive than a traditional Keurig machine. The Alta bundle that includes glassware and pods costs $499.

Melissa Valiant, director of communications for 5 Gyres, said that both the Lavazza and Keurig products still use plastic, which “ends up in a landfill, incinerator, or our environment after use, contributing to the planet’s growing plastic pollution crisis.”

New machine

Caraway has focused on developing a $495 coffee machine, released last month, that’s created entirely of stainless steel and glass, ensuring that no plastic touches the ground coffee. (Lavazza’s and Keurig’s machines contain some amounts of plastic.)

Developing a coffee machine with plastic-free brew path was challenging, according to Caraway CEO Jordan Nathan. That’s because the pricey glass and steel parts all need to be custom-made.

“We had to make the best coffee possible with no plastic on the interior with a full metal body, but also in a small (counter) footprint that had a single dial,” he told CNN.

Caraway’s new machine is sold out until January. Caraway

Concern over plastic in the kitchen and its affects on the endocrine system has been growing for the past few years, Nathan said, referencing a viral article that linked black plastics in the kitchen to alarming levels of toxic flame retardants.

Social media, influencers and various scientific studies have all fueled the conversation, with parents and other health-conscious shoppers avoiding plastic where they can, including in makeup, food and bedding. Caraway’s other plastic-free products, like cutting boards, have soared in sales over the past three years.

Coffee is a natural next step, Nathan added, because “you never want to heat plastic.”

Demand for Caraway’s new 10-cup coffee maker has been so strong that it’s sold out until January, forcing the company to ramp up production. Meanwhile, Keurig and Lavazza reported similar interest with both company’s product selling out quickly after their initial release.

That appetite for these pods and machines signals the industry will move toward more plastic-free alternatives, Nathan said.

“If you’re not doing it, you’re behind where the puck is moving,” he concluded.

World.title: Fake warnings of nuclear attack posted on hacked Russian and Ukrainian emergency apps
World.content:
Emergency warning apps in Russia and Ukraine were hacked overnight Sunday into Monday, according to authorities in both countries. It’s not clear whether the hacking of the apps is linked.

The apps warn the public of missile, drone and other threats.

But rather than spread panic, the fake messages appear to have had little impact on war-weary civilians – and instead began to generate some imaginative memes.

The messages posted on Ukraine’s public air raid app late on Sunday claimed that the capital Kyiv and other areas were subject to nuclear ⁠and chemical alerts as well as the threat of street combat.

Another fake message said Russia’s ⁠hypersonic Oreshnik missile had been deployed.

“The air alert app appears to have been subjected to enemy influence,” the Ukrainian air force said ‌on Telegram. “There ⁠is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel!”

The app had been recently updated to show the movement of drones in real time.

Stepan Tanasiychuk, who leads Ukraine’s Air Raid Alert project, said Monday it was gradually being restored, with new yellow and red alert levels currently available on the map.

“The team is taking additional measures to secure the app in order to prevent similar situations in the future, Tanasiychuk said on Instagram. “We realise how much unnecessary worry and inconvenience this has caused.”

In a separate event, ⁠the mobile app of Russia’s emergencies ministry – Emercom – was hit by a “massive cyberattack” early Monday that resulted in ⁠”the spread of false information to the public,” state news agency TASS quoted ⁠the ‌ministry as saying.

A fake alert was sent to 33 Russian regions, the ministry said.

The message claimed that “NUCLEAR WARHEADS ON P1-SUN DELIVERY SYSTEMS have been launched across ALL regions of Russia,” and added an expletive-laden warning.

“The app is currently operational, and its full functionality will be restored by the end of the day,” the emergencies ministry said later Monday. “EMERCOM specialists have analyzed the incident and identified the vulnerability exploited by the attacker.”

The ministry played down the significance of the incident, saying that alerts are distributed through regional and municipal systems such as sirens and loudspeakers, SMS messages and media broadcasts.

“All electronic resources belonging to our government agencies are under constant threat of cyberattacks,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Monday.

“As technologies, including AI, continue to evolve, the threat of cyberattacks is growing,” he said.

Few people appear to have fallen for the false messages. Some suggested it had undermined their trust in official warnings.

One Russian user said they had deleted the Emercom app “and I won’t be installing anything like that again. How can they leave apps like this vulnerable? It’s complete nonsense, of course, but what if it weren’t?”

Among comments on Instagram among Russian users of the app, one said the fake alert “was written in such a way that it’s impossible to believe it’s real.”

Another wrote: “It was hard to believe such nonsense. … How did (the Emergencies ministry) even let this happen.. let themselves get hacked.”

“You wake up, open Threads and see tons of posts like this,” another commented. “BUT THANKFULLY IT’S FAKE!”

Others joked that they had not even received the warning, with one writing: “This information was reserved for the chosen ones, don’t worry, you’re not important enough to be hacked.”

One resident of Kyiv responded to the alert about street fighting by posting: “Good thing our mayor is a boxer.”

Another social media post made up a long list of additional threats, including:

“Cat invasion – Cats are taking over the city. Hide the sausages. Pancake emergency – The city has run out of pancakes. Stay home. Clown attack – Clowns have been spotted in the city. Do not go outside without a mask. Alien invasion – UFOs are approaching Earth. Prepare for contact.”

World.title: Liberia: Unity Party Officials’ ‘Unit 2’ Meetings Stir Questions Over Who Wields Power in Boakai Government
World.content:
MONROVIA – Three senior officials of the Unity Party-led government have set tongues wagging after posting photos on Facebook of what they described as late-night strategy sessions with “Unit 2,” a label widely read in political circles as a reference to Vice President Jeremiah Kpan Koung.

By Rodney D. Sieh

The posts come at a delicate moment for the Boakai administration, which is still facing questions over its request that the European Union withdraw its envoy to Liberia, partly over remarks she allegedly made about the Vice President’s reach into sectors outside his constitutional remit. For many observers, the timing has sharpened a question already circulating in Monrovia: who is really running the country?



The Posts

Youth and Sports Minister Cornelia Wonkerleh Kruah captioned her photos: “To be a politician is not the thing… It’s the late-night meetings… Check-In with Unit 2…” She tagged the post #StrategicPartnership, #UnityParty and #PreparingForTheSecondLeg.

Mohammed “Mo” Ali, Managing Director of the Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation and a former Unity Party Secretary General, posted photos from the same room, writing: “These late-night strategic sessions keep things moving and on course.”

M. Boakai Jaleiba, Vice President for Administration at the National Oil Company of Liberia (NOCAL), followed with: “After a late-night caucus with Unit-2!”

None of the three posts mentions President Joseph Nyuma Boakai.

The EU Backdrop

Earlier this year, the Government of Liberia formally asked the European Union to recall and replace its Head of Delegation, Ambassador Nona Deprez, accusing her of making statements that undermined the country’s leadership, institutions and investment climate.

In a letter signed by Acting Foreign Minister Ethel Davis, the government alleged that the envoy made a series of derogatory and misleading comments during official engagements with Liberian authorities, investors and development stakeholders.

Some of the remarks were reportedly made at the Liberia-European Union Business Forum in Brussels on February 24-25, where the envoy allegedly questioned governance practices within the Liberian government and raised concerns about Vice President Koung’s role in the mining and energy sectors.

Critics of the move argued at the time that calling for the ambassador’s recall did not, by itself, clear the Vice President, and risked leaving the allegation unresolved in the public space.

Loyalty Signals

Against that backdrop, political watchers say the posts read less like routine party business and more like a public declaration of where loyalty lies. The hashtag #PreparingForTheSecondLeg is likely to be read as a nod to 2029, raising the question of whose second leg is being prepared.

The officials’ own histories add a layer of intrigue. FrontPageAfrica previously reported that President Boakai and his immediate circle blamed Mo Ali, Amin Modad, Cllr. Jeror Cole Bangalu and Rep. Clarence Massaquoi for the party’s defeat in Lofa. Massaquoi, now Chairman of the Liberia Telecommunications Authority, is Minister Kruah’s spouse. For some insiders, a visible alignment with the Vice President by figures once at odds with the President’s inner circle is hard to dismiss as coincidence.

‘The Prezzo Approved This Meeting’

A government official, speaking on condition of anonymity, pushed back on that reading.

“It is my understanding that the Prezzo had approved this meeting. It was primarily to discuss growing disenchantment among the young people in the party. Don’t mind the way it is being projected by the posts,” the official told FrontPageAfrica.

The source conceded, however, that the party’s troubles run deeper. “That, yes, is our biggest problem right now. People want to hold onto their jobs and not pay attention to the party. And even in their jobs, how many of the young people have they brought on board?”

Bad Optics

Critics are less forgiving, noting that most of those in the room owe their positions to President Boakai.

“These are people the President gave jobs. Is he supposed to tell them what to do? Should he provide them money? The optics are bad,” said the source.

Whatever the intent, the episode lands on a government already defending itself against claims that power has drifted from the Executive Mansion. If the meeting was sanctioned by the President, the officials chose to tell the public it was with “Unit 2,” not him. In Liberian politics, that kind of messaging is rarely accidental.

World.title: Liberia: McGill Signals CDC Comeback, Says UP Would Not Have Won 2023 Elections Had He Remained in Government
World.content:
Monrovia – Former Minister of State for Presidential Affairs Nathaniel McGill has reignited political conversations about the future leadership of the opposition Congress for Democratic Change (CDC), declaring that the ruling Unity Party (UP) would not have won the 2023 presidential elections had he remained in government.

McGill, who currently represents Margibi County in the Liberian Senate, made the assertion while defending his political influence and electoral support, despite being placed under United States sanctions.

The former minister maintained that his political standing remained intact even after the sanctions, pointing to his election to the Senate as evidence that he continues to enjoy considerable grassroots support.



“If I had remained as Minister of State, the Unity Party would not have won. Despite being sanctioned, the Liberian people still voted for me and elected me as senator. I had the backing of the people,” McGill said.

His remarks come at a politically significant moment for the CDC, which is facing growing internal conversations over whether to retain its current chairman, Janga Kowo, or install a new leader as the party positions itself for a return to power.

McGill further suggested that the Boakai-led administration was already losing its political grip, declaring that the CDC has the political strength and personnel to reclaim the presidency.

“We have men, we have soldiers in the CDC. And we are coming back,” he said.

Political Scorecard and Claims of Unfinished Projects

Beyond his political declaration, McGill sought to challenge the Unity Party government’s development record, arguing that several projects being presented as achievements of the current administration were initiated or negotiated under the former CDC-led government.

He specifically referenced the Roberts International Airport (RIA) Road Project, the agreement for the construction of an overpass bridge, and a diagnostic laboratory at the 14 Military Hospital.

“The RIA Road Project belongs to us. We signed the agreement for the overpass bridge. The diagnostic laboratory at the 14 Military Hospital was also supposed to be dedicated. We completed more roads, yet this government has not commissioned a single one,” McGill claimed.

He argued that, had he remained Minister of State, he would have demanded explanations from the Ministers of Finance and Public Works over the failure to commission completed road projects.

While McGill’s comments reflect the CDC’s attempt to reclaim political credit for projects initiated during its administration, the claims also underscore the continuing political contest between the former ruling party and the government over development achievements.

Kowo’s Leadership Under Scrutiny

But beyond the exchange over political performance, McGill’s comments have drawn renewed attention to the unresolved question of who should lead the CDC as it attempts to reorganize following its defeat in the 2023 elections.

Janga Kowo currently serves as chairman of the party, having assumed the position following the resignation of Mulbah Morlu, who stepped down both as chairman and from the party.

A former Comptroller and Accountant General of Liberia, Kowo inherited the CDC during one of the most challenging periods in its political history.

His leadership has been credited by supporters with helping to keep the party together amid internal disagreements, political uncertainty and the transition from governing party to opposition.

Under his chairmanship, the CDC has remained vocal in its criticism of the Unity Party-led government. However, some partisans have questioned whether his leadership style is sufficiently assertive to reposition the party for a political comeback.

While critics favor a change at the top, others believe removing Kowo could deepen existing divisions and undermine the relative stability he has helped maintain.

The disagreement presents a difficult choice for the former ruling party: whether to prioritize continuity and internal cohesion or embrace a more confrontational leadership capable of energizing its base.

McGill, Koijee Emerge in Succession Speculation

Sources within the party indicate that former President George Weah and some members of the CDC hierarchy are considering possible alternatives to Kowo.

Among the names circulating is McGill, whose close political relationship with Weah and experience in the former administration have fueled speculation that he could be a preferred candidate for the chairmanship.

Although no formal decision has been announced, McGill’s recent remarks, particularly his declaration that the CDC has the political personnel to return to power, have added another dimension to speculation about his possible political ambitions within the party.

Another prominent name is former Monrovia City Mayor and CDC Secretary-General Jefferson T. Koijee, who has built a strong political following, particularly among the party’s youthful supporters.

Koijee rose through the ranks of the CDC Youth League and remains one of the party’s most recognizable and outspoken figures.

His popularity among younger partisans could make him an attractive option for those seeking a more energetic and combative leadership style. However, his inclusion in the succession conversation also raises questions about the political and reputational implications of his continued presence on the United States sanctions list.

McGill, too, remains under U.S. sanctions, creating a potentially complicated leadership choice for a party seeking to rebuild its national and international political standing.

The sanctions do not automatically disqualify either man from holding the party’s chairmanship.

Other Names in the Leadership Conversation

Other names being mentioned include Eugene Lenn Nagbe, a former commissioner of the Liberia Maritime Authority and special aide to Weah.

Nagbe’s experience in public service and association with the former president have placed him among the personalities being discussed as the party considers its leadership options.

Former House Speaker Jonathan Fonati Koffa has also been mentioned as a possible contender.

Koffa, who previously belonged to the Liberty Party before switching allegiance to the CDC, currently chairs the committee overseeing the construction of the party’s headquarters.

However, sources close to the former speaker say he has no intention of contesting for the chairmanship.

His name nevertheless reflects the broader search within the party for a leader who can command political respect, strengthen internal structures and help bridge differences among competing factions.

A Defining Moment for the CDC

The CDC’s leadership question goes beyond choosing a new chairman. It touches on the party’s identity, its relationship with former President Weah, the influence of its political heavyweights and the strategy it intends to pursue ahead of the next electoral cycle.

Kowo’s supporters see continuity as essential to preserving party unity, while those advocating a change believe the CDC needs a more assertive political figure to rebuild its mobilization capacity and challenge the ruling government.

McGill’s latest remarks have added to that debate, particularly because they come from a former senior official of the Weah administration who continues to command an electoral constituency despite the controversy surrounding his U.S. sanctions.

Whether his declaration signals a genuine interest in the chairmanship or is simply an assertion of his political relevance remains unclear.

What is increasingly evident, however, is that the CDC faces a delicate leadership decision. A poorly managed transition could expose existing divisions, while a carefully negotiated succession could provide an opportunity to rebuild the party’s structures and strengthen its opposition politics.

For now, Kowo remains chairman, and no formal succession process or final decision has been announced. But with McGill, Koijee and other prominent figures featuring in the conversation, the question of who will lead the CDC into its next political chapter is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore.

World.title: EDITORIAL: BEYOND THE WALK
World.content:
On the last day of Breast Cancer Awareness Month, Liberia’s survivors and advocates did what a health system is supposed to do: they told women that cancer is not a death sentence if it is found early. They did it on a short timeline and on goodwill. It is now the government’s turn to match them with money, practical support and imagination.

ON SATURDAY, WOMEN who had been told they were dying walked to show otherwise. Benejane Shaw, ten rounds of chemotherapy behind her, called herself “a living testimony that early detection saves lives.” Florence Tugbeh, who once had no hair, said she could now “shake my head.” They were not asking for sympathy. They were asking their fellow Liberians to get screened.

THEY DESERVE MORE than applause.



Credit Where It Is Due

THE LIBERIA CANCER Resource Initiative, led by Christine E. Brooks-Jarrett, planned this year’s walk on a short timeline and still drew an encouraging crowd. It runs this campaign every year, and insists that awareness must be a year-round effort. Its stated aim is to “break the stigma surrounding cancer and encourage women to prioritize their health and get screened.” In a country where a cancer diagnosis is still whispered about, that is not a small ambition.

DR. DEDDEH SUPUWOOD, a medical oncologist at the John F. Kennedy Medical Center, carries a different kind of weight. She lost her own mother to breast cancer, and she now spends her days trying to make sure fewer Liberian daughters lose theirs. “When you save one woman’s life,” she said, “you are probably saving a whole family.” She is right, and a country that can count on doctors like her, and survivors who will stand up in public and tell their stories, should not leave them to carry the load alone.

A Walk Cannot Carry This Alone

THE LATEST INTERNATIONAL estimates put Liberia’s toll at 4,217 new cancer cases and 2,745 deaths a year. Breast cancer is the most common: 885 new cases and 421 deaths in 2024, roughly 48 deaths for every 100 women diagnosed. Estimated cases are up about 50 percent since 2018. Those figures are modeled, because Liberia has no cancer registry to count its patients properly, and that gap is itself a failure of public health.

THE SYSTEM THOSE women enter is thin. As of the World Health Organization’s last country profile, Liberia had no radiotherapy machines, no radiation oncologists, no mammography units and no national breast or cervical cancer screening program. The Kennedy hospital is described as the only public facility offering specialized cancer treatment. Many patients arrive late, and some stop chemotherapy because they cannot pay. One woman told the Liberian Observer: “My children and I were deciding what to sell next.”

What Government Should Do

THE GOVERNMENT HAS made a start, and it should be credited. Ground was broken in July 2025 for the country’s first radiotherapy center. Officials have bought mammography and imaging equipment, donated chemotherapy drugs to the Kennedy hospital in June, and told the Liberian Observer they are discussing a dedicated cancer medicines budget line. A start is not a system. We urge the President, the Ministry of Health and the Legislature to go further:

Fund cancer by name. Create a dedicated, published line in the national budget for cancer drugs, screening and the completion of the radiotherapy center, and report every quarter on what was spent. Liberia joined other African governments in pledging in Abuja in 2001 to devote 15 percent of national budgets to health; citizens are entitled to know how close the country is, and what share reaches cancer.

Take screening beyond Monrovia. Most of the new equipment sits at one hospital. Mammography, clinical breast exams and cervical screening must reach the counties, with trained staff to read the results and refer the women who need treatment.

Stop making families choose what to sell. Move the key cancer drugs onto the national essential medicines list, as officials say they are considering, and subsidize chemotherapy so that no woman stops treatment because she cannot pay.

Back the advocates in practice.

Groups like the Liberia Cancer Resource Initiative should not have to plan a national campaign on a few weeks’ notice. Offer them grants, free airtime on state media, help with permits and logistics, and a seat at the table when programs are designed.

Count the problem and publish it. Build a cancer registry and release the numbers every year, so that Liberians know how many of their neighbors are being diagnosed and dying, and so that policy follows evidence.

CLLR. TIAWAN SAYE Gongloe told Saturday’s crowd that “corruption starts with C, cancer starts with C.” The budget is where the two meet. Every dollar lost to waste is a drug not bought and a screening machine not installed.

Room for Creativity

THE FIGHT WILL not be won with money alone. The people best placed to reach Liberian women are already in their communities, and government should make room for them to be inventive.

MARKET WOMEN’S ASSOCIATIONS, churches, mosques and radio stations broadcasting in local languages reach women the clinic never sees. Community health workers could be trained to perform clinical breast exams and refer women early. Survivors like Benejane Shaw and Florence Tugbeh could serve as peer guides, walking the newly diagnosed through a system they have just survived. Schools, football clubs and musicians could carry messages about screening and cervical cancer prevention to young Liberians. Mobile teams could visit county towns on market days. None of this has to wait for a new hospital.

THE GOVERNMENT CAN invite these ideas rather than wait for them. A modest innovation fund for community cancer projects, open to local groups as well as hospitals, would let the best ideas grow, and a requirement to measure results would show which ones deserve to be copied.

SATURDAY’S WALK ENDED with games and a plate of dry rice, and a crowd that went home glad. Christine E. Brooks-Jarrett said the fight “requires collective and sustained action.” Government is the largest part of that collective. The advocates have shown the way. It should follow, and it should fund them.
