World.title: Liberia: Konneh Demands Speedy Trial; Citizens Seek Superintendent’s Recusal Over Alleged Mismanagement of Development Funds
World.content:
Gbarpolu Senator Amara Konneh

Monrovia – A US$425,000 procurement controversy involving three earth-moving machines purchased with funds from Gbarpolu County’s Social Development Fund (CSDF) is drawing renewed scrutiny, with Senator Amara Konneh demanding a speedy trial and concerned citizens calling for Superintendent Sam K. Zinnah’s recusal while the case remains before the courts.

By Augustus D.R [email protected]

At the center of the controversy are allegations of financial misconduct, procurement irregularities and the supply of refurbished or substandard equipment instead of the brand-new machines expected under the contract.



The case, which reportedly has remained on the court docket for more than two years without a final determination, has also raised questions about the condition of the equipment and whether Gbarpolu County received value for the public funds invested.

Konneh is urging the Ministry of Justice to take immediate steps to ensure that the proceedings move forward without further unnecessary delays, arguing that the people of Gbarpolu deserve answers and accountability over the use of their development resources.

US$425,000 Procurement Under Investigation

According to the indictment filed by the Liberia Anti-Corruption Commission (LACC), the Gbarpolu County Council approved the allocation of US$425,000 on June 4, 2023, in Bopolu City for the procurement of three heavy-duty earth-moving machines: a bulldozer, an excavator and a motor grader.

The equipment was intended to support road construction, rehabilitation and other critical infrastructure projects across the county.

The contract was subsequently awarded to City Lion Inc., with payments reportedly made through three separate electronic checks dated October 31, 2023, amounting to LRD 80,750,000.

However, the LACC’s indictment alleges that refurbished or substandard equipment was supplied instead of the brand-new machines required under the contract.

The indictment also raises questions about the equipment’s clearance, duty-free privileges and possible violations of procurement and public financial management laws.

Several current and former county officials, alongside the private vendor, have been implicated in the proceedings.

Those named include Gbarpolu County Superintendent Sam K. Zinnah, former Superintendent J. Keyah Saah, former Fiscal Superintendent Anthony Yorkor, former Project Management Committee Chairman Robert Benda and City Lion Inc.

The allegations have not been established in court. An indictment is not a conviction, and all accused persons are presumed innocent until proven guilty by a competent court.

Konneh Demands Speedy Trial

Senator Amara Konneh’s call for a speedy trial has brought renewed attention to the pace of the proceedings and the broader question of accountability in the management of county development funds.

He is urging the Ministry of Justice to work with the relevant prosecutorial authorities to ensure that the case proceeds without further unnecessary delays.

The reported delay of more than two years has heightened concerns about public confidence in the justice system, particularly in a case involving funds intended to address pressing development needs.

A timely judicial determination would establish the facts, determine whether wrongdoing occurred and identify responsibility where the allegations are proven, while protecting the legal rights of all parties.

For residents of Gbarpolu, the concern is not simply whether individuals will be held accountable, but whether the county can recover the value of an investment intended to improve its infrastructure.

Machines Reportedly Non-Operational

Beyond the courtroom proceedings, questions are mounting over the actual condition of the three machines purchased with the county’s development funds.

Reports indicate that the equipment is not operational, with concerns that the machines are leaking oil and cannot perform the essential functions for which they were procured.

If confirmed, the situation would represent a serious setback for Gbarpolu, where poor road connectivity and inadequate infrastructure continue to constrain economic and social development.

Gbarpolu County Superintendent Sam K. Zinnah

The machines were expected to provide the county with the capacity to undertake road construction, maintenance and rehabilitation without depending entirely on external contractors.

Instead, concerns about their operational condition have raised questions about whether the intended benefits of the US$425,000 investment have materialized.

An independent technical assessment is therefore necessary to establish the machines’ actual condition, market value, compliance with contractual specifications and the cost of restoring them to operational status.

The assessment would also help determine whether the county received what it paid for and what corrective measures may be required to protect the public investment.

Citizens Demand Superintendent Zinnah’s Recusal

As the legal proceedings continue, concerned citizens of Gbarpolu County are calling on Superintendent Sam K. Zinnah to recuse himself from his position while the case remains under judicial consideration.

They argue that his temporary recusal would help address potential conflict-of-interest concerns, protect public confidence in the county administration and demonstrate a commitment to transparency.

According to the citizens, the controversy surrounding the alleged mismanagement of development funds should not undermine the credibility of the county’s administration or its ability to function effectively.

The demand for recusal, however, is not a determination of guilt. Rather, citizens describe it as a precautionary measure intended to safeguard institutional credibility while the judicial process takes its course.

Whether the superintendent will consider the demand remains to be established. Boakai Urged to Ensure Government Action

Citizens are also appealing to President Joseph Nyuma Boakai to ensure that the relevant government institutions give the case the urgent attention it deserves.

They want the Ministry of Justice and other responsible authorities to take the necessary steps to move the proceedings toward a timely conclusion.

For residents, the controversy extends beyond the individuals named in the indictment. It raises fundamental questions about the protection of public resources, the credibility of county development institutions and the government’s commitment to fighting corruption.

They maintain that a case involving hundreds of thousands of dollars allocated for local development should not remain unresolved indefinitely.

At the same time, they are calling for accountability through established legal procedures, insisting that the rights of all accused persons must be respected.

Public Funds Must Deliver Public Value

For a county facing significant development challenges, US$425,000 represents a substantial investment that could contribute meaningfully to improved roads, community infrastructure, economic activities and access to essential services.

If the allegations of procurement irregularities and the supply of substandard equipment are established in court, the consequences would extend beyond the individuals implicated.

The greatest cost would ultimately be borne by ordinary citizens whose development priorities were supposed to benefit from the investment.

The controversy also exposes the importance of transparency and oversight in the management of County Social Development Funds.

The people of Gbarpolu deserve credible answers to several fundamental questions: Were the machines delivered according to the original contractual specifications? Why are they reportedly non-operational? Were procurement, payment and clearance procedures properly followed? Who should be held accountable if financial misconduct is established? And what measures will ensure that the county recovers value from its investment?

These questions require answers supported by documentary evidence, independent technical assessments and a transparent judicial process.

Ultimately, Gbarpolu’s development cannot be separated from the responsible management of its public resources. Funds allocated in the name of citizens must deliver the benefits for which they were approved.

The message from the county is becoming increasingly clear: Senator Konneh wants a speedy trial, concerned citizens want Superintendent Zinnah to recuse himself amid potential conflict-of-interest concerns, and residents are urging President Boakai to ensure that the relevant institutions act.

Gbarpolu cannot afford to have US$425,000 tied up in a procurement controversy while the machines purchased with its development funds reportedly remain non-operational. The people deserve answers; the justice system must act, and public accountability must prevail.

World.title: Liberia: LNP Suspends Four Officers Over Alleged Assault, Corruption, Misconduct; One Referred for Criminal Investigation
World.content:
The LNP, under the leadership of Gregory Coleman (above), says the action is the administration’s latest attempt to address alleged misconduct within the force, particularly violations involving the abuse of police authority, dereliction of duty and conduct inconsistent with the standards expected of law enforcement officers.

MONROVIA – The Liberia National Police (LNP) has suspended four officers without pay over various alleged disciplinary violations, including assault, excessive use of force, negligence of duty, corruption and gross insubordination, as the police administration intensifies efforts to enforce professional standards and accountability within its ranks.

By Victoria G. Wesseh

The disciplinary actions, communicated through letters issued by the Police Human Resource Management Division between October 28 and 29, affect Patrolmen Thomas W. Woart, Roderick Samukai, John V. Roques and Melvin K. Jappah.



Among the four officers, Woart faces the most serious administrative action. He has been placed on indefinite suspension without salary and referred for criminal investigation.

However, the police announcement did not disclose the specific allegations against him or identify the authority responsible for conducting the investigation.

Patrolman Samukai was suspended for two months without pay for negligence of duty, while Patrolmen Roques and Jappah were each handed six-month suspensions without salary over alleged corruption and other disciplinary violations.

The actions underscore the LNP administration’s latest attempt to address alleged misconduct within the force, particularly violations involving the abuse of police authority, dereliction of duty and conduct inconsistent with the standards expected of law enforcement officers.

One Officer Referred for Criminal Investigation

Woart’s indefinite suspension stands out among the disciplinary measures, as his case has also been referred for criminal investigation.

Unlike the other three officers, whose penalties carry specified suspension periods, Woart’s suspension has no stated end date.

The referral suggests that the allegations against him may extend beyond internal disciplinary matters and warrant further criminal scrutiny.

However, the LNP has not publicly disclosed the circumstances surrounding the alleged misconduct or indicated whether formal criminal charges have been filed.

A referral for criminal investigation does not constitute a finding of guilt. Any criminal liability must be established through the appropriate legal process.

Six-Month Suspensions for Alleged Corruption

Roques and Jappah received the longest fixed suspension periods, with each ordered to remain off duty without salary for six months.

The police cited alleged corruption and other disciplinary violations as the basis for the sanctions but did not provide details about the nature of the alleged corrupt practices or whether the cases involved separate incidents.

Samukai, meanwhile, received a two-month suspension without pay for negligence of duty.

The LNP’s announcement also identified excessive use of force, assault and gross insubordination among the categories of misconduct addressed through the disciplinary actions. However, it did not clearly establish which specific allegations applied to each of the four officers.

Officers Ordered to Surrender Government Property

As part of the disciplinary measures, all four officers have been instructed to surrender government-issued properties during their respective suspension periods.

The directive is intended to ensure that officers relieved of active police duties do not retain official government assets while serving their suspensions.

The affected officers, however, retain the right to appeal the decisions in accordance with the LNP Administrative Instructions on Discipline and Professional Standards.

The appeals provision offers an administrative avenue through which the officers can challenge the sanctions imposed against them.

LNP Reaffirms Zero Tolerance for Misconduct

In announcing the disciplinary actions, the Liberia National Police reaffirmed its position that indiscipline and misconduct will not be tolerated within the institution.

The police administration emphasized that professionalism, integrity, accountability and respect for lawful authority remain fundamental standards for officers entrusted with protecting lives, enforcing the law and maintaining public order.

The institution also reiterated its commitment to enforcing disciplinary regulations, protecting public confidence and strengthening professionalism within the police service while respecting established procedures and the rights of affected officers.

The latest suspensions come amid continuing public expectations for police officers to exercise their authority responsibly and remain accountable for their conduct.

For an institution at the center of public safety and law enforcement, allegations of assault, excessive force and corruption carry particular weight because they concern the exercise of state authority over citizens.

Although the LNP has yet to disclose further details of the individual cases, the disciplinary measures reinforce the institution’s position that officers are subject to internal accountability mechanisms and that alleged violations can attract serious administrative consequences, including suspension without pay and referral for criminal investigation.

The statement was issued by the Liberia National Police Press and Public Affairs Division.

World.title: Liberia: Presidential Clean Cities Initiatives Must also Focus on Public Awareness and Include the Media to Succeed
World.content:
The once elegant E.J. Roye now in a delapidated condition.

The Executive Mansion in Monrovia recently announced that President Joseph Nyuma Boakai has launched what is called the “Presidential Clean Cities Initiative to support urban sanitation and youth employment.”

By Gabriel I.H. Williams

An Executive Mansion press statement underscores that the initiative, championed by President Boakai, is designed to compliment ongoing efforts of county and municipal authorities to keep cities and communities clean, safe, and environmentally healthy.



The first phase of the Presidential Clean Cities Initiative, which began October 15, 2026, will be implemented across eight counties, covering 14 cities and one township.

Participating locations include Monrovia and Paynesville in Montserrado County; Ganta, Saniquellie, and Tappita in Nimba County; Gbarnga and Totota in Bong County; Foya and Voinjama in Lofa County; Buchanan in Grand Bassa County; Kakata City, Unification City and Schiefflin Township in Margibi County; Tubmanburg in Bomi County; and Zwedru City in Grand Gedeh County.

The Executive Mansion press statement notes that the Presidential Clean Cities Initiatives forms part of the Boakai administration’s broader efforts to improve community conditions, while providing young Liberians with opportunities to participate directly in national development.

Through the Clean Cities Initiatives, the government seeks to encourage greater community ownership of public spaces and stronger collaboration among citizens, youth groups, Community Based Organizations (CBOs), and local authorities in addressing sanitation and environmental challenges.

The first phase will engage 1,250 young people and 20 Community-Based Organizations (CBOs) in sanitation activities, environmental initiatives, and public awareness campaigns, with plans for the program to expand to additional parts of the country.

According to reports, the clean-up campaign in Monrovia will target public spaces, waterways, and beachfronts. These places are infested with heaps of garbage, especially plastic water bags and bottles. Many of the attractive beachfronts are also being used as toilets by vagrants and others. Drug addicts, locally called zogo, are seen at some of the beachfronts getting high or exhibiting behaviors of being high, while syringes used to administer drugs are thrown around in the sand.

Turning Palm Grove Cemetery into a National Shrine

Another landmark in Monrovia being targeted for the Presidential Clean Cities Initiatives is the Palm Grove Cemetery, a site of national significance. There are historical accounts that the Palm Grove Cemetery was once the only burial site in Monrovia. Buried there, in addition to ordinary citizens and residents, are almost all the presidents of Liberia and most senior officials of government, before Liberia’s civil upheavals.

Other distinguished personalities also buried at Palm Grove Cemetery include the highly revered Bishop Samuel David Ferguson, the first black bishop of the Episcopal Church of Liberia. Among his notable contributions to Liberia’s development, in 1889, Bishop Ferguson founded Cuttington Collegiate and Divinity School, now Cuttington University in Bong County, under the Episcopal Church of the United States. Cuttington is the first private, coeducational, four-year degree granting institution in sub-Saharan Africa. Under his leadership, the Episcopal Church of Liberia also established the Bromley Mission, a prominent boarding school for girls in Montserrado County.

Sadly, however, almost all of the graves at Palm Grove have been destroyed. They include the graves of my father, and my younger sister – who died from childbirth complications because she could not reach a hospital after she got into labor due to armed hostilities in Monrovia just before the end of Liberia’s brutal and barbaric civil war. Many drug addicts or vagrants slept in the graves as a home before they were evicted and the cemetery sealed off.

Accordingly, there is a need for the Palm Grove Cemetery to be transformed into a national shrine in honor of our dead.

We applaud President Boakai for launching the Presidential Clean Cities Initiatives, which is intended to give urban areas across Liberia a much need sanitary improvement.

Media Mobilization for Maximum Public Awareness

However, there is a need for a comprehensive public awareness campaign through radio, television, newspapers, and social media, to educate people, shift public perceptions, and inspire specific behavior changes regarding the need to keep our communities and environment clean.

The Presidential Clean City Initiatives will not yield the desired results if the government relies on occasional press statements or press conferences, which is what the prevailing situation appears to be. This is why many community leaders and activists do not seem to be aware. To ensure success, a sustained public awareness campaign must focus on messages not just in English but also the various local ethnic languages, targeting all sectors of society.

After years of living amid heaps of garbage, the Presidential Clean City Initiatives, could be an intervention for which most Liberians would long remember President Boakai favorably. President Boakai could be regarded as the champion of clean environment if the resources for the initiatives are properly expended and the program executed efficiently.

It goes without saying that the Presidential Clean Cities Initiatives will not yield the desired outcome to bring about clean, safe, and environmentally healthy communities without closely working in partnership with the media, which are the custodians of public information dissemination.

Need to Rehabilitate Historic Buildings and Sites

While applauding President Boakai for launching the Presidential Clean Cities Initiatives, there is also a need for the government to seriously consider undertaking a program for the rehabilitation of historic buildings and landmarks in Monrovia, be they public or private owned structures.

Those historic or famous landmarks include the Ducor Palace Hotel, opened in 1960 as the first five-star luxury hotel in West Africa, which was also the first Intercontinental hotel in the West African sub-region. The eight-story luxury hotel, located on Ducor Hill with panoramic view of Monrovia, the St. Paul River and the Atlantic Ocean, featured over 100 rooms, a circular restaurant, a swimming pool, tennis court, and casino, among others.

Ivory Coast’s first President, Felix Houphouet-Boigny is said to have been so impressed with Ducor that he then built Hotel Ivoire in Abidjan on the same model. The Monrovia conference of independent African states in 1961 hosted some 20 African leaders there, among other events of global significance. Prominent international guests hosted at Ducor included Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom and the first female Israeli Prime Minister Golda Meir.

Another famous landmark is the E.J. Roye Building, the now wrecked 10-storey skyscraper in the commercial district of Monrovia. Completed in 1965, the tower was built as the national headquarters of the True Whig Party (TWP), which dominated Liberian politics for nearly a century until the 1980 military coup ended TWP rule. E.J. Roye had a grand auditorium, which hosted numerous international musical legends such as Meriam Makeba, American legendary musical groups such as the Jackson Five and Kool and the Gang. In addition to those global icons, the venue served as a vital stage for Liberia’s own legendary musicians, such as Miatta Fahnbulleh and Nimba Burr.

The areas surrounding the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning and the dilapidated old Education Ministry building on Broad Street in the heart of Monrovia have become a very congested market ground. Many marketers have extended their market stalls from the general market down Waterside and taken over much of Monrovia’s commercial district, reducing the once beautiful downtown into nothing more than a slump.

I understand that many of the abandoned and dilapidated buildings around Monrovia are privately owned. However, there is a serious need for the government to institute appropriate measures, in keeping with laws and city regulations, for the rehabilitation of those historic buildings and sites, to give a much need facelift to Monrovia, which is full of street potholes. The terrible conditions of the streets and roadways have made driving hazardous, leading to serious traffic jams and frequent accidents in Monrovia and its environs. It is about time that the Public Works Ministry very seriously considers addressing this situation by undertaking a major road rehabilitation program.

Considering the need to maintain our historic structures and sites, the Minister of Information, Culture and Tourism (MICAT) is highly commended for rehabilitating the famous MICAT building on Capitol Hill in Monrovia, which was constructed in the 1960s. The MICAT building housed ELBC, now Liberia Broadcasting System (LBS) and other government media outlets.

The construction of the MICAT building was overseen by E. Reginald Townsend, Liberia’s first Secretary of Information, now Minister of Information. He was also the first Minister of State for Presidential Affairs under President William R. Tolbert. Chairman of the TWP when the 1980 coup occurred, he was among the 13 government officials publicly executed following the coup. In the spirit of reconciliation and national unity, I propose to President Boakai for the MICAT building to be named in honor of the late E. Reginald Townsend.

Finally, like in the case of the Presidential Clean Cities Initiatives, President Boakai’s efforts to develop the country and improve the conditions of the Liberian people will amount to little or nothing if those tasked with the responsibilities for execution drop the ball and are not performing satisfactorily. In the end, it is the President who will take the blame and the fall for the failure of his government to deliver on its promises. Let’s not forget that 2029 is around the corner when Liberians will give their verdict on whether the Boakai government performed well to be given a second term.

About the author: Gabriel I.H. Williams is a journalist and authors of the two books, including the international award-winning, “Liberia the Heart of Darkness – Accounts of Liberia’s Civil War and Its Destabilizing Effects in West Africa available on Amazon. He can be reached at [email protected] .

World.title: Liberia: UL President Commends Voices of the Elders For Restoring Stability and Infrastructure Support
World.content:
UL President Dr. Layli Maparyan, middle, receives consignment of Armchairs donated by VOTE. Archbishop Victor Moses Olasemojo, Executive Member of Liberia Council of Churches, and Rev. Augustine S. Arkoi, Co-chair of VOTE during the ceremony.

MONROVIA— In a major demonstration of civic responsibility and national development, the Voices of the Elders (VOTE), Republic of Liberia on Wednesday, October 21, presented an additional batch of 100 green classroom chairs to the Administration of the University of Liberia (UL).

The donation marks another significant milestone under VOTE’s flagship “OPERATION SEAT UL” initiative, which aims to procure and donate 22,000 durable chairs to completely eliminate the state university’s long-standing seating deficit.

The presentation was delivered on behalf of Sister Mary Laurene Browne, Chair of VOTE’s OPERATION SEAT UL by Rev. Augustine S. Arkoi, Co-Chair of VOTE and Founder/CEO of the Better Future Foundation (BFF).



Complementing the ARREST Agenda Through Citizen-Led Action

VOTE’s intervention directly reinforces the ARREST Agenda (Agriculture, Roads, Rule of Law, Education, Sanitation, and Tourism) championed by President Joseph Nyuma Boakai Sr.

By prioritizing the “E” in ARREST through localized solutions and grassroots resource mobilization, VOTE exemplifies how civil society and elder statesmen can actively partner with the Government of Liberia to drive inclusive national development and restore dignity to public higher education.

Speaking at the presentation ceremony on the Capitol Hill Campus, Rev. Arkoi emphasized that true nation-building requires active citizen participation rather than reliance on government intervention alone.

“When VOTE launched OPERATION SEAT UL on November 7, 2025, right here on this historic campus, we did so out of a deep conviction aligned with our vision: To create a country where building a nation is the conscious responsibility of each citizen, and where being Liberian is the first and ultimate identification of every Liberian,” Rev. Arkoi stated.

“Our young people deserve an environment conducive to learning. Today’s delivery of 100 additional chairs represents VOTE’s ongoing progress toward its ultimate target of 22,000 chairs. Sister Mary Laurene Browne would have me assured the University that this local delivery serves as a prelude to incoming shipments of imported chairs. VOTE solicits the continued financial and moral backing of Liberians at home and in the diaspora, reassuring the public that the 22,000-chair target will be fully realized.’’

Highlighting the symbolic weight of the contribution, Rev. Arkoi quoted Sister Mary Laurene Browne, noting that the chairs were deliberately crafted in green because “the color green signifies renewed hope.”

He added that this providential symbol aligns with the unprecedented infrastructure, renovation, and modernization works currently taking place across UL campuses under the government-backed leadership of UL President Dr. Layli Maparyan.

University Administration Praises VOTE’s Peacebuilding and Strategic Partnership

Receiving the donation, UL President Dr. Layli Maparyan expressed profound gratitude to VOTE, describing the organization as one of the state university’s most faithful and strategic partners.

Dr. Maparyan recalled Sister Mary Laurene Browne’s key role as Co-Chair of the search committee that selected her as UL President, and praised VOTE’s proactive diplomatic leadership during the intense student chair protests in July and August 2025.

“Even before the November 7, 2025 launch of Operation Seat UL, during the summer when students were protesting heavily about the chair situation, Voices of the Elders was already organizing talks behind the scenes to help calm tensions, restore reason, and find a way forward,” Dr. Maparyan revealed.

“Through your skillful and loving negotiations, we reduced the fever of the protests and crafted a bona fide solution. It takes the Elders of society to help us find the wisest solutions to our most entrenched problems.”

Dr. Maparyan further commended VOTE for empowering local entrepreneurs and boosting the Liberian economy by contracting domestic woodworkers to produce durable, sustainable wooden armchairs—preserving university tradition while introducing modern quality control.

Empowering Local Business and Expanding Contracts

In direct response to the reliability and superior craftsmanship demonstrated by VOTE’s local contractors, Dr. Maparyan announced on the spot that the University Administration is awarding an additional contract to local vendors to produce matching sets of lecturer desks and chairs donate by VOTE for every classroom across the university.

Representing the contracted vendors, Emmanuel Perry, an Executive of J. P. A. Wood & Furniture Work, thanked VOTE for trusting local Liberian entrepreneurs.

He highlighted that despite negative public perceptions, local artisans are fully capable of high-level service delivery, noting that all chairs delivered under the initiative were 100% pre-financed by the local vendors as a show of commitment to national development. Mr. Perry also expressed deep appreciation to Dr. Maparyan for the new contract award to supply matching lecturer desks.

Spiritual Consecration and Call for Stewardship

The ceremonial handover concluded with a solemn prayer of consecration and exhortation for peace, unity and love among the university administration, government, students, and civic stakeholders, officiated by His Grace, Archbishop Victor Moses Olasemojo, Chairman of the Committee on Prayer & Worship of the Liberia Council of Churches (LCC).

Closing the event, Rev. Arkoi and Dr. Maparyan jointly called on the student body and university leadership to cherish and protect the new chairs to ensure long-term utility for future generations of Liberian scholars.

Under the stewardship of Madam Maureen Johnson Hutcheson as its Chairperson, Voices of the Elders (VOTE)- Republic of Liberia is an organization of elder statesmen, women, and civic leaders dedicated to promoting national unity, sustainable peace, good governance, and citizen-led development across Liberia.

World.title: Youth Minister Challenges Gonet Academy to Anchor National Skills Drive as 909 Graduate
World.content:
Graduating students of Gonet Academy in a group photo

Youth and Sports Minister Cornelia Wonkerleh Kruah challenged Gonet Academy on Saturday to grow from a private training center into part of Liberia’s national development structure, and offered her ministry’s help in tracking graduates from training into work.

By Patience M. Jones [email protected]

Minister Kruah was keynote speaker at the Academy’s 15th graduation ceremony on October 31, 2026, at the Harvest Intercontinental Cathedral, where 909 students received certificates and diplomas.



Gonet Academy opened in February 2021, in the middle of the COVID-19 pandemic, when most institutions were closing their doors. It has since produced more than 5,000 alumni, enough, the minister joked, to form a staff several times larger than her own ministry’s.

The school offers more than 20 courses, from ten-week certificates to six-month comprehensive programs, in procurement, project management, monitoring and evaluation, financial management, logistics and supply chain, data analysis and marketing.

Founder and Chief Empowerment Officer Mohammed Kerkulah said the 909 figure counts individual graduates, and that some completed two or more courses. Counting every course, he said, total certifications exceed 940.

Of the graduates, 208 completed the six-month Comprehensive Professional Programme and 47 the Professional Diploma Programme. The Foundation Certificate Programme produced the largest number. Women made up 530 graduates, or 58.3 percent of the class, and men 379, or 41.7 percent.

Mr. Kerkulah said the Academy’s reach extends beyond Monrovia, noting that some online students from other parts of Liberia were visiting its office for the first time for the ceremony. He also said surpluses from each cohort have been reinvested in the institution rather than used for personal gain. “We are not driven by greed,” he said.

The minister’s address centered on what she called the cost of leaving youth potential to chance. Liberia has about 5.5 million people, roughly three in four of them young, and a median age of about 19. By her arithmetic, one in every 4,400 young Liberians was graduating in the hall that morning, about 0.02 percent of the country’s youth.

“For every year we delay, we pay twice,” she said: once in talent that leaves or sits idle, and again in skills the country imports to do work its own young people could do.

After taking office, she said, she traveled to all 15 counties, meeting young people in town halls and on football fields. She found youth who were “sharp, curious and restless to build something,” but few structures to find them early, develop them and carry them into work or enterprise. Borrowing the physics term entropy, she said that energy is not lost but scattered.

“Some of it leaves the country. Some of it turns into frustration. Most of it is left to luck,” she said, “and no nation should plan its future on luck.”

Minister Kruah opened with humor, joking that Procurement graduates would want to know whether her keynote had gone through competitive bidding. “It did not. It was sole-sourced. I accepted anyway,” she said.

She then pushed back on the idea that the fields the graduates studied are “soft.” “I call them plumbing,” she said. “Nobody admires the pipes, but try running a house without them.” Every mining concession, government road, partner investment and growing business, she argued, depends on such skills. “A country can sign a hundred agreements,” she said. “Without people who can plan, buy, hire, measure and manage, they stay on paper.”

An economist by training, the minister placed Gonet’s work in a global frame, noting that countries have taken different roads to prosperity.

Qatar, she said, saved its gas surplus in one of the world’s largest sovereign wealth funds and invested in universities, research and training, with average income rising from under $3,000 a year in 1970 to above $70,000 today. The United Arab Emirates treated oil “as a bridge, not a destination,” and about three-quarters of its economy is now non-oil. Botswana entered independence in 1966 with only 22 university graduates, then used diamond revenue to develop “not just the roads, but the people,” and is now an upper-middle-income country.

For countries with nothing to dig, she pointed to Singapore, where income per person rose from about $500 in 1965 to above $90,000. The decisive choice, she said, was training people for targeted industries and changing the training whenever those industries changed. She also cited Rwanda, whose Vision 2050 aims for high-income status by mid-century.

“If some countries can be built on gas and others on people, Liberia can be built on both,” she said. Liberia has iron ore, gold, timber, rubber, fertile land and the sea, she noted, but its young people are a second inheritance that “does not need to be mined, but nurtured.”

Minister Kruah urged Gonet’s leadership not to be satisfied with attendance. “A full hall is a good start,” she said, but the question for the next five years is whether the school can become a model “government can look at and say: this works, let us back it and scale it.”

She said she did not know every detail of Gonet’s model, but its ability to draw young Liberians cohort after cohort suggests real value. “People do not keep coming back to a place that gives them nothing,” she said.

She then posed what she called harder questions: Where do Gonet’s graduates go? What do they earn a year later? Which skills will Liberia need in 2030, not just in 2026?

The Ministry of Youth and Sports is asking itself the same questions, she said, through *PATHWAYS: Rooting and Rising Liberia’s Youth*, its ten-year vision. The plan puts evidence, design and foresight at the center of the ministry’s work. She defined foresight as “looking ahead on purpose,” meaning studying emerging trends and jobs so that young people in classrooms today are prepared for the economy of 2035. Evidence, she said, means judging a program by what happens to the young people in it.

On that basis, the ministry’s foresight work wants to partner with institutions like Gonet to follow young people from training into work, “so we can see where they land and what they still need.”

One of PATHWAYS’ pillars, the Pathway Framework, aims to build an ecosystem that moves young Liberians from exclusion to agency, from training into work and from ideas into enterprises. “Gonet is already part of that ecosystem,” she said. The administration, she added, has placed young people at the center of its ARREST Agenda, and PATHWAYS is how her ministry intends to deliver on that commitment over the next decade.

Turning to the graduates, the minister invoked an idea attributed to Nobel laureate Ilya Prigogine: that small “islands of coherence” can shift an entire system to a higher order. Such an island, she said, is a place where people show up, keep their word, do the job properly and help others do the same.

She illustrated the point with Desh Garments, a Bangladeshi company that in 1979 sent 130 young workers to South Korea to learn garment making to world standards. Within a few years, 115 of them had left to start their own garment businesses and trained others who did the same. Bangladesh is today one of the world’s largest clothing exporters. “It began with 130 people in a training programme,” she said. “You are more than 900. Think about that.”

She urged the graduates to keep learning, produce accurate reports, run clean procurement, start the businesses they have been talking about and hire young people who remind them of themselves. She also encouraged them to return to Gonet with ideas to improve it, since people who pass through a model “usually see its flaws first.”

Mr. Kerkulah, who recalled earning about US$100 a month as an intern roughly six years ago, urged graduates to “never, never limit yourself.” He said the Academy belongs to its graduates as well as its founders and that he hopes they will take an interest in its growth.

Minister Kruah closed by congratulating Cohort 15, their families, “some of whom paid the fees and said the prayers,” and the Academy. “This morning, the most valuable reserve this country holds grew by 909,” she said.

World.title: Ndola Council probes squash club land encroachment
World.content:
Ndola City Council says it is investigating a matter in which a Lebanese business investor has allegedly encroached on land belonging to Ndola Squash Club.

The investor, who runs food outlets, has reportedly razed down the club’s perimeter fence after procuring land said to have previously hosted old council toilets.

Ndola Town Clerk Stanley Mbewe confirmed the development in an exclusive interview with Lusaka Times Sports.

Mbewe said Council has received a complaint from Ndola Squash Club and is engaging both the club management and the developer.

“We have received that concern from Ndola Squash Club regarding a land dispute. We wish to appreciate that even the Squash Club doesn’t have a title but that person who is developing land has a title,” Mbewe said.

“So, we are reviewing the title to see if he has really encroached or not. We have taken the matter to the Ministry of Lands. Once an appropriate decision is made we will be able to communicate whether the developer has encroached or not.”

He added: “If he has encroached he will be told to go back to where his title is and we also want to establish how he acquired the title. We are engaging both sides so that we come up with an amicable solution.”

Meanwhile, the Chapter for the Revival of Ndola City has accused the Council of having a malicious and irresponsible scheme against prime sports facilities by encouraging foreign investors to encroach on their land.

Chapter President Chungu Kapema said Ndola lacks adequate functional sports facilities and the Council should not aid illegalities at the expense of sports development.

Kapema cited a similar attempt at Ndola’s Kwacha Centre where the Council allegedly wanted to sell land to a foreign investor to set up a filling station.

He called on residents to object to the illegality and petition the Town Clerk to stop the development.

“All this has been done without presenting any documentation to prove so and without engaging Ndola Squash Club management,” Kapema said.

World.title: Stakeholders extolled for ballot paper inspection
World.content:
Kanchibiya District Electoral Officer, Julius Katuka, has commended political party representatives and other stakeholders for witnessing the inspection of ballot papers ahead of the November 5, 2026 Lubaleshi Ward By-Election.

Mr Katuka said stakeholder participation in electoral activities was important in promoting transparency and building confidence in the electoral process.

Speaking in an interview with the Zambia News and Information Services (ZANIS) after the inspection exercise held today, Mr Katuka encouraged political parties and other stakeholders to actively participate in all stages of the electoral process.

He said stakeholders were free to witness electoral activities conducted by the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) as part of efforts to ensure transparency.

Mr Katuka further assured stakeholders that adequate security measures had been put in place at every stage of the electoral process.

He said the Commission remained committed to conducting free, fair and credible elections.

Meanwhile, United Party for National Development (UPND) District Secretary, Peter Bwalya, expressed satisfaction with the ballot paper inspection exercise.

Mr Bwalya said the participation of political party representatives in the exercise was important in promoting openness and accountability.

And National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) representative, Maybin Chibende, also expressed satisfaction with the exercise, saying stakeholders had been given an opportunity to witness the electoral preparations.

Meanwhile, Citizens First (CF) Party representative, Webster Chanda said the exercise had given stakeholders confidence in the preparations for the forthcoming by-election.

The Lubaleshi Ward By-Election which was necessitated by the death of UPND before the August general election is scheduled to take place on November 5, 2026.

World.title: Nchelenge Council receives funds for revenue enhancement
World.content:
Nchelenge Town Council has received K400,000 from the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) towards the implementation of a revenue enhancement plan aimed at improving revenue collection and reducing revenue leakages.

‎

Council Secretary, Benson Malama says community members have already been sensitised on the initiative, while data collectors have also been trained.

‎

‎ Mr Malama says data collection has since been completed, with the remaining process being consolidation of the data before it is submitted to Chipata City Council for review.

‎

‎He says the initiative is expected to improve revenue collection and accountability once implemented.

‎

‎“Once this plan is implemented, we expect to reduce revenue leakages and maximise revenue collection because payments will be deposited directly into the council’s account,” Mr Malama said.

‎

‎He notes that the system will also help reduce manpower costs while making it convenient for residents to pay for council services.

‎

‎“People will be able to pay for services from the comfort of their homes, and monitoring will be much easier because all businesses will be captured in the database,” Mr Malama said.

‎

‎Nchelenge Town Council is among five local authorities in Luapula Province that have received support from UNICEF for the revenue enhancement initiative.

World.title: Heavy rains blow off teacher’s house in Kawambwa
World.content:
A teacher’s house at Buyaka Primary School in Kawambwa District in Luapula Province has had its roof blown off following heavy rains.

Deputy Head Teacher, Cornelius Chalwe, said the situation is raising concerns over the condition of school infrastructure ahead of the anticipated El Nino weather conditions.

Mr Chalwe has appealed to the Government to consider renovating the school’s dilapidated infrastructure before the onset of heavy rains to prevent further damage.

He has also appealed for support towards the construction of a Secondary School to improve access to education in the area.

Meanwhile, Kawambwa District Commissioner, Godfrey Chilambwe has urged schools to utilise available funds to maintain and improve their infrastructure.

Mr Chilambwe said schools are allocated five percent of their funding for infrastructure development and should use the provision to undertake renovations in line with the established guidelines.

He encouraged school authorities to prioritise the maintenance of buildings to ensure a safe learning environment for learners and teachers.

And the Disaster Risk Management Division (DRMD) representative, Muunga Hansingo has echoed the need for schools to maintain and renovate their infrastructure in preparation for the anticipated El Nino weather conditions.

Ms Muunga has called on school authorities to take preventive measures to minimise damage to infrastructure during the rainy season.

World.title: President Hichilema calls for stronger partnerships in school feeding programme
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has called for stronger partnerships, investments as well as practical solutions to improve school meal programmes worldwide.

Mr Hichilema has also called for increased investment in research and innovation, stronger supply chains, climate-resilient approaches, clean cooking solutions and new financing mechanisms to support sustainable growth.

He has described Zambia’s successful school feeding programme as an investment in education, nutrition, health, agriculture and national development.

The President said this in a speech read on his behalf by Vice President, Mutale Nalumango, in Lusaka today at the official opening of the 2026 Global Child Nutrition Forum.

He noted that Zambia’s home-grown school meals programme now reaches more than 5.6 million learners across all 116 districts.

“The programme links schools with local agricultural production, aiming to provide meals while creating markets for local farmers and supporting community economies,” Mr Hichilema stated.

He further stated that despite the success, challenges persist that include climate shocks affecting food production, supply, gaps in school infrastructure, and limited access to clean cooking technologies.

The President, however, indicated that Zambia is working with nutrition experts, agricultural stakeholders and development partners to diversify school menus and improve their nutritional value across all the 116 districts in the country.

Ukraine First Lady, Olena Zelenska, says Zambia’s success in the School Feeding Programme is well acknowledged and must be a point of reference.

She stressed that the country’s commitment to turning its vision into action continues to impress the global stage.

Ms Zelenska, who attended the Forum virtually, noted that currently despite the war, Ukraine has about 3 million children benefiting from school meals and further called for equal opportunities in nutritional food for all children.

GCNF Executive Director, Arlene Mitchell, noted that despite world challenges, Zambia continues to thrive in School Meals Programme

Ms Mitchell urged participants from around the world to ensure that their actions and decisions on nutrition support the growth and health of children.

Earlier Minister of Education, Harry Kamboni, highlighted that the forum allows strengthening collaborations of sustainable school meals programmes worldwide.

He commended the government for positive reforms and policies such as the free education policy that have allowed millions of children to enroll in school.

The Global Child Nutrition Forum has attracted participants from Kenya, Cameroon, Ukraine, UAE, United Kingdom, the Republic of Yemen and Nigeria.

Others are from Togo, Sri Lanka, the Kingdom of Sweden, Malawi, Zimbabwe, South Africa and Sudan among others.

World.title: Kawambwa residents urged to improve on waste management
World.content:
Kawambwa Town Council Secretary, George Biemba has urged residents to improve waste management practices ahead of the rainy season to prevent environmental pollution and the spread of waterborne diseases.

Mr Biemba noted that proper waste disposal is important in maintaining a clean and healthy environment, especially during the rainy season when poor sanitation could increase the risk of disease outbreaks.

He said this in a press release issued to the media by Kawambwa Town Council Public Relations Officer, Mwango Kapalaula,

Mr Biemba said poorly managed waste could block drainage systems and contaminate water sources, increasing the risk of diseases such as Cholera and Diarrhea.

He has since urged residents to avoid dumping garbage on roadsides, in drainage channels and in open spaces.

And Ms Kapalaula has also encouraged households to ensure that waste is properly collected, stored and disposed of at selected disposal points.

She said poor waste management could create breeding grounds for disease causing organisms and pests, posing a public health risk to communities.

She said keeping Kawambwa clean is a shared responsibility that requires the active participation of every resident.

World.title: A 10 year old boy drowns in Solwezi River
World.content:
A 10 year old boy from the Kyawama area has drowned in Solwezi River after he went swimming with his friends.

Northwestern Province Police Commanding officer, Brighton Siwale confirmed the incident in a statement to the media in Solwezi today identifying the deceased as Ignitious Mwendelema aged 10.

Mr Siwale said the incident occurred on November 1, 2026 at around 17:00 hours at Kafwaya Bridge in Kimasala area of Solwezi District.

He said the incident was reported on November 1, 2026 at 18:30 hours by the boy’s father, Muluku Mwendelema, aged 40 of Kimasala area that his son, Ignitious aged 10 of the same residence drowned in Solwezi River and that his body was still missing despite concerted efforts by the fire brigade team, the Police and members of the general public that conducted the search.

He said the brief facts of the matter are that Ignitious Mwendelema, now believed to be dead, was last seen on November 1, 2026 at around 15:00 hours in the company of his friends going to the river to swim.

Mr Siwale said a few hours later, around 17:00 hours, he was reported missing by his friends who called his parents and the matter was officially reported to the Police.

“Upon receipt of the report, the Police officers called in the fire brigade emergency response team and moved to the scene at Kafwaya bridge,” he said.

He said a search was conducted on the river until it was dark but could not find the body.

“The mission was called off for safety reasons since it was dark. However, this morning, a search continued, and the body was retrieved from the river, and physical inspection by officers reviewed no injuries, hence no foul play suspected,” he said.

Mr Siwale said the body has since been deposited into Solwezi General Hospital Mortuary awaiting postmortem examination and burial.

In a related development another 34 year old man of Kasempa District of Northwestern Province has drowned in Lwamadamba stream.

North-Western Province commanding officer, Brighton Siwale confirmed the incident to ZANIS in a statement in Solwezi district today and identified the deceased as Mulyata Lumuna of Lwamadamba area.

Mr Siwale said the incident happened between 28th October, 2026 at 10:00 hours and October 1st 2026 at 08:50 hours in the Lwamandamba area situated four kilometers away from Kasempa Police Station.

He said the matter was reported on 1st October, 2026 at 09:20 hours at Kasempa police station by Timothy Mushili aged 52, a village headman of Lwamandamba that his nephew Mulyanta Lumuna aged 34 drowned in the nearby stream and his body was discovered floating in Lwamandamba stream.

Mr Siwale said the brief facts of the matter are that the deceased was last seen on 28th October, 2026 at 10:00 hours, and his body was discovered floating in a stream running down the village area.

“His disappearance was not reported to the Police by the relatives as he had a habitual tendency of going out to stay with friends for a few days before returning back home,” he said.

Mr Siwale said after disappearing from the village, villagers who were at the stream came across his body floating in the stream and informed others who identified it as that of Mulyanta Lumuna.

He added that it was at that point that the deceased’s uncle took up the responsibility and made the report to the Police.

“Upon receipt of the report, the officers visited the scene where they confirmed the incident, and the body was retrieved from the water with the help of the family and neighbors. Further, the officers conducted a physical inspection, and no visible marks of injuries were found,” Mr Siwale said.

He said police suspect no foul play and that the body was deposited into Mukinge Mission Hospital mortuary awaiting postmortem examination and burial.

World.title: Stakeholders laud ZRA’s Extended Voluntary Disclosure Scheme
World.content:
Kabwe Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KCCI) president, Kapai Banda has commended the Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA) for supporting the growth of the informal sector through provision of an amnesty facility to taxpayers.

Mr Banda said in an interview with the media that the Extended Voluntary Disclosure Scheme, which is being implemented by ZRA across the country, has provided relief to eligible taxpayers in Central Province.

The scheme allows businesses and individuals to disclose previously declared liabilities and settle principal tax obligations with relief from qualifying penalties and interests.

“As KCCI, we are happy with the Extended Voluntary Disclosure Scheme that has been offered to the business community by ZRA. It is a good tax relief to the business community,” he said.

ZANIS reports that Mr Banda said the initiative has motivated eligible taxpayers to regularise their tax affairs on favorable terms to avoid penalties.

He said the organisation will always support initiatives aimed at supporting the growth of the informal sector.

Mr Banda said the business community in Kabwe will continue supporting such government initiatives by fulfilling their tax obligations as a way of contributing to the country’s economic development.

He called for fair, transparent and collaborative tax administration ahead of this Friday’s National Budget presentation by Minister of Finance and National Planning, Situmbeko Musokotwane.

Mr Banda urged eligible taxpayers to take advantage of the amnesty to settle their tax obligations to avoid penalties.

Under the Extended Voluntary Disclosure Scheme, taxpayers who disclose undeclared liabilities and settle their principal tax obligation receive a proportionate waiver of qualifying penalties and interest of up to100 percent.

ZRA is targeting to raise K185 million this year.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - November 3, 2026
World.content:
press review

US to Cut South Africa and Rwanda from AGOA Trade Deal

U.S. President Donald Trump has notified Congress of plans to remove South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), effective 1 January 2027, after a review found both countries failed to meet the programme's eligibility requirements. The US cited trade and investment barriers, national security and foreign policy concerns, with additional concerns over corruption in South Africa and human rights, political pluralism and workers' rights in Rwanda. The decision comes amid strained relations between Washington and both countries, with Rwanda also facing US sanctions over its alleged support for M23 rebels in eastern DR Congo. South Africa's Trade Minister Parks Tau described the move as unfortunate, saying Washington had raised new concerns not part of ongoing trade negotiations. He said the government would continue diversifying export markets to protect jobs.

Uganda Begins Withdrawal of Troops from Somalia After 20 Years



Uganda has begun withdrawing its troops from Somalia after nearly 20 years of military involvement. The first group of soldiers is already returning home. The phased withdrawal, announced by the country's military leadership, is expected to be completed by the end of 2027 and will include troops serving under the African Union mission. Uganda was the first African country to deploy forces to Somalia in 2007 under the African Union Mission in Somalia (AMISOM), helping government forces push al-Shabaab militants out of Mogadishu and other strategic areas. Uganda's army spokesperson Chris Magezi said the withdrawal would allow Somalia to assume full responsibility for its security. The move follows talks between Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud and Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni, during which Somalia reportedly asked for an extension of Uganda's military presence. The withdrawal comes as the AU's current mission faces uncertainty over future funding and ongoing efforts to build up Somalia's security forces.

UNESCO Warns 86% of Journalist Murders Worldwide Remain Unpunished

UNESCO has warned that 86% of crimes committed against journalists worldwide remain unpunished, highlighting persistent threats to press freedom and the safety of media workers. In a report released on the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes Against Journalists, the UN agency said more than 1,600 journalists had been killed globally over the past 20 years, with local journalists accounting for nine out of every ten victims. Africa continues to face serious challenges, with journalists in countries such as Somalia, Uganda and the Sahel region exposed to killings, intimidation and online harassment. Reporters Without Borders recorded two journalist deaths in Africa this year, in Uganda and Somalia, with neither case resulting in arrests or convictions. UNESCO also raised concerns about the growing use of social media campaigns to discredit journalists and warned that reporters are increasingly being targeted in conflict zones, including through drone attacks. The agency called for greater accountability and protection for journalists, stressing that press identification does not guarantee their safety.

Tensions Flare at Inquiry Into Malawi's Deadly Plane Crash

A parliamentary inquiry into the plane crash that killed former Malawian Vice-President Saulos Chilima and eight others descended into heated exchanges after independent campaigner Christy Lwara clashed with lawmakers over his testimony on the military's handling of the search operation. Lwara told the Ad Hoc Parliamentary Committee that he was dissatisfied with the military's response, questioning why soldiers allegedly stopped people from proceeding to Kasangazi, citing fuel shortages. He said his discussions with officers had led him to believe the aircraft had crashed in the area, prompting him to continue searching there. However, lawmakers challenged his account, accusing him of giving contradictory statements about the search operation. The questioning escalated into personal insults between Lwara and MPs George Jivason Kadzipatike and Joshua Malango, forcing committee leaders to repeatedly intervene to restore order. Committee chairperson Macmillan Water Nyamilandu Manda said he was frustrated by the conduct and warned members that the enquiry could not continue in such an atmosphere. The confrontation comes as lawmakers continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding one of Malawi's deadliest aviation tragedies.

Renewed Tigray Conflict Threatens Ethiopia's Economic Recovery

Ethiopia's strong economic growth prospects are facing renewed uncertainty as escalating tensions in the northern Tigray region threaten to undermine the country's recovery from years of conflict. The International Monetary Fund forecasts economic growth of 9.2% for the 2025–26 fiscal year, driven by agriculture, mining and electricity generation. The conflict caused huge damage to infrastructure and great economic losses. Increased military spending may divert resources away from infrastructure, education and social services, discouraging investment and cutting government revenues, according to financial analyst Abdulmenan Mohammed. If the conflict starts up again, there is a danger of increased military spending. More instability could also exacerbate inflation, shortages of foreign currency and pressure on the national currency. Agriculture and tourism are highly susceptible to insecurity, disruption of transport routes, poor rainfall and climate-related crop challenges that threaten livelihoods and production. Analysts warn that a prolonged conflict could reverse economic gains and place additional pressure on already struggling households.

Close 

Five Arrested Over Attack on South African Farmer

South African police have arrested five suspects in connection with a brutal attack on a 50-year-old cattle farmer, Donovan Marx, at his farm in Ventersdorp, North West. Marx was ambushed by masked attackers during a house robbery last Wednesday, shot, stabbed, and had his ears cut off before the suspects fled with three firearms and his vehicle. Police said the attackers first tied up a farm worker before assaulting Marx when he returned home. The worker later managed to free himself and alert authorities. Marx remains in hospital and may require prosthetic ears after surgeons were unable to save his. His family has welcomed the arrests, saying the legal process must now take its course. The five suspects, aged between 26 and 56, are expected to appear in court facing charges including house robbery, attempted murder and illegal possession of firearms and ammunition. Agriculture Minister Willie Aucamp condemned the attack, while Parliament's police committee chair Ian Cameron called for a thorough investigation and prosecution.

World.title: South Africa: Cape Town Taxi Rivals Agree to Seven-Day Truce - South African News Briefs - November 3, 2026
World.content:
press review

Cape Town Taxi Rivals Agree to Seven-Day Truce

Rival Cape Town taxi associations, the Cape Amalgamated Taxi Association (CATA) and the Cape Organisation for the Democratic Taxi Association (CODETA), have agreed to a seven-day truce, reports EWN. This comes after months of deadly violence that has claimed about a dozen lives and disrupted public transport. The agreement is aimed at restoring calm along the Delft-Langa-Epping corridor, where tensions have been fuelled by disputes over unlawful taxi operations. Both associations have also committed to an independently facilitated process to address the underlying causes of the conflict, with a follow-up meeting with government. The South African National Taxi Council (SANTACO) has welcomed the agreement, saying it is important to protect commuters, drivers and taxi operators.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

IEC Warns Voters Against Photographing Marked Ballots

The Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) has reminded voters of the rules at voting stations ahead of the Local Government Elections, reports SABC News. It warned that taking photographs of marked ballot papers is strictly prohibited. Deputy Chief Electoral Officer Masego Shiburi said voters must mark their ballots in private and follow the instructions of election officials. The commission has also warned against campaigning, canvassing, intimidating or attempting to influence voters inside voting stations. It further urged the public not to intimidate electoral staff or take and share unauthorised photographs of officials on social media. Shiburi said that voting booths are positioned to protect ballot secrecy and prevent voters from being pressured into photographing their choices in exchange for favours or other benefits.

SAHRC Urges Urgent Action to Fix Gauteng Water Crisis

The South African Human Rights Commission (SAHRC) has called on Gauteng municipalities and water service providers to urgently rehabilitate failing wastewater treatment plants and improve access to reliable water and sanitation services, reports EWN. The appeal follows the release of the commission’s report on water and sanitation service delivery in the province, which highlights serious challenges affecting water infrastructure and security. The commission found that approximately 1.5 billion litres of water are lost daily in Gauteng due to leaks. While acknowledging the substantial support provided by the Department of Water and Sanitation to the province's water sector, SAHRC commissioner Henk Boshoff warned that greater attention must be given to protecting and rehabilitating water resources. The commission raised concerns about the deteriorating condition of the resources on which Gauteng's long-term water security depends.

World.title: Somalia: Indian Navy Rescues 20 Crew Members From Hijacked Fishing Vessel Off Somalia
World.content:
Mogadishu — The Indian Navy has rescued all 20 crew members of a hijacked Iranian fishing vessel off the coast of Somalia following a 48-hour military operation involving naval forces and the Indian Air Force, India's Defence Ministry said on Tuesday.

The operation, completed on November 2, involved locating and intercepting the vessel, identified as Azini, which had been seized by armed pirates off Somalia's northeastern coast last month.

The ministry said all 20 crew members were freed safely, with no casualties or injuries reported.

The fishing vessel had been hijacked on October 29, raising concerns that it could be used as a so-called mother ship to launch further attacks on commercial vessels travelling through the strategically important shipping routes in the Arabian Sea and the Gulf of Aden.



In response, the Indian Navy deployed a warship supported by maritime surveillance aircraft to locate and intercept the vessel.

According to the Defence Ministry, the naval platforms maintained persistent surveillance, tracked the vessel's movements and used calibrated non-kinetic measures to restrict its movement and prevent it from escaping.

Indian Marine Commandos, known as MARCOS, were subsequently deployed in a precision airdrop operation from an Indian Air Force C-17 military transport aircraft.

The commandos boarded and secured the fishing vessel, overcoming the pirate threat and freeing all the hostages.

India's Defence Minister Rajnath Singh congratulated the navy and other personnel involved in the operation, describing it as a demonstration of the country's ability to respond to maritime security threats far from its shores.

"The swift localisation, interception and safe release of the crew and vessel from significantly-armed pirates, with timely support from the Indian Air Force, speak well of the Indian Navy's high operational readiness and ability to respond decisively to maritime threats across the region," Singh said in a statement posted on X.

He added that the operation demonstrated India's commitment to protecting seafarers, securing maritime trade routes and maintaining stability across the Indian Ocean.

The rescue took place more than 3,000 kilometres from Mumbai, highlighting the operational reach of India's naval forces.

The incident comes amid renewed concerns over piracy off Somalia, where armed groups have stepped up hijackings of fishing vessels and commercial ships after years of relative calm.

Somali piracy reached its peak between 2008 and 2012, when armed groups seized numerous vessels and held crew members for ransom. International naval patrols and improved security measures subsequently helped reduce attacks.

Close 

However, a resurgence in piracy since late 2023 has raised fresh concerns about the security of international shipping routes connecting the Indian Ocean, the Gulf of Aden and the Red Sea.

The Indian Navy said it remained committed to protecting maritime trade and ensuring safe passage for vessels operating across the Indian Ocean region.

World.title: Malawi: 'You're Not Okay Upstairs!' Chilima Crash Inquiry Erupts As Witness and MPs Trade Insults
World.content:
A parliamentary inquiry into the plane crash that killed former Vice-President Saulos Chilima and eight others descended into chaos after independent campaigner Christy Lwara clashed with lawmakers in a tense exchange marked by accusations, insults and repeated interventions from the committee chair.

Earlier, Lwara told the Ad Hoc Parliamentary Committee he was unimpressed by the military's handling of the search operation.

"I felt that the officers were a bit relaxed, considering how the military operates," he said.

Lwara questioned why soldiers allegedly stopped people from proceeding to Kasangazi, claiming they cited fuel shortages as the reason.



"I did not understand why they were stopping people from going to Kasangazi. They said they did not have fuel, but I asked them how they knew they had no fuel. It seemed like a problem," he testified.

He further claimed discussions with officers on the ground led him to believe the aircraft had crashed in Kasangazi, prompting him to continue searching in the area.

But proceedings took a dramatic turn when George Jivason Kadzipatike, Member of Parliament for Dowa Kasangazi, challenged apparent inconsistencies in Lwara's testimony.

Kadzipatike questioned why Lwara had earlier suggested soldiers were turning people back from Kasangazi, but was now saying they were redirecting people from Nthungwa.

Seeking to explain himself, Lwara offered an unusual analogy.

"Let me just give clarity. It's like saying you saw a hyena and later saying it was a dog. They look similar, but they are different," he said.

He urged committee members not to focus on what he described as minor mistakes.

"If I made a mistake in one statement, don't just quote where I got it wrong. Look at the point I am making."

Then came the remark that ignited tempers.

"Today let me educate you members, although some of you may already be educated," Lwara said.

The comment immediately drew a sharp response from Joshua Malango, Member of Parliament for Dedza Kasina.

"No, let me educate you," Malango fired back.

As Lwara insisted on continuing, Malango escalated the confrontation.

"Let me educate you, because it seems you are not okay upstairs," he said.

The exchange prompted Vice-Chairperson James Mpunga to raise a point of order as tensions boiled over.

Malango accused the witness of presenting contradictory evidence before the committee.

"You have come here with inconsistencies. We need you to tell the truth, not lies," he said.

Close 

An irritated Lwara hit back, accusing the legislator of conduct unbecoming of an honourable member.

"This is not your Parliament. Next time don't put this one in a commission of inquiry. He doesn't behave like an honourable member," he said.

Malango refused to back down.

"Don't come here and threaten members of Parliament. You cannot intimidate me."

As the verbal sparring intensified, Committee Chairperson Macmillan Water Nyamilandu Manda repeatedly intervened in an effort to restore calm.

Lwara continued his attack.

"I have educated big people. Who are you?" he challenged.

Malango responded with a mocking swipe at the witness's educational background, prompting immediate rebuke from the chair.

"Gentlemen, we can't do that. We are honourable members," Nyamilandu Manda cautioned.

When the exchanges still failed to subside, the chairperson expressed frustration at the deteriorating decorum.

"If this was a football match, I would have issued red cards," he remarked.

The explosive confrontation highlighted the high emotions surrounding the inquiry as lawmakers continue examining the events leading up to one of Malawi's deadliest aviation tragedies.

World.title: South Africa: What Now? - Experts Weigh in After Trump Boots South Africa From AGOA
World.content:
From next year, South Africa will no longer be eligible for benefits under the AGOA trade pact.

South Africa will, from next year, be removed from the duty-free benefits of the African Growth and Opportunity Act (Agoa), the US government announced. This was after the SA government had "constructively responded" to US concerns.

South Africa will be removed from the duty-free benefits of the African Growth and Opportunity Act (Agoa) from next year, the US government announced on Monday night.

Citrus farmers have called it "a serious blow to the citrus industry".

Cosatu said it was deeply concerned by the impact South Africa's exit from Agoa would have on thousands of agricultural and manufacturing jobs linked to it.

"We have already seen many jobs lost at factories and companies in Cape Town, Atlantis, Malmesbury and Tulbagh, amongst others. We have seen the devastation it threatens to these workers and farmers' abilities to take care of their families," said spokesperson Matthew Parks.

The US trade representative, Jamieson Greer, said that President Donald Trump had decided to remove South Africa "for engaging in practices that are inconsistent with Agoa's eligibility criteria. In South Africa, the Trump administration is deeply concerned by barriers to US trade and investment, corruption, and threats to US national security and foreign policy interests."
