On Tuesday 3 November 2026 Americans vote for all 435 House seats, 35 of 100 Senate seats and 36 governorships. Polymarket bets favour Democrats for the House (94.5%) and Senate (76.5%) at 4:32 a.m. ET; first polls close 6 p.m. ET.

Start my free brief Yes, email me my free daily brief — I can unsubscribe any time. — What is happening Americans vote today for 435 House seats, 35 Senate seats and 36 governors; polls close from 6 p.m. to 1 a.m. ET.

— Why it matters Congress writes the trade, aid and immigration-funding laws that reach Latin America and Africa, but tariffs rest on executive powers.

— The numbers Republicans hold 53 of 100 Senate seats, so Democrats need a net gain of four; a House majority is 218.

— Who is who Donald Trump, president since January 2025, is not on the ballot; the House has 435 voting seats, the Senate 100.

— What to watch Polls close 6 p.m. to 1 a.m. ET; control of the House and Senate may stay unclear until Wednesday 4 November.

— What it means for you Section 301 tariffs of 10% to 12.5% stand whoever wins; AGOA, Africa’s US trade preference, expires Thursday 31 December.

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives Democrats a 94.5% chance of the House and 76.5% of the Senate (3 November, 4:32 a.m. ET).

What Is on the Ballot Today

All 435 House seats are on the ballot, and 218 seats make a majority. The Clerk of the House lists two vacant seats, in Florida’s 20th and Texas’s 23rd districts.

In the Senate, 35 of 100 seats are up, and Republicans hold 53 against 47 for Democrats and their two independent allies. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to reach 51, because the vice president breaks 50-50 ties.

Thirty-six governorships are also on the ballot, and each state runs its own voting and count. Two of the 35 Senate contests are special elections, in Ohio and Florida, for seats vacated in January 2025.

A law needs both chambers and the president’s signature, so a split Congress can block the other side. Overriding a veto takes two-thirds of each chamber, a threshold neither party holds today.

In Georgia a candidate needs a majority to win. If nobody gets one, a runoff would be held on Tuesday 1 December 2026.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Poll Closing Times and When Results Arrive

The first polls close at 6 p.m. ET in parts of Indiana and Kentucky. Georgia, South Carolina, Vermont, Virginia and most of Florida follow at 7 p.m. ET.

Ohio, North Carolina and West Virginia close at 7:30 p.m. ET, and the largest batch of states at 8 p.m. ET. More states close at 9 and 10 p.m. ET.

Western states, including California, Oregon and Washington, close at 11 p.m. ET. Hawaii and most of Alaska close at midnight ET, and the western Aleutian Islands at 1 a.m. on Wednesday 4 November.

Florida, North Carolina and Georgia usually count quickly, while Michigan, Wisconsin and Pennsylvania can take longer. Calls in close races may wait until Wednesday 4 November or later.

In Brasília and São Paulo the first closings come at 8 p.m. Tuesday, and the big wave two hours later. In Mexico City the first closings come at 5 p.m., one hour before ET, and Bogotá matches ET.

In Lagos the first closings fall at midnight, and the 8 p.m. ET wave at 2 a.m. on Wednesday. Johannesburg is at 1 a.m. and 3 a.m., and Nairobi at 2 a.m. and 4 a.m.

Where the Results Stand

As of the morning of Tuesday 3 November 2026, no polls have closed and no results exist. This section will carry the House and Senate tally after polls close tonight.

Only the first two sentences and this section change when results arrive; every other section stays valid. Official results come from state election offices, and certification can take days or weeks.

The Clerk of the House publishes the official list of members, and the Senate does the same for senators. Recounts in close races can delay the final tally beyond Wednesday 4 November.

What Prediction Markets Say

At 4:32 a.m. ET on 3 November, Polymarket, a US prediction market, priced a Democratic House at 94.5%, with US$43.0 million traded. It priced a Democratic Senate at 76.5%, with US$18.4 million traded.

Its balance-of-power market, with US$61.6 million traded, gave Democrats both chambers 75.5% and a Democratic House with a Republican Senate 18.5%. Republicans keeping both chambers stood at 5.5%.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for Latin America

Most US tariffs now rest on executive powers, so a vote for Congress does not change them overnight. Section 301 duties of 10% or 12.5% on 60 economies took effect at 12:01 a.m. ET on 24 July 2026.

The US Trade Representative’s notice sets Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Peru at 12.5%. Mexico is in the lower 10% tier, and the notice lists exclusions for some products.

A Democratic House could hold hearings and use spending bills to question tariffs and deportation funding. It cannot remove either alone, because the Senate and the president must also agree.

A 1% US tax on cash remittances has applied since 1 January 2026 under the 2025 budget law, Public Law 119-21. Transfers from bank accounts and cards are exempt, so the tax falls mainly on cash senders.

For more, see our analyses of Mexico and the US midterms, Brazil and Trump’s tariff pressure and Colombia and deportations. Our Latin America coverage has the latest.

What It Means for Africa

Section 301 duties of 12.5% apply to Algeria, Angola, Egypt, Libya, Morocco, Nigeria and South Africa, the notice says. Kenya, Ghana and Ethiopia are not among the 60 economies covered.

The African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) gives eligible sub-Saharan countries duty-free access to the US market for many goods. It was extended on 3 February 2026, retroactive to 30 September 2025, and now expires on Thursday 31 December 2026.

A stopgap spending law, H.R. 6500, signed on Wednesday 2 September 2026, funds federal agencies through Friday 11 December. Full-year funding for State Department and aid programmes is still undecided.

The Congress elected today takes office on Sunday 3 January 2027 and will shape 2027 aid and trade bills. It can renew AGOA, but only with the Senate and the president, who also decide how long any renewal lasts.

For more, see our Africa pillar on the new scramble and the Africa coverage. The full US midterms hub and the results night guide by time zone carry live updates.

What It Means for You

If you export to the US, check your country’s Section 301 tier, 10% or 12.5%, and the notice’s product exclusions. The duties apply from 24 July 2026 whoever wins today.

If you send money to Latin America or Africa, cash transfers carry a 1% US tax; bank and card transfers do not. Repeal would need both chambers and the president.

If you follow from Africa or Latin America, first signals arrive after 7 p.m. ET and a fuller picture by Wednesday morning. Treat early projections as estimates until states certify their counts.

What to Watch Next

Tuesday 3 November: polls close from 6 p.m. ET, with the last at 1 a.m. ET on Wednesday 4 November.

Wednesday 4 November: South Africa holds local government elections, and Brazil’s central bank announces its rate decision.

Tuesday 1 December: Georgia runoff, if no candidate wins a majority (state of Georgia election calendar).

Friday 11 December: the stopgap law funding agencies expires; Thursday 31 December: AGOA expires.

Sunday 3 January 2027: new members’ terms begin at noon under the 20th Amendment.

Tonight: this page will be rebuilt with results; only the first two sentences and the results section will change.

What Is Not Known

No seat has been decided, and prediction-market prices change by the minute. Which Senate races will decide control is not yet known.

Whether Congress will renew AGOA, extend the stopgap law or change tariffs is not known. Prediction-market prices are not results.

Frequently Asked Questions

When do polls close in the US midterm elections?

Polls close from 6 p.m. ET on Tuesday 3 November 2026, with the last at 1 a.m. ET in Alaska’s Aleutian Islands. Hours vary by state.

Who is expected to win the US midterms?

Polymarket gave Democrats a 94.5% chance of the House and 76.5% of the Senate at 4:32 a.m. ET on 3 November. These are bets, not results.

How could the US midterms affect Latin America?

Congress shapes spending, trade reviews and remittance rules, but Section 301 tariffs and deportation policy rest largely with the president. A Democratic House would add hearings, not repeal.

How could the US midterms affect Africa?

Congress decides whether to renew AGOA, which expires on 31 December 2026, and funds aid programmes. Section 301 tariffs of 12.5% on seven African economies are executive.

World.title: Iran Ceasefire Odds Fall 20 Points to 78%
World.content:
File photo: the White House in Washington, D.C.

IRAN · UNITED STATES · PREDICTION MARKETS

Key Facts — Prediction markets Polymarket, a crypto-based betting exchange, prices a ceasefire through 2 November at 78%, down 20 points in 24 hours (3 November, 4:30 a.m. ET).

— Trigger Senior US officials confirmed limited strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island, near the Strait of Hormuz, on 2 November.

— Next US midterm elections are today; Iran says it can carry out its seven-day plan in two days.

— Volume About US$38 million traded in all and US$5.2 million in 24 hours.

Traders have cut the odds that the US-Iran ceasefire survived 2 November, after US strikes on an Iranian island that Washington calls defensive.

Polymarket traders cut the chance that the US-Iran ceasefire holds through 2 November to 78%, down about 20 points in 24 hours. Our report of 29 October covered a related ceasefire contract.

It matters to US readers because the ceasefire decides the oil price, the safety of US warships in the Strait of Hormuz and the next move of the White House after today’s midterm elections.

In plain English Polymarket is a crypto-based exchange where people bet real money on events, and the price is the crowd’s implied chance. Qeshm Island is an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz, the sea lane that carries about one-fifth of the world’s oil trade. It lies just off Iran’s southern coast. The ceasefire contract pays “Yes” unless the US carries out a qualifying air or missile strike on Iranian territory by the stated date.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket lists the question “US-Iran ceasefire continues through…?” with one contract per date. A contract pays “No” if the United States carries out a qualifying air or missile strike on Iranian territory by that date.

Through 2 November: 78%, down about 20 points in 24 hours; roughly US$1.2 million traded in 24 hours.

78%, down about 20 points in 24 hours; roughly US$1.2 million traded in 24 hours. Through 31 October: 89%, down about 10 points in 24 hours and 4.5 in a week; roughly US$1.3 million traded in 24 hours.

89%, down about 10 points in 24 hours and 4.5 in a week; roughly US$1.3 million traded in 24 hours. Through 3, 5, 6 and 7 November: between 0.6% and 0.8% each.

Contracts for 4 and 8 November have already resolved to “No”, and those for 15, 22 and 30 November and 31 December show as closed at “No”. In total about US$38 million has traded on the question, including US$5.2 million in the past 24 hours, so this is not a thin market.

Polymarket lists the 31 October and 2 November contracts as disputed, which means the proposed outcome is being challenged. Our reading is that the prices for 3 to 7 November mostly reflect how the contracts settle, not a fresh forecast, and that part of the move may be a dispute over what counts as a qualifying strike.

Kalshi, an exchange regulated in the US by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), did not list a comparable contract when we looked.

These prices are bets, not polls and not a forecast by this newsroom. Live prices are on our Prediction Markets page.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Why the Odds Moved

On 2 November, senior US officials confirmed that American forces had carried out limited strikes on Qeshm Island. Iran’s state news agency IRNA reported explosions, and no Iranian retaliation had been reported by early Tuesday.

The island hosts a naval base, an underground missile facility and a desalination plant, according to US officials. They described the strikes as defensive, meant to weaken Iran’s ability to attack ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

The same officials said such limited strikes had been carried out in secret over several weeks. That clashes with President Donald Trump, who told reporters on Monday: “we haven’t been doing any fighting for months.”

Trump also said on social media that falling oil prices showed markets did not expect a renewed war. Oil prices fell on 2 November as hopes of a deal grew.

Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesman, Esmail Baghaei, said Tehran’s seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could now be carried out in two days. Iran’s conditions include an end to the war on all fronts, the release of frozen Iranian assets, the lifting of oil sanctions and an end to the US blockade of Iranian ports.

Vice President JD Vance said: “We’ve certainly made some progress.” Qatar and Pakistan are mediating between the two sides.

Our reading, not a claim from any source: traders appear to have priced in that a strike has already happened, while the political talk about peace has not changed that fact.

What It Means for US Readers

The first link is oil. Our oil markets report of 2 November tracks that move, and a confirmed strike on Iranian soil would test any calm.

The second is politics. Trump said “No” when asked whether he would strike Iran after the 3 November vote, yet his officials still describe ongoing limited strikes.

For investors, the 78% price is partly a bet on how a disputed contract is settled, not a forecast of war. It is a signal worth watching beside the oil price.

What It Means for Latin America and Africa

Our analysis, not a claim from the sources: the main channel is the oil price. About one-fifth of the world’s oil trade passes through the Strait of Hormuz, so a lasting break in the ceasefire would lift fuel costs for importers in Africa and Latin America. Oil exporters such as Brazil and Guyana would gain on price but face the same risk of a sudden swing. See our report on Hormuz deal odds for the earlier talks.

Regional prediction markets are on our Latin America odds page and Africa odds page. Our report of 19 October covers the earlier 17-point drop.

What Is Not Known

It is not known how Polymarket will settle the disputed contracts, or whether a strike that was not announced at the time counts.

It is not known whether the US will strike again after the election. Trump said “No” when asked, yet he has also left the option open.

It is also not known whether Iran will answer the Qeshm strikes. So far, no significant retaliation has been reported.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are prediction markets saying about the US-Iran ceasefire?

Polymarket prices a ceasefire holding through 2 November at 78% as of 3 November, 4:30 a.m. ET, down about 20 points in 24 hours. That contract is listed as disputed.

Why did the odds fall?

Senior US officials confirmed limited strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island, near the Strait of Hormuz, on 2 November. Traders have not said what moved them, so the link is our reading.

What counts as a qualifying strike on Polymarket?

An air or missile strike launched by the US that hits Iranian territory. Ground incursions, naval gunfire and intercepted munitions do not count.

Is the US-Iran ceasefire over?

Officials have not said so. Trump says there has been no fighting for months, while US officials describe limited defensive strikes over several weeks.

Does a market price mean a strike will happen?

No. Prediction market prices are bets by traders, not forecasts by this newsroom or any government, and they can reverse as news arrives.

World.title: Spain Election Odds Put Feijóo at 84%
World.content:
File photo: Óscar Puente, Spain's Transport Minister. Photo: La Moncloa - Gobierno de España, via Wikimedia Commons (attribution licence).

Spain is heading into a snap election with a deadly rail crash still fresh, and bettors already expect a change of government. Real-money traders give the conservative leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo an 84% chance of becoming prime minister, as our Spain Election 2026 coverage tracks.

Today also brings a test for the Socialist government, as the transport minister answers to parliament over the crash.

On Polymarket, a crypto-based prediction market, Feijóo is at 84% to become Spain's next prime minister as of 4:25 a.m. ET on 3 November. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, who leads the Socialist Party (PSOE), is at 12%.

That question has drawn about US$2.6 million in trading. These prices are bets, not polls, and they can move within minutes of the news.

Polls Hold the Conservatives Ahead

Sigma Dos, a Spanish polling institute, put the People's Party (PP) at 31.1% and the PSOE at 24.6% in fieldwork on 29 and 30 October, published 2 November. NC Report, another Spanish pollster, has the PSOE at 25.6%.

Sigma Dos projects 133 to 139 of the 350 seats in Congress for the PP and 97 to 103 for the PSOE, which won 121 in 2023. Vox, a hard-line conservative party in third place, polls at 19.3%, or 63 to 69 seats.

The Rio Times tracker, which averages 176 polls, shows the PP at 31.3%, the PSOE at 26.6% and Vox at 19.4%. The state-run Centro de Investigaciones Sociológicas (CIS) pollster, in an October survey taken before the crash, had the PSOE ahead by about 12 points, 34% to 22.2%.

Why the Rail Crash Is Now a Campaign Issue

Transport Minister Óscar Puente is due before the Permanent Delegation of Congress, a committee that sits between sessions, at 11 a.m. ET today, 3 November (5 p.m. in Spain). He asked to appear himself.

An AVE high-speed train of the state operator Renfe hit a stationary train of the private operator Iryo at Urda, in Toledo province, at 3:53 a.m. ET on 28 October (8:53 a.m. in Spain), and 69 people died. Puente has called the decision of the control centre of Adif, the state rail-network operator that depends on his ministry, to let the AVE resume service “inexplicable”.

Puente offered his resignation after the crash, and Sánchez refused it as “unjust”. The PP called the appearance “insufficient” and asked for Puente to resign and for Sánchez to appear in Congress.

Vox filed a complaint at the Supreme Court, the only court that can investigate ministers, alleging negligent manslaughter and injuries.

Dates Ahead

Spain votes on Sunday, 29 November, for Congress and the Senate (the upper house), after Sánchez called the election when Congress rejected his housing decrees on 2 October. Sánchez and Feijóo have agreed to debate on Mediaset, a Spanish private TV group, on Monday, 16 November.

The PP has proposed further debates on 23 and 26 November, which are not confirmed.

What It Means for US Readers

Voters choose the 350-seat Congress, where 176 seats make a majority, and the Senate. Sigma Dos projects 196 to 208 seats for the PP and Vox together.

A conservative-led government would change who speaks for Spain, a NATO member and the euro area's fourth-largest economy, in talks with Washington. Markets, though, price a campaign that still has four weeks to run.

What Is Not Known

Puente's appearance was still ahead when this article was written, so what he tells the committee is unknown. Whether he stays in office is also unknown.

The cause of the crash is unresolved. AITAT, Spain's independent rail-accident investigator, says its work is preliminary, and a separate judicial case is under way in a local court in Orgaz, Toledo province.

The CIS and Sigma Dos differ by about 12 points on the PSOE-PP gap, and it is not known whether the post-crash shift in the polls will last.

World.title: Brazil Amazon Drought Hits 146,000 Families
World.content:
BRAZIL · CLIMATE

Key Facts Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

What is happening Drought has hit 146,425 families in Brazil’s Amazonas state, and 47 of its 62 municipalities are in a state of emergency.

Why it matters The other 15 municipalities, including the state capital Manaus, are on alert, so every municipality in the state is now in emergency or on alert.

The numbers The state has sent 4,800 food baskets, 3,400 cleaning kits and 3,060 water tanks to 15 municipalities, and firefighters fought 24,505 fire outbreaks since 1 June.

Who is who Defesa Civil is the state civil-defence agency that issues the bulletin; CBMAM is the state military fire brigade, which counts the fires.

What to watch Whether the 47 emergencies grow, how far rivers fall, and whether aid beyond the first phase reaches the remaining municipalities.

What it means for you Visitors to Manaus and river towns should expect smoke in places and follow local civil-defence and US State Department travel advice.

Drought has affected 146,425 families in Amazonas, Brazil’s largest state, the state civil-defence agency says. Forty-seven of its 62 municipalities are in a state of emergency.

Drought has affected 146,425 families in Amazonas, Brazil’s largest state by area. Of its 62 municipalities, 47 are in a state of emergency, the state civil-defence agency Defesa Civil said on Monday, 2 November.

Another 15 municipalities, including the state capital Manaus, are on alert, so all 62 are now in emergency or on alert. Amazonas is more than twice the size of Texas, and in much of it rivers are the main roads.

What the Bulletin Shows

The 47 municipalities in emergency include Parintins, Tefé, Coari, Manacapuru, Lábrea and Humaitá. The 15 on alert include Manaus, Itacoatiara, Tabatinga and São Gabriel da Cachoeira.

The bulletin counts families, not people, so the number of individuals affected is higher. It does not give river-level readings.

Air quality was rated worst in Parintins on Monday morning, at the bulletin’s lowest grade, “péssima”, meaning very poor. Ten more municipalities were rated poor or very poor, including Itacoatiara, Iranduba and Maués.

Manaus was rated moderate, as were many other municipalities. Air quality is reported in the same bulletin as the drought and fire figures.

How the State Is Responding

The state government runs Operation Drought 2026, called Operação Estiagem 2026 in Portuguese. Its first phase has reached 15 municipalities.

So far it has delivered 4,800 food baskets, about 96 tonnes, and 3,400 cleaning kits. It has also supplied 3,060 water tanks of 500 litres, three 5,000-litre reservoirs and 18 water-purifier kits.

On Tuesday, 27 October, the state sent more than 13 tonnes of food to Anamã and Rio Preto da Eva. Those two towns are due to receive 670 food baskets, 400 cleaning kits and 200 water tanks.

The state says aid will continue according to river monitoring and the demand from municipalities. The bulletin gives no cost figure for the programme.

Fires and Smoke Add to the Strain

The state military fire brigade, CBMAM, recorded 3,957 urban and forest fire incidents from 1 June to 1 November. Crews fought 24,505 fire outbreaks, of which 4,759 were in the capital and 19,746 in the interior.

About 1,500 firefighters and forest brigade members are deployed, with 18 aircraft, 16 of them federal and two state-owned. The state has also hired 153 more forest brigade members.

A 120-day ban on the use of fire applies across Amazonas, with legal exceptions. The state has also issued 180-day emergency decrees for fire-hit areas and for the whole state because of the drought.

A Strong El Niño Is the Backdrop

El Niño is a warming of Pacific Ocean waters that often brings drier weather to parts of the Amazon basin. The US weather agency NOAA has an El Niño Advisory in force, issued on Thursday, 8 October.

NOAA measured the central Pacific 2.1 degrees Celsius above normal. It sees a strong to very strong El Niño through March 2027.

What It Means for US Readers

Amazon drought affects US readers through climate, commodities and travel. Brazil is a major supplier of soybeans, coffee and beef, and investors in farm and logistics firms track river and rainfall data.

Travellers to Manaus or river towns should check local civil-defence updates and the US State Department advice for Brazil. Smoke can irritate people with asthma or heart conditions.

Related Rio Times reports cover the soy crop outlook and a scientist’s El Niño warning. More is in El Niño and the grid, Brazil’s economy explained and the Brazil hub.

What Is Not Known

The bulletin gives no river-level readings, so how far the Rio Negro and Rio Solimões have fallen is not confirmed here. It also gives no figure for people affected, costs or crop and livestock losses.

The state government’s own bulletin pages could not be opened, so the figures here are those it published and regional newspapers relayed. Whether El Niño is the main cause of this drought has not been stated by the authorities.

What Comes Next

Defesa Civil is expected to keep publishing updated bulletins, and aid continues under Operation Drought 2026. NOAA’s next monthly El Niño update is due in November.

An emergency declaration opens access to aid and does not by itself measure damage. The count of 47 may rise or fall as rivers and rainfall change.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many families are affected by the drought in Amazonas?

The state civil-defence agency counted 146,425 families as affected in its bulletin of Monday, 2 November. The bulletin counts families, not individual people.

How many municipalities are in a state of emergency?

Forty-seven of the state’s 62 municipalities are in emergency, and 15 more are on alert. Manaus, the state capital, is on alert.

What is the state doing to help?

It runs Operation Drought 2026, which has delivered food baskets, cleaning kits and water tanks to 15 municipalities. More aid will follow according to river monitoring and municipal demand.

Is El Niño causing the drought?

El Niño often brings drier weather to parts of the Amazon, and NOAA says a strong event is under way. The state bulletin does not state a cause.

Sources: Defesa Civil do Amazonas, state drought bulletin of 2 November 2026, published through the Amazonas state government (state website could not be opened; figures checked against three independent regional reports); NOAA Climate Prediction Center, ENSO diagnostic discussion of 8 October 2026; Geological Survey of Brazil (SGB), Amazon basin hydrological alert bulletins (river levels) (all accessed 3 November 2026).

World.title: Brazil Debt Defaults Hit 84 Million People
World.content:
BRAZIL · CONSUMER CREDIT

Key Facts Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

What is happening Brazil had 84.2 million people with overdue debts in September, a record and the first time the count has passed 84 million.

Why it matters The count is up 6% in a year and equals roughly Germany’s population, so credit strain is widespread among Brazilian households.

The numbers Overdue debt totals BRL 597.4 billion (about US$110 billion), and the average debt per person is BRL 7,093.83 (about US$1,305), or about 4.4 minimum wages.

Who is who Serasa is a leading Brazilian credit bureau; Copom is the central bank’s rate committee, which sets the Selic benchmark rate, now 13.75%.

What to watch Copom’s Selic decision on Wednesday, 4 November, Serasa’s debt-settlement fair until 6 December, and the October count next month.

What it means for you Holders of US-listed Brazilian lenders should watch loan losses, and the record is a sign of stretched household budgets, not proof that banks are in trouble.

Serasa counted 84.2 million Brazilians with overdue debts in September, the highest figure on record. The average debt was BRL 7,093.83 (about US$1,305) per person.

Brazil had 84.2 million people with overdue debts in September, a record, according to the credit bureau Serasa. Serasa is a leading Brazilian credit bureau that tracks who has fallen behind on payments.

That is roughly the population of Germany, and about 300,000 more people than in August. For investors in Brazilian lenders and for anyone doing business there, it shows how stretched household budgets have become.

A Record Number of Brazilians Are Behind

Serasa published its Debt and Renegotiation Map on Monday, 2 November, with data for September. It counted 84.2 million people with overdue debts, up from 83.9 million in August.

That is about 6% more than a year earlier and 34.17% more than in 2020. It is the highest level in the series and the first time the count has passed 84 million.

Brazilians call a person in this position negativado, meaning the name sits on a credit blacklist. A listing makes it harder to get a loan, a credit card or an instalment plan in a shop.

Who Owes Money and to Whom

Total overdue debt reached BRL 597.4 billion (about US$110 billion), up 0.90% from August. The average debt per person was BRL 7,093.83 (about US$1,305), which equals about 4.4 minimum wages.

Banks and credit cards hold the largest share of overdue debt, at 27.16%. Finance companies, which offer personal and consumer loans outside the big banks, rank second at 20.66%.

That is the first time finance companies have passed water, electricity and gas bills, which hold 20.32%. Utilities had traditionally ranked second among creditors.

People aged 41 to 60 are the largest group, at 35.7% of those listed. Those aged 26 to 40 follow with 33.2%, then those over 60 with 20.1% and those aged 18 to 25 with 11%.

Women account for 50.5% of the listed and men for 49.5%. The count covers people, not individual debts, and Serasa’s July release counted more than 348 million open debts.

Why Interest Rates Matter Here

Brazil’s central bank has kept borrowing costs high to fight inflation. Its benchmark Selic rate stands at 13.75%, after cuts from 15.00% earlier this year.

The IPCA consumer price index, from the statistics office IBGE, rose 4.58% in the 12 months to September. That was up from 4.22% in August, which adds pressure for borrowers with card and loan balances.

Serasa’s figures do not say why defaults rose, so high rates are context, not a proven cause. Copom, the central bank’s rate committee, announces its next Selic decision on Wednesday, 4 November.

Help for Borrowers Starts This Week

Serasa’s debt-settlement fair, called Feirão Limpa Nome, runs from Tuesday, 3 November, to Sunday, 6 December. It is the bureau’s campaign to help people settle overdue debts and clear their names.

Serasa’s July release counted more than 14 million settlement agreements from May to July, up 41% from a year earlier. Those deals involved more than 7 million consumers.

What It Means for US Readers

Investors in US-listed Brazilian lenders, such as Itaú Unibanco and Nu Holdings, watch consumer delinquency because it drives loan losses. A record count of listed borrowers is a warning light for household credit, not proof that any bank is in trouble.

Brazil is the largest economy in Latin America, so strained households can slow spending, including on US goods. The next clues are the central bank’s rate decision and Serasa’s October count.

Related Rio Times reports include Brazil Household Defaults Hit Record 8.1% and Brazil Weighs Loan Limits as Debt Hits 49.9%. More is in Brazil’s economy explained, the Selic guide for foreign investors and the Brazil hub.

What Is Not Known

Serasa’s figures do not explain why the count rose in September. It is unclear how many are new borrowers falling behind and how many are older debts staying on record.

Serasa’s own September release could not be opened in full, so the figures here are those it published and regional newspapers relayed. State-level and income breakdowns for September were not available.

What Comes Next

Copom decides on the Selic rate on Wednesday, 4 November, and Serasa’s settlement fair runs to Sunday, 6 December. Serasa’s October count will show whether September was a peak.

A higher count does not mean the economy is in recession. It also does not show how many of the debts will ever be repaid.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does 84.2 million people with overdue debts mean?

It is the number of Brazilians with overdue debts on a credit-bureau record in September. It is a record and roughly equals the population of Germany.

What is Serasa?

Serasa is a Brazilian credit bureau that keeps records of who has fallen behind on payments. It publishes a monthly map of overdue debts and settlement deals.

How big is the average overdue debt?

It was BRL 7,093.83 (about US$1,305) per person in September, or about 4.4 minimum wages. Banks and credit cards hold the largest share of overdue debt.

Can Brazilians clear their names this month?

Serasa’s settlement fair, Feirão Limpa Nome, runs from Tuesday, 3 November, to Sunday, 6 December. It is Serasa’s campaign to help people settle overdue debts.

World.title: Nigeria Stocks Slip as Oil and Banks Fall
World.content:
NIGERIA · MARKETS

Key Facts What is happening Nigeria’s stock market opened November lower on Monday 2 November, with the All-Share Index down 0.02% to 254,245.21, while Lagos prepares to host a peace summit on 7 November.

Why it matters Oil and gas shares fell 3.75% and banks 1.79%, yet the index is still up 63.38% this year, so the dip is small against a very large rally.

The numbers Market value fell NGN 35.25 billion (about US$26 million) to NGN 165.08 trillion (about US$123 billion), and decliners outnumbered gainers by roughly two to one.

Who is who The Nigerian Exchange (NGX) runs the stock market in Lagos; Yinka Babalola, president of Rotary International, a global volunteer service network, convenes the peace summit.

What to watch Whether oil, gas and bank shares keep falling this week, and what the Lagos summit concludes on governance, justice and peace.

What it means for you US investors mostly reach Nigerian shares through funds, and the US State Department tells Americans to reconsider travel to Nigeria, a Level 3 advisory.

Nigeria’s main stock index slipped 0.02% on the first trading day of November. Oil and bank shares led the losses, while insurers and industrial firms rose.

Nigeria’s stock market opened November lower on Monday 2 November, with the NGX All-Share Index easing 0.02% to 254,245.21 points. The Nigerian Exchange (NGX) runs the market in Lagos, and the All-Share Index tracks every listed share.

Oil, gas and bank stocks did most of the damage, but the index is still up 63.38% for the year to date. For US readers, it is a small pause after a very large rally.

How Nigeria Stocks Opened November

The index fell 54.28 points from Friday’s close of 254,299.49. Market value dropped by NGN 35.25 billion (about US$26 million) to NGN 165.08 trillion (about US$123 billion).

Conversions use the central bank (CBN) official rate of NGN 1,346.26 per US$1, set on Friday 30 October 2026. The bank had not published a separate rate for Monday.

Investors traded 517.26 million shares, 48.15% fewer than on Friday, worth NGN 47.48 billion (about US$35 million). Decliners outnumbered gainers by roughly two to one, with 41 shares down and 21 up in most tallies.

Which Sectors Fell and Which Rose

The NGX Oil and Gas Index fell 3.75%, the steepest drop among the main sector indices. The commodity index lost 2.76%, the banking index 1.79% and the consumer goods index 1.17%.

The industrial index rose 3.34% and the insurance index 0.93%, which cushioned the fall. Aradel Holdings, an oil and gas company listed on the exchange, dropped 9.99%, close to the 10% daily limit.

Lagos Prepares for a Peace Summit

Lagos will host the All Nigeria Rotary Peace Summit on Saturday 7 November at the Victoria Garden Event Centre in Alausa, Ikeja. Ikeja is the capital of Lagos State, where the state government sits.

The convener is Yinka Babalola, a Nigerian who became president of Rotary International on 1 July 2026. He is the second Nigerian to lead the organisation.

The theme is Good Governance, Justice and Equity: Foundations for Sustainable Peace. Organisers have invited community leaders, peace advocates, policymakers and the private sector.

Nigeria’s next general elections are due in 2027, which gives a summit on governance and peace extra weight. Any declaration issued there would be a statement of intent, not law.

Earlier Rio Times reports include Nigeria Stocks Shed US$1 Billion as Energy Shares Slide and Dangote IPO Allotment Awaits SEC Nod. See also Zenith Bank Profit Hits US$690 Million and the Nigeria hub.

What It Means for US Readers

Few Nigerian companies trade in New York, so most US exposure comes through funds that hold shares listed in Lagos. A one-day drop of 0.02% is noise, but a 3.75% slide in oil and gas shares is worth watching.

The US State Department tells Americans to reconsider travel to Nigeria, a Level 3 advisory. Anyone attending the summit in Lagos should check it first.

What Is Not Known

The reason for the fall in oil, gas and bank shares is not confirmed, and it may simply be profit-taking. Reports differ slightly on the number of decliners, at 41 or 42.

The exchange’s own data page did not show the day’s figures when checked. The index numbers rest on identical figures in several Nigerian market reports.

Expected attendance has not been published. A programme carried by one outlet lists panels on governance, justice and security, so speakers and timings may change.

What Comes Next

Trading resumes on Tuesday 3 November, and the summit follows on Saturday 7 November. One weak day does not mark a trend, and a summit does not by itself change policy.

Frequently Asked Questions

How did Nigeria’s stock market open November?

The NGX All-Share Index slipped 0.02% to 254,245.21 on Monday 2 November. Oil and gas shares fell 3.75% and banks 1.79%.

Is Nigeria’s stock market still rising this year?

Yes, the index is up 63.38% for the year to date. The Monday dip was small against that gain.

When is the All Nigeria Rotary Peace Summit?

It is due on Saturday 7 November at the Victoria Garden Event Centre in Alausa, Ikeja, Lagos. The theme is Good Governance, Justice and Equity.

Is it safe for Americans to travel to Nigeria?

The US State Department rates Nigeria Level 3, Reconsider Travel, and lists several states as Do Not Travel. Check the current advisory before any trip.
