World.title: Apple beats sales and profit expectations but AI costs weigh on holiday sales
World.content:
San Francisco – Apple exceeded analysts’ expectations for its latest results on Monday when the iPhone-maker said it notched a “revenue record” for the July-September quarter, driven by iPhone sales and services revenue, but increased costs related to AI will drag down margins.

“We’re closing the year with our most ambitious lineup yet,” CEO John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook in September, said in a statement before speaking on a call with analysts Monday afternoon.

Ternus hinted at an optimistic outlook for sales of its latest products, including the foldable Duo, during the holiday season.

However, CFO Kevan Parekh warned that the company Apple’s gross marin will slow a bit in the final stretch of the year, compared to its September quarter margin of 47.9 percent.

“We expect gross margin to be between 45 percent and 46 percent. This includes primarily the impact of higher memory costs, as well as some costs related to the ramp of Siri AI,” Parekh said.

In June, the company overhauled Siri, its digital assistant, through a partnership with Google, whose Gemini model was used to beef up the new Siri AI.

Apple tried to assuage investors’ concerns about rising AI costs.

“We feel AI offers a compelling reason for customers to upgrade and switch in order to get the latest capabilities, and we also feel there’s opportunities across third-party apps and partnerships as well as first-party opportunities,” Parekh said.

Apple launched three new phones in September — the 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max and its first folding phone called the Duo — in addition to two new desktop computers.

In October, it also unveiled a new smart display powered by Siri AI called HomeView, as well as a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen for the first time.

In July, the company also launched Apple Upgrade, a leasing program that lets US customers pay for an iPhone or other devices in monthly installments.

-Chips crunch-

Long criticized for falling behind in the AI race, Apple stands to benefit from the heavy spending of its peers on data centers while keeping its own investments lean.

Analysts expected the Cupertino giant to spend $11 billion in the 12 months that ended in September, when its fiscal year ends.

That’s a fraction of the annual expenditures of Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta, which are on track to spend more than $700 billion on capital investment this year — roughly the size of Argentina’s or Belgium’s entire economy — much of it on AI infrastructure, according to analyst estimates.

In July, Meta said it expected to spend $145 billion this year, nearly double what it spent in 2026.

Last week, Amazon said it expects to spend $220 billion this year, and Microsoft said it expected to spend $170 billion by the end of the year.

Alphabet’s latest forecast for spending is between $195 billion to $205 billion in 2026.

The iPhone-maker is in a legal battle with one of its close AI partners, though.

In July, Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly orchestrating a campaign to steal the iPhone maker’s trade secrets as the AI lab tries to develop its own consumer hardware device.

OpenAI’s flagship product, ChatGPT, has been integrated into Apple products since 2024.

World.title: Ex-Air chief AP Singh wrote to Rajnath, urged him to keep Race Course land under IAF control
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Days before retiring as chief of air staff, Air Chief Marshal AP Singh wrote to defence minister

, raising concerns over the sealing of the Indian Air Force's (IAF) sports complex at the Race Course Air Force Station in New Delhi.

In a letter dated October 26, Air Chief Marshal AP Singh urged the defence minister to ensure that the over 40-acre land parcel remained under the Air Force's control, news agency PTI reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

AP Singh also raised the issue during an in-person meeting with Rajnath Singh on October 29, three days before his retirement on October 31. He sought the minister's intervention after authorities under the ministry of housing and urban affairs (MoHUA) sealed the sports complex, triggering concern within defence circles, as reported by PTI.

The sealing of the facility, which includes a golf course, swimming pool and other amenities, also led to the cancellation of a planned farewell for the outgoing Air Chief Marshal.

There has been no official statement from either the IAF or the defence ministry on the matter.

IAF flags operational concerns

In his letter, AP Singh referred to a joint survey of the land parcel conducted in 2014 by the then ministry of urban development, the Defence Estate Department and the Air Force.





He argued that the land should remain with the IAF, citing the sports complex's important role in the overall functioning of the air station.

The Air Force has also conveyed its objections to the defence ministry and sought the cancellation of the sealing process, the people said.

It has highlighted the operational importance of the Race Course Air Force Station, particularly its role in addressing potential aerial security threats in the high-security zone around the Prime Minister's residence.

AP Singh also referred to the station's history and its existing land arrangement in his communication. The complex comprises three distinct segments of land, and he stressed that all its facilities should continue to function as usual.

'Absolute disgrace': Congress slams Centre over reclaiming IAF complex

The Congress on Tuesday criticised the Centre's move to reclaim the land housing the Indian Air Force Sports Complex, accusing the Modi government of showing "utter disrespect" to the IAF community.

Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh shared a media report on X which said that Air Chief Marshal AP Singh had written to defence minister Rajnath Singh.

In his post, Ramesh said, "The IAF Sports Complex has a long history and has, over the decades, served many public purposes, as well as being an integral part of the Indian Air Force social infrastructure."

"The Modi government's actions are an absolute disgrace and show utter disrespect to the entire IAF family," Ramesh added.

Centre's drive to reclaim prime land

The sealing is part of a wider government exercise to reclaim high-value land parcels in the vicinity of Lok Kalyan Marg.

Over the past several weeks, the land and development Office (L&DO), under the Union housing and urban affairs ministry, has reviewed plots being used for defence golf courses and sports facilities.

World.title: 'Huge impact on polls': IB opposes shifting convict in ex-Punjab CM Beant Singh's assassination to state jail
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Intelligence Bureau (IB) on Tuesday opposed the transfer of Jagtar Singh Hawara, convicted in the 1995 assassination of then-Punjab chief minister Beant Singh, from Delhi's Tihar Jail to a prison in Punjab, telling the Supreme Court that the move could have a âhuge impactâ on the upcoming assembly elections in the state.

The agency also classified Hawara as a high-risk prisoner and said he should not be shifted to Punjab. A bench of Justices M M Sundresh and P B Varale described the IB report as âvery damningâ while hearing Hawara's plea seeking a transfer to a prison in his home state.

Senior advocate S Muralidhar, appearing for Hawara, told the court, âIf elections are a concern, this may be taken up after three months.â The Supreme Court posted the matter for hearing in February next year.

Elections to the 117-member Punjab Assembly are due early next year.

Beant Singh, who served as Punjab chief minister from 1992 to 1995, was killed in a suicide bombing outside the state civil secretariat in Chandigarh on August 31, 1995. The blast also killed 16 others. Hawara, a member of the banned Babbar Khalsa International, was convicted in the assassination case and is serving a life sentence for the remainder of his natural life.





Why is Hawara seeking a transfer?

Hawara's plea argues that he is a native of Punjab's Fatehgarh Sahib district and should be allowed to serve his sentence in a prison in the state. It also says there are no cases pending against him in Delhi and that his conduct in prison has been without blemish, apart from a jailbreak in January 2004.

Hawara was among four inmates who escaped from Chandigarh's high-security Burail Jail on January 22, 2004, by digging a nearly 100-foot-long tunnel.

The other escapees were Paramjit Singh Bheora, Jagtar Singh Tara and Devi Singh. Hawara and Bheora were subsequently arrested, while Tara was caught in Thailand. Devi Singh remains absconding.

Opposing the transfer, Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Delhi government, had earlier told the Supreme Court that Hawara's jailbreak history raised the risk of another escape. She also cited a Union home ministry advisory on the transfer of high-risk prisoners and the Punjab government's concerns over the possible impact on law and order.

The Punjab and Haryana High Court commuted the sentence to life imprisonment in October 2010, directing that he should not be released for the rest of his life. World.title: 'Gaddar': BJP accuses Rahul Gandhi of treason, calls him 'Bhasmasur'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party (

) on Tuesday launched a scathing attack on Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha

, accusing him of treason, promoting anarchy and attempting to undermine India's democratic institutions.

BJP national spokesperson

labelled Rahul Gandhi 'gaddar' (traitor) and 'Bhasmasur', alleging that his political approach was aimed at destabilising the country and weakening its constitutional framework.

Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, Bhatia questioned Rahul Gandhi's foreign engagements, raised allegations over the Congress's memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Communist Party of China (CCP) and demanded answers about the alleged funding of protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

"This issue is about the model of anarchy, disorder, and treason that the Leader of the Opposition is presenting to the country... That is why he is being referred to as 'Rahul Gaddar'," Bhatia said.

He also accused Rahul of advocating unconstitutional regime change and attempting to weaken democratic institutions.

'Bhasmasur': BJP accuses Rahul of seeking to strangle democracy

Bhatia described Rahul Gandhi as a destructive force and accused him of promoting anarchy instead of respecting India's democratic framework.





"If India has one greatest strength, it lies in its democratic government, its reverence for the Constitution, and the stability it has maintained for 12 years. On the other hand, there is an opposition that is anarchic in its thinking, anti-Constitution, and openly speaks of overthrowing the government. Rahul Gandhi believes in anarchy and destruction; it is not for nothing that he is called a 'Bhasmasura' (a destructive force).

He has become the kind of leader who seeks to usher in anarchy by killing democracy, strangling it to death," he said.

The BJP spokesperson alleged that the opposition was seeking to overthrow elected governments and undermine constitutional institutions, including Parliament and the Supreme Court.

"The other ideology says that whatever you build, our only task is to destroy it. That is why Rahul Gandhi is not called Bhasmasur without reason.

If anyone is attempting to destroy these institutions, it is Rahul Gandhi," he said.

'People will end your political careers': BJP warns Rahul, Mamata and Tejashwi

Bhatia also targeted Gandhi, former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and former Bihar deputy chief minister Tejashwi Yadav over their alleged support for regime change.

He warned that repeated calls for regime change could instead turn public opinion against the opposition and threaten the political future of its leaders.

"I say this with a lot of responsibility: people wanting a regime change might witness a situation where the people of the country feel that the Opposition is irresponsible and should be changed. The public will find an alternative to the opposition; do not imagine, Rahul Gandhi, Mamata Banerjee, or Tejashwi Yadav, that you will gain anything through anarchy. This public will put an end to your political careers. Indiaâs democracy will remain unscathed," he said.

The remarks came amid a controversy over the use of the phrase 'regime change' by senior advocate Prashant Bhushan, All India Students Association (AISA) president Neha Bora and Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera during public statements and press conferences in Delhi.

The comments were made in the context of protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

BJP questions Rahul's foreign meetings, demands answers on China MoU

Bhatia also questioned Rahul Gandhi's meetings with foreign figures, including US Congresswoman Ilhan Omar and Mushfiqul Fazal, whom he accused of adopting anti-India positions.

"How can the leader of opposition in India be anti-India? How can he betray the nation?... The central question is why Rahul Gandhi is meeting individuals like Ilhan Omar or Mushfiqul Fazal who adopt anti-India stances. Is there any discussion about weakening India and bringing about regime change?" he asked.

He further demanded that Gandhi disclose the contents of the Congress's MoU with the Communist Party of China and explain the alleged funding behind protests.

"Rahul Gandhi signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Communist Party of China (CCP) but has not disclosed what it contains to this day... He must also clarify where the funding for these protests, which are being organized with the aim of creating anarchy, is coming from."

BJP accuses Rahul of inappropriate conduct with woman police officer

The BJP spokesperson also accused Gandhi of inappropriate physical conduct with a woman police officer during an anti-CEC protest on Ashoka Road near Jantar Mantar.

"Rahul Gandhi's inappropriate touching of a woman police officer is disgraceful. No political position gives anyone the right to touch a woman inappropriately. He must answer for his shameful behaviour," Bhatia said.

He argued that Gandhi's position as Leader of the Opposition did not give him the right to behave inappropriately with security personnel.

'They want to overthrow elected governments': BJP targets opposition

In his concluding remarks, Bhatia accused Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders of attempting to weaken India's democratic institutions and destabilise elected governments.

World.title: India, Israel vote against Pakistan-backed UN arms control resolution: What it means
World.content:
In a significant move, India and Israel opposed a UN resolution proposed by Pakistan and Belarus concerning regional arms control.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view How effective do you think regional arms control efforts are in ensuring global security? Very effective Somewhat effective Not effective 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

India and Israel have voted against a Pakistan- and Belarus-sponsored draft resolution at the united nations seeking conventional arms control at regional and subregional levels, with New Delhi arguing that national security concerns cannot be restricted by geographical boundaries.The draft resolution, titled âGeneral and complete disarmament: Conventional arms control at the regional and subregional levelsâ, was adopted by the UN general assemblyâs First Committee on Monday, receiving 180 votes in favour, two against and no abstentions.According to the news agency PTI, India and Israel were the only two countries among the 193 UN member states to oppose the resolution.Explaining India's position, Anmol Sher Bedi, first secretary at India's permanent mission to the UN, maintained that conventional arms control was a global issue and should not be addressed primarily through regional and subregional frameworks.âWe are not fully convinced that it should be pursued primarily in regional and sub-regional contexts,â Bedi said while presenting India's explanation of vote before the UNGA first committee.He added that New Delhi's opposition was in line with its consistent position on the matter.India also raised questions over the resolution's call for the UN disarmament commission to develop principles that could provide a framework for regional agreements on conventional arms control.âWe read this request with a certain degree of curiosity,â Bedi said, pointing out that the commission had already reached three consensus-based outcomes on related issues.These included guidelines and recommendations on regional disarmament adopted in 1993, guidelines on conventional arms control and disarmament finalised in 1999, and recommendations on practical confidence-building measures concerning conventional weapons agreed upon in 2017.âThat makes three consensus outcomes on this very subject in the very body now being asked to start from scratch,â he said.Questioning the need for further discussions, Bedi said it was difficult to understand why an issue that had already undergone extensive deliberations needed to be taken up again, unless the intention was to keep the UN's disarmament machinery occupied.India also criticised the resolution's emphasis on maintaining a balance in defence capabilities within regional and subregional settings.Bedi argued that the approach wrongly presumed that countries' security interests were confined to their immediate geographical neighbourhoods.âThis assumes that the security concerns of States politely stop at their regional borders. They do not,â he said.He further stressed that national security considerations often extend beyond narrowly defined regional boundaries, adding that the idea of maintaining a military balance within a particular region or subregion was unrealistic.The resolution argues that conventional arms control should primarily be pursued at regional and subregional levels, as most threats to international peace and security in the post-Cold War period have emerged among countries within the same geographical regions.It also calls for promoting agreements that strengthen regional peace and security while maintaining armaments and military forces at the lowest possible levels.Separately, India voted against a paragraph referring to conventional arms control proposals concerning South Asia.The paragraph took note of initiatives undertaken in various regions, including consultations among certain latin American countries and proposals for conventional arms control in South Asia, while acknowledging the importance of such measures for regional security.The resolution further states that militarily significant countries and nations possessing greater military capabilities have a special responsibility to advance agreements aimed at strengthening regional peace and security.

World.title: 'Can't occupy a site for all times': SC on Delhi protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
World.content:
A traders' counsel told the court that around 50 lakh people lived in areas surrounding the protest site and claimed that shops remained shut

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday said no protest group can occupy a designated demonstration site indefinitely, observing that the right to protest must be balanced with the rights of other citizens. Hearing pleas filed by traders' associations over the impact of demonstrations in Delhi, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said designated protest venues must be made available to different groups for specific periods."You can't occupy a site for all times. Where farmers, journalists, etc. will go? Everyone has right to protest. Designated time must be given for designated period," CJI Surya Kant said, according to LiveLaw.The bench also said that orders granting permission for protests must clearly specify the reasons for allowing or refusing them. "You can't prevent other people, that I am doing protest now you can't," the CJI observed.The court was hearing pleas raising concerns over alleged police brutality, mass detentions, the closure of Metro stations and internet shutdowns during protests, besides the impact of demonstrations on businesses.A traders' counsel told the court that around 50 lakh people lived in areas surrounding the protest site and claimed that shops remained shut, with virtually nobody visiting Connaught Place. The court issued notices to the Centre and other authorities on a plea by the Kirana Committee Delhi seeking a halt to protests during the festive season.However, the bench said it could not adjudicate the traders' grievances unless all organisations involved in the protests were made parties to the proceedings. It asked the traders' associations to implead the organisers of the anti-CEC protests.The hearing comes weeks after the Centre de-notified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, identifying Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground as alternative venues for demonstrations.

World.title: Azam Khan, facing 95 cases since 2017, moves SC against his arrest by ED
World.content:
NEW DELHI: SP leader and ten time MLA

on Monday moved

challenging the ED decision to arrest him on stepping out of Rampur jail after Allahabad HC granted him bail in the last of the 95 cases, which have been slapped on him after BJP came to power in Uttar Pradesh in 2017.

Advocate Mohd Nizamuddin Pasha told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the arrest by ED in a 2019 case, in which FIR itself was registered 13 years after the allegations about land purchase transactions fo Jauhar University from farmers, was illegal.

Though the bench initially asked Khan why he did not move the Allahabad HC, it agreed to list the matter for hearing. Khan said he was forced to move the SC because of âblatant illegality of his arrest including the manner and timing and the gross abuse of process and mala fide exercise of power whereby the machinery of criminal justice system is used for political ends to keep an opposition leader indefinitely in incarceration particularly on account of the approaching assembly elections in UP.

â

Seeking invocation of SCâs exclusive Article 142 powers for grant of interim bail, Khan said since 2017, he has been made an accused in 95 criminal cases, including the ED case. He has been acquitted in six cases, and three cases were closed after his complicity could not be proved.

âHe has been convicted in six; in four of these his sentence has been suspended and/or his conviction stayed, and in the other two, the sentence of two years has been undergone.





The remaining 80 cases are pending trial. The clear pattern that emerges is that whenever the Petitioner is about to be released, a fresh case is registered or revived, and he is sought to be kept behind bars,â Khan alleged.

The 78-year-old petitioner, who had also been a UP cabinet minister as member of both Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha, complained that he was illegally arrested in a 7-year-old ECIR from the gate of District Jail Rampur on Oct 31 without providing him with the arrest memo or written grounds and reasons for arrest.

NEW DELHI: West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh on Tuesday criticised former chief minister Mamata Banerjee for attending the INDIA bloc rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Taking a dig at Mamata, he said that she was turning to Congress leader Sonia Gandhi for leadership out of "utter helplessness".Ghosh claimed that Banerjee's party has lost political ground in its state and that she was seeking political relevance by aligning with the Congress leadership.âEarlier, she set out to become the top leader herself. Now, she has nothing left in her hands. Today, she isnât even an elected representative. That is why, out of utter helplessness, she goes around accepting Sonia ji as her leader again. Her party is finished today,â news agency ANI reported, quoting Ghosh.He also hit out at Banerjee over her objections to the electoral process, saying political parties must respect the people's mandate. He alleged that she had no complaints about the Election Commission or democracy when her party was winning elections.âAs long as she was winning, democracy was fine, and the Election Commission was fine. The moment she lost, everything went wrong. Keep faith in the people; the people decide who wins and who loses. One must accept the verdict of the public,â he said.The minister further claimed that the removal of fake voters during the electoral roll revision had paved the way for free and fair elections in West Bengal. He alleged that Banerjee had benefited from such voters in previous elections.âLook, when the revision occurred, the fake voter base through which Mamata used to win was eliminated. Once they were separated, a free and fair election took place. A genuine election happened in Bengal after many years, and people are happy about it; change has arrived. No outsider can simply enter and become a citizen of this country or avail benefits here,â he said.Ghosh also said the ruling government and party workers would organise rallies across the state to counter the Opposition's attempts to create unrest and communicate their position to the public.âIt is also our responsibility to make people understand and deliver the right message. The people are nationalist, and the government is nationalist. No one will be permitted to create unrest in the country. We will also reach out to the people and hold rallies everywhere; this is just the beginning,â he said.Meanwhile, Ghosh said the state government was making arrangements to ensure that Deepavali, Kali Puja and Jagaddhatri Puja celebrations passed off peacefully.He said every cabinet minister had been assigned a district to oversee law and order during the festive season. Ghosh has been given responsibility for Purba Medinipur, also known as East Midnapore.âThe government is keeping a close watch across all of West Bengal to ensure that the upcoming Deepavali, Kali Puja, and Jagaddhatri Puja are conducted smoothly and with enthusiasm. Every cabinet minister has been assigned the responsibility of overseeing law and order in one district. I have been given charge of Purba Medinipur (East Midnapore). I am also meeting with them to ensure all arrangements are in place and nothing goes wrong. This is the governmentâs duty, and the public must cooperate,â he said.The minister also criticised the previous Trinamool Congress government over the functioning of development boards set up for marginalised communities, including the Matua community.He alleged that several boards formed during Banerjee's tenure had not received adequate funds or been given meaningful work.âMamata Banerjee had formed several development boards in West Bengal: the Rajbanshi Board, the Matua Board, the Bhumij Adivasi Board, but gave neither funds nor work to anyone. She only played politics,â he said.Ghosh said the Matua community, many of whose members migrated from Bangladesh, continued to face economic hardships and needed focused development measures. He said the board should be made functional and provided with funds.âNow, for that community, especially the Matua community, most of whom came from Bangladesh, have numerous hardships and are poor. Their development must happen; therefore, the board must be actively functional for them, and funds must be provided, which our chief minister (Suvendu Adhikari) has initiated," he said.

World.title: Indian seafarer killed in attack on ship near Oman; 13 others rescued: MEA
World.content:
One ​Indian ‌was killed after ​an ⁠attack on a commercial ‌vessel near ‌Limah ‌in ⁠Oman, ⁠the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said ​on ‌Tuesday (November 3, 2026).

13 other Indian nationals ‌on ​board the MSV ⁠AL JUSUFI have ‌been rescued after the incident ‌on Monday (November 2, 2026), ​the Ministry said in ⁠a statement.

The deceased seafarer was identified as Gandhar Nahim Ajij from Gujarat, according to Union Minister for Ports, Shipping, and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal.

Condemning the incident, the MEA called for an immediate de-escalation of tensions and the conclusion of ongoing negotiations for a diplomatic solution in West Asia.

The Ministry, in its statement, stated that the Indian Embassy in Oman is “closely monitoring the situation and coordinating with the Omani authorities” for the early repatriation of the rescued Indian nationals and the mortal remains of the deceased.

Our statement on attack on a commercial vessel off the coast of Oman ⬇️ 🔗 https://t.co/AhtSyD77kl https://t.co/ExpNZGVy9V — Randhir Jaiswal (@MEAIndia) November 3, 2026

“The targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure in the region must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through the international waterways in the region, in keeping with international law, must be restored at the earliest,” it added in a post on X.

Earlier in the day, Mr. Sonowal said the vessel was struck by an “unidentified aerial object” and also confirmed that the tanker had 14 Indian seafarers on board when it was attacked.

⚠️ IMPORTANT UPDATE ⚠️ On Nov 2, the Indian MSV AL JUSUFI, carrying 14 Indian seafarers, was struck by an unidentified aerial object while navigating near the coast of Oman. While 13 crew members safely evacuated and were rescued by the Omani Coast Guard, I am deeply saddened to report that one of our seafarers, Gandhar Nahim Ajij from Gujarat, tragically succumbed to his injuries. My heartfelt condolences go out to his family and loved ones during this hour of immense grief. The Ministry and Indian Embassy in Oman are in contact with local authorities to ensure immediate assistance for the 13 survivors and facilitate the swift repatriation of both the surviving crew and mortal remains of our deceased seafarer. — Sarbananda Sonowal (@sarbanandsonwal) November 3, 2026

“While 13 crew members safely evacuated and were rescued by the Omani Coast Guard, I am deeply saddened to report that one of our seafarers, Gandhar Nahim Ajij from Gujarat, tragically succumbed to his injuries,” he said in a statement on social media.

Mr. Sonowal added that his Ministry and Indian Embassy in Oman are in contact with local authorities to ensure immediate assistance for the 13 survivors and facilitate the repatriation of both the surviving crew and mortal remains of the deceased seafarer.

India is one of the largest contributors of sailors to merchant shipping worldwide, with more than 3,20,000 active seafarers in 2025, according to the shipping ministry.

With inputs from Reuters, ANI

World.title: Mamata, Rahul fighting for infiltrators to keep them in India: Bengal CM
World.content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) attacked the INDIA bloc for holding a rally in Delhi two days ago over alleged electoral irregularities, claiming that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and his predecessor Mamata Banerjee joined hands to protect infiltrators.

Speaking to reporters at Bagdogra airport in Siliguri, Mr. Adhikari said the Centre and the Election Commission of India (ECI) were making efforts to drive out illegal immigrants from the country.

He also attacked Ms. Banerjee for participating in the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi on November 1, claiming that "nobody had invited her to inaugurate even a single Durga Puja in West Bengal".

"The ECI and the Centre have taken up the task of driving out infiltrators from the country, whereas Mamata Banerjee and Rahul Gandhi are fighting together to keep them in India," Mr. Adhikari said.

The Bengal CM is scheduled to participate in a party programme and a State government event in north Bengal on Tuesday (November 3).

World.title: Theni jail warders thrashed 17 escapees after recapture, alleges mother of prisoners at Madras High Court
World.content:
The mother of two out of the 17 prisoners who escaped from Theni district jail on October 26, 2026 has approached the Madras High Court alleging the prison warders beat all 17 inmates black and blue after their recapture within 42 hours of the escape.

Passing interim orders on her writ petition, a Division Bench of Justices A.D. Jagadish Chandira and B. Karthikeyan on Tuesday (November 3) ordered medical examination of the petitioner’s sons and two other inmates who had been specifically named by her.

On being told that all four of them had now been shifted to Salem Central Prison, the judges ordered constitution of a team of three government doctors to visit the prison along with the chairperson of the district legal services authority for examining them.

The Bench ordered that the medical team should visit the prisoners on Wednesday (November 4), examine the prisoners, provide necessary medical treatment and file a report before the court by November 6 when the writ petition would be taken up for hearing next.

K. Arumugathammal, 50, of Madurai had filed the writ petition claiming her sons K. Meenakshisundaram and K. Tirupathi were arrested by the local police on false charges of robbing ₹500 and possessing 300 grams of ganja on October 9 and lodged in the Theni district prison.

Thereafter, her sons had told her about the presence of worms in the food served to them and the prison warders taking away the articles given to the inmates by their visitors. She said, Meenakshisundaram was assaulted by the warders when he complained about it.

Due to the alleged ill-treatment, her sons and 15 other inmates had escaped from the prison. While not justifying their act of jailbreak, the petitioner, in an affidavit filed through her counsel P. Pugalendhi, said, the alleged ill-treatment and physical assault inside the prison require an impartial inquiry by an independent authority.

Claiming her sons realised the mistake of escaping from the clutches of law and surrendered before the police on October 28, the petitioner said, all the 17 recaptured prisoners were beaten up with lathis and boots by the prisoner warders at Theni district jail on October 29.

Thereafter, the recaptured prisoners were transferred to different prisons across Tamil Nadu. Her sons were sent to the Salem Central Prison along with two others, Solai Mugileswaran and Sabarinath, without providing proper medical treatment for the injuries sustained due to severe thrashing by the prison warders, she claimed.

When her plea was heard on Tuesday, Justice Chandira took note that the Tamil Nadu State Legal Services Authority had on Monday directed the chairpersons of the district legal services authority to visit all the prisons where the 17 recaptured prisoners had been lodged at present and conduct an inquiry with them.

Therefore, the Bench directed the medical team to accompany the chairperson of the Salem district legal services authority to examine the petitioner’s sons and two other recaptured remand prisoners.

World.title: Cyclone Murasu LIVE updates: No loss of life in Andhra Pradesh due to Cyclone Murasu, says NDRF
World.content:
The eye of the severe cyclonic storm Murasu, which has battered several parts of Andhra Pradesh with torrential rains, has crossed the coast at 5.30 a.m. on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), and the rear end of the weather system continues to make landfall, a Met Department official.

Murasu formed over South Coastal Andhra Pradesh moved north to northwestwards with a speed of 8 kmph in the past six hours and lay centred over the same region at 8.30 a.m., the official told PTI.

Watch: Days after Cyclone Arnab, Cyclone ‘Murasu’ forms over Bay of Bengal

According to the Visakhapatnam-based Cyclone Warning Centre (CWC) and Indian Meteorological Department (IMD), the weather system was located 30 km north to northeast of Ongole, 40 km southwest of Bapatla, 90 km north to northeast of Kavali, 100 km south to southwest of Vijayawada and 120 km west to southwest of Machilipatnam.

Based on the CWC’s observations at 8.30 a.m., the severe cyclonic storm was likely to move north to northwestwards and weaken gradually into a cyclonic storm by Tuesday noon, accompanied by wind speeds reaching up to 90 kmph and gusting up to 100 kmph.

Later, it is expected to subside into a deep depression by Tuesday (November 3, 2026) midnight with wind speeds reaching up to 75 kmph.

Several thatched houses collapsed and residents were stranded at Samatha Nagar in Ongole, Prakasam district, following heavy rains and strong winds triggered by Cyclone Murasu. The district administration has initiated rescue operations to evacuate those stranded. The statue of Andhra Kesari Tanguturi Prakasam Panthulu in the Prakasam district Collectorate premises in Ongole collapsed early Tuesday after a large tree fell on it due to heavy rain and strong winds.

World.title: ST seat reservation: Goa to move Supreme Court against High Court order stalling the process
World.content:
Seeking to clear the way for political reservation for Scheduled Tribes (ST) ahead of the 2027 assembly polls, the Goa Government is set to move the Supreme Court this week, challenging a Bombay High Court order that stalled the identification of tribal population figures, officials said on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).

The Panaji Bench of the HC had last week restrained the Census Commissioner from notifying ST population estimates, observing that such figures could not be determined on any basis other than the first official Census conducted after 2026.

Talking to PTI, Goa NRI Commissioner Narendra Sawaikar, who was part of a State delegation that visited New Delhi, said the Government would seek a vacation of the stay and file a Special Leave Petition (SLP) before the Supreme Court by Wednesday (November 4, 2026).

A delegation of Goa leaders, including Assembly Speaker Ganesh Gaonkar, Art and Culture Minister Ramesh Tawadkar, and Sawaikar, rushed to the national capital on Monday (November 2, 2026) to explore legal remedies after the HC's order threatened to stall the process of reserving assembly seats.

A division Bench comprising Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit S. Jamsandekar had ordered the interim stay while hearing a petition challenging the constitutional validity of the Readjustment of Representation of Scheduled Tribes in Assembly Constituencies of the State of Goa Act, 2025.

The legislation, enacted by Parliament in August 2025 and brought into force in August 2026, provides for the determination of the ST population in Goa and the readjustment of assembly constituencies to enable political reservation for the community.

The Court questioned the Census Commissioner's decision to presume that the ST population constituted 9.9% of Goa's total population based on the 2001 Census, despite acknowledging that available data did not permit an accurate assessment of the current population.

The Bench also noted that the Kunbi, Gauda, and Velip communities were included in the ST list in January 2003, after the 2001 Census had recorded only 566 tribal individuals across Goa.

The High Court's interim order has created uncertainty over the proposed reservation of four assembly constituencies for the ST community ahead of the 2027 polls.

Political reservation for the ST community has been a long-pending demand in Goa, with tribal organisations and community leaders seeking adequate representation in the State legislature.
